# All4one ### 404 working tools. One portable binary. No plugins, no packs, no filler. Every tool gets its own page with its own options — search it, open it, set what you need, run it. ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-4.1.0-6d8cff?style=flat-square) ![Tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-404-3fb950?style=flat-square) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%2F11-0078D4?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-f7c948?style=flat-square) ![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial-blue?style=flat-square) **🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/All4ONE/)** · **🖼️ [Screenshots](#-what-it-looks-like)** · **📚 [All 404 tools](TOOL_CATALOG.md)** · **⬇️ [Download](https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE/releases)**
--- ## What this is A rebuilt utility suite for Windows: file and folder work, text and data, encoding and hashing, images, PDFs, media, documents, network diagnostics, system and disk maintenance, developer helpers, security checks, calculators and generators — in a single executable that needs no installer, writes nothing to the registry, and runs off a USB stick. It is a rewrite, not a reskin. The previous version registered 551 tools across 45 plugin packs behind one dense table; a large share of those were thin adapters with near-duplicate behaviour ("Image Cropper — Crop image.", "Sparse File Inspector — report internals"). That architecture is gone: | | Before (3.x) | Now (4.0) | |---|---|---| | Structure | 45 plugin packs, a Packs tab, enable/disable toggles | One flat catalogue — nothing to enable, nothing to install | | Tools | 551 registered, many trivial or duplicated | 404, each with a real implementation and its own options | | UI | Tkinter, one table + details pane for everything | Qt (PySide6), sidebar navigation, one page per tool | | Options | Free-text argument box | Typed controls generated from each tool's own schema | | Verification | Registry smoke test only | Every runnable tool executed against fixtures on every build | Nothing was kept just to keep the count up. Every tool listed in [TOOL_CATALOG.md](TOOL_CATALOG.md) runs, and the sweep that proves it ships with the repository. ## What it looks like | Home | A tool page | |---|---| | ![Home](docs/screenshots/home-dark.png) | ![Tool page](docs/screenshots/tool-page.png) | | Category listing | Light theme | |---|---| | ![Category](docs/screenshots/category.png) | ![Light](docs/screenshots/home-light.png) | ## How it works **Sidebar.** Home, Favourites, Recently used, then every category with a live count. Dependencies and Settings sit at the bottom; the sun/moon button switches theme. **Search.** `Ctrl+K` from anywhere. Results are ranked on name, category, summary and keywords — typing "split" finds PDF splitting, file splitting and text splitting. **A tool page.** The header carries the tool's name, category, readiness and a star for favourites. On the left, the options: text boxes, dropdowns, numbers, colour pickers, toggles, and file/folder pickers that accept drag-and-drop. On the right, the output console: streaming lines as the tool works, a progress bar when the tool reports progress, and buttons to copy, save or open whatever the tool produced. **Running.** `Ctrl+Enter` runs. Long jobs stream and can be stopped. Tools that change or delete data ask first, and show a red badge on their page. **Readiness, not gatekeeping.** A tool that needs FFmpeg, Tesseract or a Python package is still listed; it says what is missing and how to get it. Nothing is hidden and nothing silently fails. ## Quick start ### The portable build Download `All4one-4.1.0-windows.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE/releases), unzip, run `All4one.exe`. That is the whole installation. ### From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE.git cd All4ONE pip install PySide6 # only needed for the desktop UI python main.py # desktop app python main.py list # every tool, by category ``` The engine and every standard-library tool run on bare Python — PySide6 is only for the window. ## Command line The same binary is a proper CLI, and every GUI option has an identical flag: ```powershell all4one list # all 404 tools, grouped all4one list --category PDF # one category all4one search hash # ranked search all4one show pdf-merge # options, defaults, readiness all4one run hash-file --file report.pdf --algorithm sha256 all4one run gst-calc --amount 10000 --rate 18 all4one run pdf-extract-pages --file book.pdf --pages "1-3,7" --output ch1.pdf all4one deps # what optional extras are installed ``` Options come from the tool's own field definitions, so the CLI can never drift from the UI. Boolean options are `--flag` / `--no-flag`. ## Optional dependencies The app and 380 of the tools run on the Python standard library alone. The rest declare what they need and light up when it is present: | Needs | Unlocks | |---|---| | Pillow | 26 image tools | | pypdf | 24 PDF tools | | FFmpeg / ffprobe | 20 media tools | | openpyxl · python-docx | 15 document tools | | Tesseract · Poppler | OCR and PDF-to-image | | 7-Zip · LibreOffice · git | archive, office conversion, git tools | | cryptography | file encryption | | pywin32 | the Windows API tools | Run `all4one deps` — or open **Dependencies** in the app — for the exact install line for each one. ## Architecture ```text main.py entry point: no arguments opens the UI, else the CLI core/ tool.py the contract — a tool is a function + a field schema registry.py discovery, validation, ranking, readiness runner.py one execution path for UI and CLI, streaming + cancel deps.py optional dependency probes and install hints cli.py argparse front-end built from the same schemas settings.py one small JSON file: theme, favourites, recents ui/ theme.py design tokens + the whole stylesheet (dark and light) icons.py line icons as inline SVG — no image files to ship widgets.py cards, chips, option editors, the output console pages.py home, category, search, tool page, settings, dependencies window.py sidebar shell, navigation history, search tools/ 16 modules; a tool is ~15 lines plus its options scripts/ catalogue + landing-page generators, release audit tests/sweep.py runs every runnable tool against fixtures docs/index.html the landing page, generated from the registry ``` A tool looks like this, and that is all it takes to appear in the app with a page: ```python @tool(id="gst-calc", name="GST Calculator", category="Numbers", summary="Add or remove GST at any rate, and split CGST/SGST or IGST correctly.", fields=[F.number("amount", "Amount (₹)", 10000.0, minimum=0.0), F.choice("rate", "GST rate", ["5", "12", "18", "28"], "18")]) def gst_calc(v, ctx): ... ``` The UI renders the fields, the CLI turns them into flags, and the catalogue is generated from the same metadata. There is no registration step and no plugin manifest. ## Building the binary ```powershell pip install -r requirements-build.txt python build.py # audit → tests → PyInstaller onefile → zip ``` Output in `dist/`: `All4one.exe` and `All4one--windows.zip`. PyInstaller cannot cross-compile a Windows binary, so the real `.exe` is produced by GitHub Actions on a `windows-latest` runner — every push to `main` builds one, and a `v*` tag publishes it as a release. The Linux job runs the audit and the full tool sweep on every push. ## Verification ```bash python scripts/audit.py # catalogue integrity, versions, hygiene, imports python tests/sweep.py # executes every runnable tool against real fixtures ``` Both are wired into CI and must pass before a build is published. The audit rejects duplicate ids, duplicate summaries, unknown dependency keys, undocumented tools and version drift; the sweep is what stops a tool from quietly becoming decoration. ## Documentation | Document | For | |---|---| | [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md) | Using the app: search, tool pages, options, output, shortcuts | | [INSTALLATION.md](INSTALLATION.md) | Portable build, from source, optional dependencies, troubleshooting | | [TOOL_CATALOG.md](TOOL_CATALOG.md) | Every tool, its options and what it needs — generated from the registry | | [DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md](DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md) | The tool contract, adding a tool or a category, testing | | [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) | The build pipeline, CI workflows, releasing | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | What changed in 4.0 and why | | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) | Reporting, and the safety design | | [docs/index.html](docs/index.html) | The landing page served at drsamonline.github.io/All4ONE | The catalogue and the landing page are generated from the live registry (`scripts/catalogue.py`, `scripts/landing.py`), and the audit fails if either drifts from the code — so the numbers in these pages are the numbers in the app. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence Released under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0** — free for personal and other noncommercial use; # BlinkTransfer ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Send a file with light. No internet, no Bluetooth, no cables.** Animated QR codes, **rateless-coded** so a missed frame never breaks the transfer — the receiver only needs *enough* frames, not every one. [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-7c3aed)](LICENSE) [![Commercial licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/commercial-licence%20available-22c55e)](COMMERCIAL.md) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/commits) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/stargazers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/total)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases) [![Top language](https://img.shields.io/github/languages/top/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER) [![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-6366f1)](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/play/) **[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/play/)**  ·  **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/)**  ·  **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases/latest/download/BLINKTRANSFER-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases/latest/download/BLINKTRANSFER.apk)
--- BlinkTransfer moves files between two devices using **only a screen and a camera**. One device shows an animated QR code; the other points its camera at it. Nothing leaves the room — there is no server, no network and no pairing. It is the **universal** member of the optical-transfer family: monochrome QR only, standards-based, and deliberately dependency-light, so it works on the cheapest phones and in the worst light. ## Why it is different - **Rateless (fountain) coding.** Frames are LT-encoded symbols, not an ordered list. Miss one, or twenty, and the transfer still finishes — you just need about *k* good frames out of the loop. This is the feature the previous version promised and did not ship. - **Any-scanner compatibility mode.** A small text file can be sent as a single plain QR that *any* third-party scanner can read — no app needed on the other side. - **Truly offline.** Fully installable PWA; after first load it never touches the network. - **Light on dependencies.** Two small, well-known libraries (`qrcode-generator` to draw, `jsQR` to read) and nothing else at runtime. ## How it works ``` files ─▶ gzip ─▶ split into k blocks ─▶ LT fountain symbols ─▶ QR frames (loop) │ files ◀─ gunzip ◀─ reassemble ◀─ LT belief-propagation decode ◀─ jsQR ◀ camera ``` Each QR carries a 22-byte self-describing header plus one fountain symbol, so the receiver can lock on to **any** frame — there is no header QR to catch first. A header CRC-16 drops mis-read frames; the QR's own Reed-Solomon handles bit errors; a CRC-32 on the whole payload confirms the finished file. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER.git cd BLINKTRANSFER npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm test # run the test suite npm run build # production bundle into docs/play/ ``` Open the dev URL on both devices (or install the PWA). On one, **Send** and pick files; on the other, **Receive** and point the camera. ## Performance Throughput is roughly `frame bytes × frame rate`. Defaults: ~1.4 KB per frame at 12 fps ≈ 17 KB/s, and larger files loop. | What | Note | |------|------| | Per frame | ~1.4 KB (balanced), ~0.8 KB (robust), ~1.8 KB (dense) | | Frame rate | 2–24 fps, your choice | | Limits | 20 MB total per transfer | | Overhead | ~5–15% extra frames for the fountain decoder | Bigger files work, but for anything over a few MB a network would be faster — this is for when there is no network, or when you would rather there were not. ## Compatibility mode Tick **Compatibility mode** to send one small text file (≤ 1.2 KB) as a single plain QR. Any phone camera app will read it — useful for links, addresses, Wi-Fi passwords and quick notes, with no second device running BlinkTransfer. ## Browser support Chrome 80+, Edge 80+, Firefox 114+, Safari 16+. Requires `getUserMedia` (camera), `CompressionStream` (gzip) and — for the sender — the Wake Lock API (optional). `jsQR` and `qrcode-generator` are bundled, so nothing is fetched at runtime. ## Project layout ``` src/ index.html styles.css main.js sw.js lib/ fountain.js LT fountain codes (encoder + belief-propagation decoder) frame.js frame header, presets, CRC codec.js multi-file container + gzip qr.js QR encode (qrcode-generator) / decode (jsQR) utils.js CRC-16/32, PRNG, helpers public/ manifest + icons tests/ node --test suite (fountain, frame, codec, optical loopback) tools/ build.mjs, dev.mjs, serve.js docs/ landing page + built demo (GitHub Pages) ``` ## Testing ```bash npm test ``` The suite includes a full **optical loopback**: files → gzip → fountain frames → rendered QR pixels → jsQR → fountain decode → files, with binary data. No browser required. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence BlinkTransfer is **free for personal, academic, hobby and non-profit use** under the [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](LICENSE). **Commercial use needs a paid licence** — see [COMMERCIAL.md](COMMERCIAL.md) for what counts as commercial and how to get one (by email invoice). Third-party components and their licences are listed in [NOTICE](NOTICE). > Note: earlier versions were published under the PolyForm Noncommercial licence. That grant stands > for copies already distributed; this and future versions use the dual model > above. ## Credits Built by **Dr Sohil Momin** ([@drsamonline](https://github.com/drsamonline)). # CLDR — Command Line Dispatch & Route **A single tiny Rust binary that sits in your tray, pops up on a keystroke, and runs whatever you type — a sum, a path, an app, a search.** [![Build & Release](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/actions/workflows/build-release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/actions/workflows/build-release.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/CLDR?include_prereleases&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux-blue?style=flat-square)](#-download) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-orange?logo=rust&logoColor=white&style=flat-square)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [![License: MIT + attribution](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2B%20attribution-yellow?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) ### [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/CLDR/) · [Download the latest release](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) · [User guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) · [Setup guide](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md) · [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
--- --- ![CLDR command window](docs/screenshots/01-main.png)
Type anything. CLDR routes it — math, unit conversion, a path, an app, or a web search.
--- ### `/cmd` — run it and read the answer `/run` spawns detached and shows nothing, which is right for opening an editor. `/cmd` is for the other question: *what does this print?* ```text > /cmd lumen stats $ lumen stats → exit 0 index /home/you/.local/share/lumen/lumen.db photos 131 favourites 3 with GPS 0 folders 4 > /cmd lumen search "harbour at dawn" --json > /cmd git status --short > /cmd uname -a ``` - Arguments are split the way a shell would, so quotes work: `/cmd lumen search "harbour at dawn"`. - stdout and stderr are both captured, capped at `max_results` rows; a single line longer than 500 characters is truncated and says how many characters were dropped (`… (+39412 chars)`). - The exit code is shown on the summary line. - **It gives up after five seconds.** A launcher that freezes is worse than one that says "still running", so a command that outlives the cap is reported and left running in the background — use `/run` for anything long. ## 📌 What is CLDR? CLDR is a **single-binary command launcher** for Windows and Linux. Bind it to a desktop shortcut or global hotkey; it stays resident in the background and **summons its command window** when you press the key. Type anything — CLDR *routes* it to the right action instantly and shows the result inline. ```text > 2*(3+4)/7 → [CALC] 2*(3+4)/7 = 2 > 10 km in mi → [CALC] 10 km in mi = 6.213712 mi > notes.md → [OK] opened /home/you/notes.md > code → [RUN] spawned `code` (detached) > rust lifetimes → [WEB] browser → https://duckduckgo.com/?q=rust+lifetimes ``` ## ✨ Features | | | |---|---| | 🪟 **Tray-resident, one keystroke** | Lives in the background; the shortcut **summons** the existing window instead of opening a duplicate | | 🧠 **Smart routing cascade** | math → unit conversion → existing path → PATH binary → web search | | 🧮 **Zero-dep calculator** | `+ - * / % ^ ( )` with unary minus, right-associative power, div/mod-by-zero guards | | 📐 **Unit conversion** | `10 km in mi`, `2 h in min`, `10 GB in MB` — ten dimensions: length, mass, time, volume, area, speed, data, pressure, energy, temperature | | 🗂️ **Slash commands** | `/run` `/cmd` `/open` `/ls` `/find` `/web` `/calc` `/sys` `/help` `/clear` | | ⏱️ **Command history** | `↑`/`↓` (or `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+N`), persisted between runs | | 📋 **Copy without a clipboard crate** | `Ctrl+Y` copies the last result via OSC 52 — works over SSH | | ⚙️ **Config + aliases** | `~/.config/cldr/config.toml` — search engine, caps, and `alias.g = /web` | | 🩺 **Hardware diagnostics** | `/sys` — cores, OS, hostname, user, no external tools | | 🪶 **Near-idle** | Redraws only on change; idle cost is one `poll()` every 250 ms | | 🔒 **No clipboard, no telemetry, no network daemon** | The only socket is loopback-only, for summon | ## 📥 Download Grab the latest from the [**Releases**](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) page. | Platform | Portable | Installer | |---|---|---| | **Windows 10/11 x64** | `cldr-windows-x86_64.zip` — extract & run `cldr.exe` | `cldr--setup.exe` | | **Linux x86_64** | `cldr-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` — extract & run `./cldr` | `./install.sh` | | **Linux ARM64** (Pi 4/5) | `cldr-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | `./install.sh` | Every release ships a `SHA256SUMS.txt` and SLSA build provenance. ### Portable (no install) ```powershell # Windows Expand-Archive cldr-windows-x86_64.zip -DestinationPath $env:LOCALAPPDATA\cldr & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\cldr\cldr.exe" --summon ``` ```bash # Linux tar -xzf cldr-linux-x86_64.tar.gz ./cldr-linux-x86_64/cldr --summon ``` ### Installer ```powershell # Windows — run the setup, or from a portable folder: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-shortcut.ps1 ``` ```bash # Linux — installs to ~/.local/bin + menu entry + tray autostart + Super+Alt+C ./install.sh ``` ## 🏁 Build from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR && cd CLDR cargo build --release # → target/release/cldr(.exe) cargo test # engine + IPC + extras unit tests cargo run -- --self-test # 14 headless checks (exit 0 = pass) ``` No system libraries, no C toolchain beyond what Rust already needs. ## 🗂️ In-window commands | Command | Description | |---|---| | `/run ` | spawn detached via the OS shell | | `/open ` | open a file/folder in the default viewer | | `/ls [path]` | list a directory (row-capped) | | `/find ` | recursive search (depth-capped) | | `/web ` | search in your default browser | | `/calc ` | arithmetic `+ - * / % ^ ( ) unary-` | | `/sys` | hardware diagnostics | | `/help` · `/clear` | cheat sheet · clear pane | | *(no prefix)* | auto: math → units → path → PATH app → web | ### Keyboard | Key | Action | |---|---| | `Enter` | submit | | `↑` `↓` | history (empty input) / scroll results | | `Ctrl+P` `Ctrl+N` | history prev / next | | `PgUp` `PgDn` `Home` `End` | scroll results | | `Ctrl+Y` | copy last result (OSC 52) | | `Ctrl+L` | clear pane | | `Del` | clear input | | `Esc` / `Ctrl+C` | quit | ![Routing examples](docs/screenshots/02-routing.png) ## ⚙️ Configuration `cldr --config` writes a commented starter file to `~/.config/cldr/config.toml` (Linux) or `%APPDATA%\cldr\config.toml` (Windows). Everything is optional. ```toml # search engine — {q} is replaced by the URL-encoded query search_url = "https://duckduckgo.com/?q={q}" # search_url = "https://www.google.com/search?q={q}" max_results = 50 # /ls and /find row cap find_depth = 4 # /find recursion depth # aliases: "name = replacement"; "name arg" appends arg alias.g = /web alias.gh = /web github.com alias.n = /run nvim ``` ## 🧲 How the tray + summon works ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User (shortcut / hotkey) participant S as cldr --summon participant I as Loopback IPC (127.0.0.1, ~/.cldr/port) participant W as Running window U->>S: press shortcut S->>I: connect, send "SUMMON" I->>W: accept, reply "OK-WINDOW" W->>W: raise_window() (Win32 / xdotool) S-->>U: exits (no duplicate window) ``` Loopback-only control channel — no clipboard, no privileged APIs, no firewall prompt. A detached daemon (`--daemon-start`) services queued `open`/`run`/`sys` requests from atomically-published per-request files in a private, per-user state directory. ![Help cheat sheet](docs/screenshots/03-help.png) ## 🎯 Design goals | Goal | How | |---|---| | **Small** | 4 crates total (`crossterm`, `ratatui`, `open`, `walkdir`); full LTO, one codegen unit, symbols stripped, `panic=abort` | | **Fast** | Redraw only on change; a single 250 ms `poll()` when idle; no async runtime | | **Dependency-free at runtime** | One binary; nothing to install, no DLLs, no Python | | **Private** | Never reads or writes the clipboard; no telemetry; the only socket is loopback | > **Why a terminal window, not a native GUI?** A native toolkit (winit/egui/Qt) > would add tens of MB of dependencies and binary size. The terminal *is* the > smallest possible GUI here — on Windows the console is auto-shrunk to a > compact ~92×26 box; on Linux your terminal emulator sizes it. ## 🏗️ Project layout ```text src/ ├─ main.rs CLI router (foreground / --summon / --tray / daemon / --self-test) ├─ engine.rs dispatcher, calc parser, smart cascade (+ unit tests) ├─ extras.rs config, aliases, history, unit conversion, base64, self-test ├─ ipc.rs loopback-TCP summon control channel ├─ tui.rs ratatui command window (dirty redraw, history, compact window) ├─ summon.rs window raising, autostart, tray loop └─ daemon.rs detached background worker packaging/ Windows installer (Inno Setup), Linux install/uninstall, portable notes scripts/ shortcut installers (PowerShell + sh) docs/ user guide, setup guide, shortcut recipes, screenshots ``` ## 📚 Documentation | Document | Contents | |---|---| | [docs/USER_GUIDE.md](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) | walkthrough, keys, examples, troubleshooting | | [docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md) | build, install, shortcuts, autostart, releases | | [docs/SHORTCUTS.md](docs/SHORTCUTS.md) | per-DE / per-tool hotkey recipes | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | version history | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | dev workflow, code style, PR rules | ## 🚀 Releases Releases are **tag-driven** and fully automated: ```bash # bump version in Cargo.toml + CHANGELOG.md, then: git tag v1.3.0 && git push origin v1.3.0 ``` CI builds Windows + Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), packages portable archives and the Windows installer, generates `SHA256SUMS.txt`, attests build provenance, and publishes the GitHub Release. ## ⚖️ License & attribution © **2026 Dr. Sohil Momin ([drsamonline](https://github.com/drsamonline))** — [PolyForm Noncommercial licensed with a mandatory attribution clause](LICENSE). HCS: # Holistic Compression Sources (HCS) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) Canonical, offline, vendored source vault for the **CHCE** engine (Chimera Hybrid Compression Engine) and all CHIMERA-family projects (`heavenzip`, `ziptastic`, `compfactory`). Every third-party compressor, preprocessor, recompressor, and entropy-coder reference used by CHCE lives in [`/old`](./old), pinned at a known-good revision. Consumers pull this repo with `git subtree` and build from the pinned tree. **Design constraints (non-negotiable):** 1. **Offline-only.** No neural networks, no model files, no GPU runtimes. Context-mixing (CM) compressors like `zpaq`, `paq8px`, `lpaq` are pure algorithms — they are **not AI** and are fully offline. 2. **Single source of truth.** One copy of each source, no nested `.git` directories. Sources are vendored flat, with one deliberate exception: 23 of them are **git submodules** pinned to an upstream commit, because copying another project's history would make this vault a fork of it rather than a mirror. See [Vendored sources and submodules](#vendored-sources-and-submodules). 3. **License-audited.** Every source is listed with its licence identifier in `SOURCES`. The full licence texts are **not yet collected** — see [Known gaps](#known-gaps). --- ## Integration Model | Consumer | How it uses HCS | |---|---| | `ziptastic` (native engine) | `git subtree` of `HCS` into `vendor/` | | `heavenzip` (orchestrator) | Consumes **prebuilt binaries** released by `ziptastic` — does not build from `/old` | | `compfactory` (workshop) | Full checkout; edits propagate back to HCS via PR | > **Rule:** `heavenzip` must never contain algorithm code; `ziptastic` must > never shell out to external executables. HCS exists to feed `ziptastic`. --- ## Repository Layout HCS/ ├── README.md # this file ├── SOURCES # machine-readable manifest (id, url, pin, licence, integration) ├── .gitmodules # URL mapping for Treat it as an **external process** invoked by `heavenzip`, or drop JPEG recompression for now. - **`advancecomp` is GPL-3.** Same rule: external process, not linked. - **`upx` is GPL-2.0.** Same rule. - **`lzo` is GPL / commercial dual.** Do not link unless CHCE is GPL. - **`paq8px` is GPL-2.0.** Treat as an **external process** in `heavenzip` for the `--max-ratio` tier, not a linked library. All other listed sources are permissive (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, zlib, PD, 0BSD) and safe to link into a closed-source CHCE core. --- ## 🏆 The Offline Ratio Ladder CHCE selects a tier per block based on the joint parser's cost model. This is the target performance envelope across the sources in `/old`: | Tier | Backend(s) | Ratio vs xz | Speed vs xz | |---|---|---|---| | **Max ratio** | `paq8px` / `LPAQ9` | 0.70–0.80× | 0.001× | | **High ratio** | `zpaqfranz -m5` / `zpaq` | 0.80–0.85× | 0.01× | | **Strong** | `bzip3` / `libbsc` / PPMd (`7z`) | 0.90–0.98× | 0.5–2× | | **Baseline** | `xz` (LZMA2) | 1.00× | 1.00× | | **Balanced** | `zxc` / `zstd -19` / `brotli -q11` | 1.05–1.15× | 3–10× | | **Fast** | `density` / `lz4` / `csc` / `lizard` | 1.3–1.5× | 20–50× | | **Ultra-fast** | `heatshrink` / `brieflz` / `snappy` | 2× | 100×+ | Plus these orthogonal transforms that operate **before** the entropy tier: - **Semantic recompression** — `preflate`, `preflate-rs`, `precomp-cpp`, `aqueous`, `rhefo` (DEFLATE, JPEG, PNG, PDF, PE, SQLite, ~20 formats) - **Text tokenization** — `parmar` (+7–9.6 % on LZMA2 over raw text) - **Numeric bit-transpose** — `bitshuffle`, `pcodec` (2–10× on typed arrays) - **Short-string coding** — `shoco`, `smaz` - **Long-range dedup** — `srep` (matches beyond LZMA's 64 MB window) - **Executable packing** — `upx`, `zelf` --- ## Bumping a Source 1. `cd old/` and check out the desired revision. 2. Update the `pin` in `SOURCES`. 3. Confirm the licence from the source's own `LICENSE`/`COPYING` file and correct the `SOURCES` row if it moved. (`LICENSES/` is planned, not present — see [Known gaps](#known-gaps).) 4. Regenerate any integration tests in `ziptastic` that consume this source. 5. Open a PR titled `bump: → `. --- ## Adding a New Source 1. `git clone --depth=1 old/` **inside this repo**. 2. `rm -rf old//.git` — **critical, do not skip**. 3. Add a row to `SOURCES`. 4. Record the licence identifier in the `SOURCES` row. Full licence texts are not collected yet — see [Known gaps](#known-gaps). 5. Add a row to the appropriate section of this README. 6. Commit: `add: ()`. --- ## Quick Verification To check that `/old` contains no nested `.git` folders (the most common mistake when vendoring): ```bash find old -name .git -type d # should print nothing ``` (The 23 pinned submodules are the exception and are expected to carry `.git`; the check above is about *copied* sources.) The equivalent for the pins is `./scripts/check-vendor.sh`, below. ## Vendored sources and submodules Most of `old/` is plain vendored source. 23 entries are **git submodules** — they pin one commit of an upstream repository rather than copying its history, so the mirror stays a mirror and HCS never claims authorship of code it did not write. ```bash git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/drsamonline/HCS # or, in an existing clone: git submodule update --init --recursive ``` **Verify at any time:** ```bash ./scripts/check-vendor.sh # exit 0 = every source present and mapped python3 tools/check-sources.py # exit 0 = every directory recorded, every id resolves ``` The second one exists because the first never reads `SOURCES`. A directory can materialise and still have no recorded upstream, licence or integration, and an id can point at a directory name the vault does not use (`xz` for `xz-master`). `tools/check-sources.py` reads both sides and says which rows and which directories disagree. It runs in CI, advisory until the findings it currently reports are settled. ### Why the guard exists Until this was fixed, `old/` carried those 23 gitlinks with **no `.gitmodules` file at all**. That state is unrecoverable: git records a commit SHA for each submodule but has nowhere to fetch it from, so `git submodule update --init` could not work, and every clone — HCS, and every repo that vendors a copy of it — silently got 23 empty directories. Nothing failed until a build or a benchmark reached for one of them, and then it looked like a missing source rather than a broken mirror. The repair was to add the URL mapping that was always missing (the recorded pins were all valid — 20 resolve by ref, and the remaining 3 fetch fine by SHA). The guard is the part that makes it not happen again: `scripts/check-vendor.sh` fails if any directory under `old/` is empty, if a gitlink has no `.gitmodules` entry, or if a `.gitmodules` entry points at a directory that does not exist. CI runs it on every push with `submodules: recursive`, so a mirror that cannot materialise goes red instead of going quiet. ## Known gaps - **Licence texts.** `SOURCES` records an SPDX identifier and an integration verdict per source, which is what `ziptastic` needs to decide whether a source may be linked. The full texts are not in the repository: there is no `LICENSES/`. Nothing in the tree is broken by this, but a downstream user shipping a binary cannot audit a licence from this vault alone, and the "copy the text before linking" rule has never had a directory to copy into. - **`MANIFEST.json`** records a producer and class per file for the files it knows about, and was last written on 2026-11-04. It is not regenerated on every push, so treat it as a snapshot rather than an index. `tools/manifest.py` is what writes it. - **The HCS `LICENSE` is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0**, which covers the files this repository authors (the manifest, the catalogue, the tooling). The vendored sources under `old/` keep their own licences, which are the ones that govern them; the PolyForm terms cannot relicense code HCS did not write. That distinction is worth stating plainly because the badge at the top of this file reads as if it covers everything. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # 🏥 HHMS — Homeopathic Hospital Management System ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **A LAN-based hospital management system purpose-built for homeopathic hospitals and clinics.** Runs entirely on the local network with a server-owned database — *no internet dependency, no cloud lock-in.* [![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/landing%20page-live-1d4ed8?logo=githubpages&logoColor=white)](https://drsamonline.github.io/HMS/) [![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-1d4ed8?logo=githubpages&logoColor=white)](https://drsamonline.github.io/) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.0.1-informational)](VERSION) [![License: Proprietary](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Proprietary-red.svg)](LICENSE) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-569%20passed-brightgreen)](backend/tests) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20LAN-lightgrey)](docs/DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) **Landing page:** · **Demo build:** · **Demo data guide:** [docs/DEMO_DATA.md](docs/DEMO_DATA.md) HHMS is a LAN application, so there is no hosted web demo — a fresh install seeds a full demo dataset automatically on first run.
--- ## 📐 Architecture at a Glance ```text ┌──────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ HHMS-Client.exe │ ─────► │ LAN HTTP/JSON │ ─────► │ HHMS-Server.exe │ │ (WebView2 UI) │ │ │ │ (server-owned SQLite) │ └──────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────┘ ``` | Layer | Description | |-------|-------------| | 💻 **Client** | Lightweight HTML/CSS/vanilla-JavaScript interface hosted in WebView2 | | 🔌 **Transport** | HTTP/JSON over the hospital LAN with automatic server discovery | | 🗄️ **Server** | The only component that touches the shared SQLite database — the client never opens it directly | 📖 Details: [DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE](docs/DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [BACKEND_ARCHITECTURE](docs/BACKEND_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [FRONTEND_ARCHITECTURE](docs/FRONTEND_ARCHITECTURE.md) --- ## 📁 Repository Layout | Path | Contents | |------|----------| | [`backend/`](backend) | Python server: API routers, services, models, Alembic migrations, tests | | [`frontend/`](frontend) | Client UI: HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript modules | | [`client/`](client) | Native Windows client host (WebView2 shell) | | [`docs/`](docs) | Full specification, architecture, workflow, and batch documentation ([index](docs/INDEX.md)) | | [`.ai/`](.ai) | Project constitution, coding rules, decisions, and state tracking | | [`data/`](data) | Runtime data directory (server-owned database and secrets) | --- ## ✨ Features **Clinical** — patient registration & search, OPD queue with token system, homoeopathic case records, diagnosis/ICD-11, prescriptions, IPD admission with ward/bed management, investigations/laboratory/X-Ray, annual case rollover and archival. **Operational** — billing & payments with live-derived invoice balances, pharmacy stock ledger with dispense integrity, procurement/goods receipt, department/service/designation masters, role-based dashboards (outstanding billing, bed occupancy, pending investigations, OPD queue, discharge audit). **Reporting & printing** — statistics engine, 16 screen/paper-parity print envelopes (receivables aging, collection summaries, receipt continuity, settlement/refund audits, ward occupancy, investigation billing reconciliation), PDF generation, report scheduling, batch printing. **Release-ready infrastructure** — LAN server discovery (UDP port 38541), single-file Windows/Linux server binaries, Inno/NSIS installers, automatic dual-platform GitHub releases (rolling `nightly` prerelease on every push to `main`, stable Release on `v*.*.*` tags), backup/restore workflows, login rate limiting, JWT hardening, secret-key rotation runbook. **569 backend tests passing.** --- ## 🚀 Quick Start ```bash cd backend pip install -r requirements.txt python -m app.server ``` The server runs migrations automatically, creates the default administrator (`admin` / `admin` — change it immediately; disable with `HHMS_BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT_ADMIN=false`), seeds a full **2025 demo dataset** on first run (no commands needed — see below), serves the built-in web GUI at `http://localhost:8000/`, and listens on the configured LAN port. See [SERVER_STARTUP](docs/SERVER_STARTUP.md) and [DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE](docs/DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) for production setup. ### Demo data (automatic on first run — no commands) On a brand-new install the server seeds a full year of realistic demo data by itself at startup — patients, OPD tokens, cases, prescriptions, dispenses, lab results, admissions, invoices and payments — so the GUI is populated the moment you open it. Portable builds (folder or EXE) work out of the box: copy → run → log in as `admin` / `admin`. - The seed runs **only** when the database is pristine; any install that already contains real data is never touched. - Opt out with environment variable `HHMS_SEED_DEMO_DATA=false` (recommended for production deployments). - Optional manual commands (not required): `python -m app.server seed-demo-data` supports `--year` and `--force`. Details: [docs/DEMO_DATA.md](docs/DEMO_DATA.md). --- ## 🔧 Development Workflow 1. Use the latest verified repository ZIP as the source of truth. 2. Add any number of symptoms to each, each with a chapter, grade and modalities. | | **Repertory** | Chapters (Mind, Head, Stomach…) → rubrics → graded remedies. Rubrics support a parent heading and a note. | | **Marking system** | Define the grading scale yourself. Four presets ship in, and you can edit any of them or add your own schemes. | | **Author & branding** | Your name, credentials, clinic, email, website, book title, edition, year, copyright line and licence — stamped into every PDF, HTML file and workbook you export. | | **Cases** | A private case logger: log a case, track the outcome (Cured / Improved / No Change / Aggravated / Suppressed) and review the history. | | **Help** | The full how-to guide lives inside the app, plus a first-run tour and print-to-PDF. | | **About** | The dedication, the maker, and the licence it is released under. | Everything is stored **locally in your browser** (IndexedDB). Nothing is uploaded anywhere. --- ## 🎚️ Your marking scale Four schemes ship in — **Kent 3-point**, **4-point with capitals**, **Boenninghausen 5-point** and a **Simple 0–2** — or press *New scheme* and define your own: any number of levels, each with a label and a style (plain / italic / bold / bold-italic / capitals / superscript). Rubrics everywhere use the active scheme, and every export renders the grades accordingly. --- ## 📖 How to use it The same guide is built into the app — open the **Help** tab, or press **Take the tour**. **Getting started** 1. Open the **Materia Medica** tab and add your first remedy (or edit the three starter remedies). 2. Give it an abbreviation — short forms like `Acon` or `Nat-m` are what the repertory shows. 3. Add symptoms to it: pick a chapter (Mind, Head, Stomach…), write the symptom, set a grade. 4. Open the **Repertory** tab, add a chapter, then add rubrics inside it. 5. Inside a rubric, type a remedy abbreviation and press Enter to attach it, then choose its grade. 6. Fill in your **Author** details, then go to **Data** and export your book. **Building the repertory.** A rubric is a symptom heading such as *Anxiety, about health*. It may also have a parent heading (so *Morning* under *Sweat of the feet* reads as *Sweat of the feet, Morning*) and a note. **Backups.** Your work lives only in this browser. Export a JSON backup regularly, and import it on another device to carry your project across. --- ## 📤 Export & import | Format | Contents | |---|---| | **JSON — full backup** | Everything, re-importable here to restore the project. | | **JSON — OMM** | Repertory and/or materia medica in the reader-app schema (v1.1). | | **CSV** | All datasets as a zip, or one dataset at a time. | | **Excel (.xlsx)** | A workbook: Info, Remedies, Symptoms, Repertory, Cases, Marking. | | **PDF** | A printable book with your author block and copyright. | | **HTML** | A self-contained, styled document you can open or host. | | **SQL (.sql)** | Portable `INSERT` statements for SQLite, Postgres or MySQL. | | **SQLite (.sqlite)** | A real database file (`meta`, `remedy`, `symptom`, `rubric`, `remedy_link`, `case_log`). | **Import** accepts a full JSON backup, an OMM repertory or materia-medica file, or CSV — with **Merge** or **Replace** mode. --- ## 🔧 Under the hood All writers are dependency-free and run entirely in the browser: the `.xlsx`, `.pdf` and `.sqlite` files are generated byte-by-byte in JavaScript, so the app never needs a network connection or a library from a CDN. --- ## 🔗 Compatibility with the OMM reader app The JSON exports use the same envelope the reader app reads (`schema_version: "1.1"`, `type: "repertory"` / `"materia_medica"`, a `book` provenance block, and `sections → rubrics → remedy_table` / `remedies → symptoms`). A repertory built here drops straight into that collection, and a book extracted by the OMM pipeline can be imported here for editing. --- ## 🛠️ Running it locally ```bash python3 -m http.server 8080 # then open http://localhost:8080 ``` Deploy anywhere static — GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages. The service worker takes it offline automatically. --- ## 🧱 Data model ``` remedy { id, name, abbrev, common_name, kingdom, family, source, notes } symptom { id, remedy_id, chapter, text, grade, modalities[{dir,text}], notes } section { id, title, order } rubric { id, section_id, text, parent, note, remedies[{remedy_id, grade, polarity, note}] } case { id, patient_initials, age, gender, chief_complaint, prescribed_remedy_id, potency, dosage, outcome, follow_up_notes, date } settings { author{…}, marking{active, schemes[{id,name,levels[{v,label,style}]}]} } ``` `grade` is a level value from the active marking scheme. `polarity` is `+` (default) or `-` (antidotal). **Upgrading from v1:** the app opens the same `MateriaMedicaDB` database at version 2 and adds the new stores — existing remedies, symptoms and cases are preserved and old symptom fields are migrated automatically. --- ## # NOVA — Semantic Programming Platform [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **A statically-typed, compiled systems programming language.** Its compiler lowers NOVA source through a semantic pipeline — lexer, parser, semantic analyser, SIR, lowerer — to four backends: **C, JavaScript, Rust and WebAssembly**, with a runtime, package manager, language server and debugger alongside. **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/NEO/)** · **[Examples](examples/)** · **[Language spec](docs/language/)** · **[Development plan](DEV_PLAN.md)** · **[Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md)** · **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** Live demo: not yet available — the project is pre-release (Phase 4 in progress).
--- Semantic Programming Platform [![Phase 1 Complete](https://img.shields.io/badge/Phase-1%20Complete-brightgreen)](DEV_PLAN.md) [![Phase 2 Complete](https://img.shields.io/badge/Phase-2%20Complete-brightgreen)](DEV_PLAN.md) [![Phase 3 Complete](https://img.shields.io/badge/Phase-3%20Complete-brightgreen)](DEV_PLAN.md) [![Phase 4 Next](https://img.shields.io/badge/Phase-4%20Next-yellow)](DEV_PLAN.md) [![Compiler Core](https://img.shields.io/badge/Compiler-3500%2B%20LOC-blue)](compiler/) [![Runtime System](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runtime-2881%2B%20LOC-orange)](runtime/) [![Tooling](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tooling-3600%2B%20LOC-orange)](pkg/) [![Backends](https://img.shields.io/badge/Backends-4%20Targets-orange)](backends/) ## Overview NOVA is a statically-typed, compiled systems programming language with a complete tooling ecosystem. The compiler transforms NOVA source code into multiple target languages (C, JavaScript, Rust, WebAssembly) through a robust semantic analysis pipeline. ## Current Status **✅ Phase 1: Compiler Core - COMPLETE** - Full lexer, parser, semantic analyzer implemented - SIR (Semantic Intermediate Representation) defined - Lowerer converts AST to SIR - 4 backends: C, JavaScript, Rust, WebAssembly - Total: ~3,500+ lines of compiler code **✅ Phase 2: Runtime System - COMPLETE** - ✅ Memory management (192 lines, arena allocation, GC foundation) - ✅ Type system (260 lines, type registry, dynamic values) - ✅ Error handling (297 lines, panic handling, backtraces) - ✅ FFI support (332 lines, C interop, FFI arrays) - ✅ Core runtime library (139 lines, initialization, stats) - ✅ Garbage collection (315 lines, mark-and-sweep implementation) - ✅ I/O runtime (535 lines, file I/O, streams, directories) - ✅ Threading primitives (314 lines, mutexes, RW locks, condition variables) - ✅ Async runtime (114 lines, futures, channels, delay) - Total: 2,881 lines, 30+ tests **✅ Phase 3: Tooling - COMPLETE** - ✅ Package manager (1,674 lines) - CLI with 12 commands, manifest parsing, dependency resolution, registry - ✅ Language server (522 lines) - LSP handlers, completions, diagnostics, hover, go-to-definition - ✅ Debugger (1,405 lines) - Interactive REPL, breakpoints, session management, target control - Total: 3,601 lines across all tools **🔄 Phase 4: Polish & Integration - NEXT** - Standard library implementation - LSP-compiler integration for real-time diagnostics - Debugger-binary integration - End-to-end testing - Performance optimization - Documentation See [Development Plan](DEV_PLAN.md) for detailed status. ## Quick Start ```bash # Compile a NOVA program to C cd compiler # (Rust toolchain required) cargo run -- ../examples/test_final.nova --target c ``` ## Project Structure ``` /workspace ├── compiler/ # Main compiler (~3,500 LOC) │ ├── src/lexer/ # Tokenization (309 lines) │ ├── src/parser/ # Recursive descent parser (907 lines) │ ├── src/sema/ # Semantic analysis (773 lines) │ ├── src/sir/ # IR definition (146 lines) │ ├── src/lowerer/ # AST→SIR lowering (550 lines) │ └── src/backend/ # Backend interface (338 lines) ├── backends/ # Target code generators (1,529 lines) │ ├── c/ # C backend (449 lines) │ ├── javascript/ # JavaScript backend (343 lines) │ ├── rust/ # Rust backend (352 lines) │ └── wasm/ # WebAssembly backend (385 lines) ├── runtime/ # Runtime system (2,881 lines) │ ├── src/memory.rs # Memory management (192 lines) │ ├── src/types.rs # Type registry (260 lines) │ ├── src/error.rs # Error handling (297 lines) │ ├── src/ffi.rs # FFI support (332 lines) │ ├── src/gc.rs # Garbage collection (315 lines) │ ├── src/lib.rs # Core library (139 lines) │ ├── src/io/ # I/O runtime (535 lines) │ ├── src/threading/ # Threading primitives (314 lines) │ └── src/async_rt/ # Async runtime (114 lines) ├── pkg/ # Package manager (1,674 lines) │ └── src/ # CLI, manifest, resolver, registry ├── lsp/ # Language server (522 lines) │ └── src/main.rs # LSP handlers, completions, diagnostics ├── dbg/ # Debugger (1,405 lines) │ └── src/ # REPL, breakpoints, sessions, target control ├── crates/nova-common/ # Shared utilities ├── stdlib/ # Standard library (scaffolds) ├── examples/ # Example programs └── tests/ # Test suite ``` ## Features ### Implemented ✅ - Repertorium-Publicum: # Repertorium Publicum Explorer ![offline: no network](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![deps: 0 runtime](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) ![tests: 14 passing](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![rubrics: 74,480](docs/assets/badge-rubrics.svg) ![payload: 1.9 MB, one file](docs/assets/badge-size.svg) ![licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg) **A repertory you can search like a ledger.** 74,480 rubrics and 735,460 graded remedy links from **Repertorium Publicum** (2008) — the printed three grades intact, a case builder, and grade-weighted repertorisation — in one HTML file that runs with no server, no account and no network. **[Open the repertory →](https://drsamonline.github.io/kent-repertory-explorer/play/index.html)** · [the landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/kent-repertory-explorer/) · [the data](https://github.com/drsamonline/homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json) · [the source](pipeline/) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) --- ## What it is, precisely The data is **Repertorium Publicum** by **Vladimir Polony (2008)**, published as part of the [OpenRep](https://github.com/nondeterministic/oorep) source code and licensed **GPL v3**. It is **not** Kent's *Repertory of the Homoeopathic Materia Medica*, 1897 first edition. It has its own chapter structure — separate *Clinical*, *Appetite*, *Blood* and *Heart & Circulation* chapters, which Kent does not have — and its own additions. Earlier releases of this app described it as Kent 1897; that was wrong, and it has been corrected throughout: this README, the page, the app's own footer and both manifests. ## What's inside | | | |---|---| | Rubrics | **74,480** | | Graded remedy links | **735,460** | | Remedies | **669** | | Chapters | **41** | | The whole app | **one 1.9 MB HTML file** (gzip + base64, decompressed in the browser) | | The dataset itself | **1.35 MB gzipped**, down from 1.46 MB after re-encoding | Every link carries a grade, taken from the typography of the printed repertory: | grade | meaning | links | |---|---|---| | **3** | strongest association | 71,582 | | *2* | moderate | 198,591 | | 1 | least | 465,287 | ## Features - **Search in repertory language** — `anxiety night`, `thirstless`, `weeping consolation`. Results are ranked **narrowest first**, because the rubrics with three remedies are the ones that narrow a case. - **Chapter browse** across all 41 chapters, with rubric counts. - **Filters** — narrow-only with an adjustable threshold, sort by narrowest / broadest / A–Z / chapter. - **Named cases** — keep several at once: switch, rename, delete. Each holds its own rubrics and notes. - **Case builder** — add rubrics, attach a note to each, remove or clear. **Undo/redo** with `Ctrl+Z`. - **Scoring you can see** — three weightings (3·2·1, 1·1·1, 9·4·1) and an eliminative filter that keeps only grade-2-or-better coverage. The formula is printed under the control and every export says which one produced the numbers. - **Analysis** — remedies ranked by the sum of grades and rubrics covered; minimum-grade filter; "cover all rubrics"; exclude a remedy (it stays visible, struck through, and can be brought back). - **Matrix** — remedy × rubric grid showing each grade. - **Why a remedy ranks** — click it in the analysis to see every rubric of *this* case it covers, at which grade, and which it misses. - **Remedy → rubrics** — click any remedy chip to see every rubric it appears in, by chapter and grade. - **Chapter drill-down** — browse a chapter, then its branches, then search inside one. - **"Did you mean"** — a spelling that finds nothing is matched against the repertory's own vocabulary. - **Export** — plain text, CSV, JSON, copy to clipboard, and a clean print/PDF sheet. - **Deep links** — `#q=anxiety+night`, `#tab=analysis`, `#demo=case`, `#remedy=Ars`, `#rubric=`. No router, no dependency; this is what drives the live demo on the landing page. - **Themes** — dark, light, high-contrast. **Keyboard-first** with `/`, `↑ ↓`, `Enter`, `c`, `a`, `m`, `t`, `Esc`. - **Offline-first** — one self-contained HTML file, a manifest at the right path and a service worker that precaches the app and serves the HTML network-first, so a release lands on the next visit. The header says `Offline ready` once the app is cached, and offers `New version — reload` when one lands. - **A print sheet that is the case** — rubrics, notes, analysis and matrix, without the interface. - **A build stamp in the footer**, so "am I on the new one?" is answerable from inside the app. - **Case persists** in local storage; notes included. ## Using it 1. Search in **repertory language** — not the patient's words. 2. Prefer **narrow** rubrics; a rubric with 250 remedies tells you little, one with three is gold. 3. **Add** the rubrics that survive to your case. 4. Open **Analysis** to rank remedies across them. 5. Treat the ranking as a **shortlist to study in the materia medica** — the repertory narrows, the materia medica decides. ## Screenshots | landing page | the app | |---|---| | ![Landing page](docs/assets/landing-desktop.png) | ![The app](docs/assets/app-desktop.png) | Both are taken from the real pages by `scripts/shot.sh` — headless Chromium, no mock-ups. Write notes in plain natural language — SmartNote uses an LLM to automatically classify them, detect priority, generate a title, and extract dates/times ("tomorrow at 3pm") so nothing slips through the cracks. **🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/SmartNotes/)**  ·  **▶ [Demo & screens](https://drsamonline.github.io/SmartNotes/#demo)**  ·  **[Source](https://github.com/drsamonline/SmartNotes)**
--- - **License:** PolyForm Noncommercial — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE) - **Version:** 1.0.0 - **Portable apps (planned):** Windows `.exe` + Linux portable builds — design in [docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md](./docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md) ## Features - 🤖 **AI note analysis** — automatic categorization into *Tasks, Deadlines, Schedule, Thoughts, Learning*, priority detection (Low/Medium/High), title generation, and natural-language date/time extraction. - ⏰ **Reminder scheduling** — reminders fire 1 hour before a deadline or scheduled time via a durable heartbeat endpoint (`POST /api/scheduled/process-reminders`). - 🔔 **Multi-channel notifications** — push notifications (Manus owner notification API) and optional email delivery through a provider-neutral webhook. Every delivery attempt is logged as `sent`, `failed`, or `skipped`. - 🔍 **Search & filtering** — full-text search over titles/content, category tabs, "hide completed" toggle, and sorting by date, priority, or category. - 📊 **Dashboard stats** — totals, completed, pending, and overdue counts with per-category summaries and overdue highlighting. - 💾 **Backup & export** — JSON backup export/import, CSV and Markdown exports, and reusable filter presets. - 🎨 **Brutalist design system** — black background, oversized condensed white typography, red divider accents; fully responsive with mobile navigation. ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | |-----------|--------------------------------------------------------| | Frontend | React 19, Vite 7, Wouter, TanStack Query, tRPC client | | UI | Tailwind CSS 4, Radix UI (shadcn/ui), Framer Motion, Lucide icons | | Backend | Node.js, Express, tRPC 11 | | Database | MySQL via Drizzle ORM + drizzle-kit migrations | | Auth | Manus OAuth (session cookie `app_session_id`, JWT via `jose`) | | AI | LLM invoked through the platform forge API | | Testing | Vitest | | Packages | pnpm (workspace uses patched `wouter` via `patches/`) | ## Project Structure ``` ├── client/ # React SPA (pages, components, hooks, contexts) │ └── src/ │ ├── pages/ # Home, CategoryView, SearchPage, NotificationHistory, Settings │ ├── components/ # DashboardLayout, NoteFilters, ui/ (shadcn primitives) │ └── contexts/ # ThemeContext ├── server/ # Express + tRPC backend │ ├── _core/ # Framework: trpc, oauth, llm, notification, heartbeat, env │ ├── notes.router.ts # Notes CRUD, search, stats, backup, notification history │ ├── ai.ts # LLM categorization / priority / date-time extraction │ ├── notifications.ts # Reminder processing and delivery logging │ ├── db.ts # Drizzle data access layer │ └── *.test.ts # Vitest suites ├── shared/ # Code shared between client and server ├── drizzle/ # Schema and SQL migrations ├── patches/ # pnpm dependency patches ├── vite.config.ts # Client build config └── vitest.config.ts # Test runner config ``` ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites - Node.js ≥ 20 - pnpm (`packageManager: pnpm@10.4.1`) - A MySQL-compatible database (e.g. TiDB/MySQL 8) ### Installation ```bash pnpm install ``` ### Environment Variables Copy your values into a `.env` file in the project root: | Variable | Required | Description | |-------------------------|----------|----------------------------------------------------| | `DATABASE_URL` | ✅ | MySQL connection string | | `JWT_SECRET` | ✅ | Secret used to sign session cookies | | `OAUTH_SERVER_URL` | ✅ | Manus OAuth server base URL | | `VITE_APP_ID` | ✅ | Application identifier | | `OWNER_OPEN_ID` | | Open ID of the app owner (target of push notices) | | `BUILT_IN_FORGE_API_URL`| | Platform LLM/forge API endpoint | | `BUILT_IN_FORGE_API_KEY`| | Forge API key | | `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL` | | Webhook endpoint for outbound email delivery | | `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_API_KEY` | | Optional bearer key for the email webhook | Email delivery is optional: if `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL` is not configured, email deliveries are recorded as **skipped** in the notification history rather than failing silently. ### Run ```bash # Development (tsx watch on server + Vite HMR on client) pnpm dev # Type check pnpm check # Tests pnpm test # Production build & start pnpm build pnpm start ``` ### Database Migrations ```bash pnpm db:push # drizzle-kit generate && drizzle-kit migrate ``` ## API Overview All APIs are served under `/api/trpc` (tRPC) plus a few REST endpoints. ### tRPC routers - **`system`** — health/system info. - **`auth.me`**, **`auth.logout`** — session user and cookie logout. - **`notes.*`** (protected unless noted): - `create` — create a note (AI analysis runs automatically) - `list`, `get`, `listByCategory`, `search` - `update`, `updateNote`, `toggleComplete`, `delete` - `stats` — dashboard metrics - `notificationHistory` — recent delivery log - `importBackup` — bulk restore from exported JSON ### REST endpoints - `POST /api/oauth/callback` — OAuth code exchange, sets session cookie. - `POST /api/scheduled/process-reminders` — processes due reminders. Wire this to a durable scheduler (see below). ## Data Model - **users** — Manus OAuth identity (`openId` unique), role, profile. - **notes** — `userId`, `title`, `content`, `category` (enum of the 5 categories), `priority` (Low/Medium/High), `dueDate`, `scheduledDate`, `isCompleted`. Indexed on `(userId, category)`, `(userId, dueDate)`, `(userId, scheduledDate)`. - **reminders** — `noteId` (cascade delete), `reminderTime`, `notificationType` (push/email/both), `isSent`. - **notificationLogs** — per-channel delivery record: `channel` (push/email), `status` (sent/failed/skipped), title, content, error. See `drizzle/schema.ts` for the authoritative definition. ## Production Reminder Setup Reminders are processed by an external durable scheduler calling: ``` POST /api/scheduled/process-reminders ``` After deployment, create a **one-minute Heartbeat job** targeting that endpoint. Failed/skipped-only reminders stay pending and will be retried once the email provider is configured. ## Testing ```bash pnpm test ``` Vitest suites cover AI parsing fallbacks, auth/logout cookie handling, note export/import round-trips, templates, preferences, and reminder delivery (sent/failed/skipped states). ## Known QA Notes - Chromium smoke checks passed at 1280px and 375px (dashboard, category, search, alert history views). - Firefox/Safari checks are recommended post-deployment (not available in the development sandbox). ## 📚 Documentation Set | Document | Purpose | |---|---| | [README.md](./README.md) | This file — overview, setup, usage | | [LICENSE](./LICENSE) | PolyForm Noncommercial license | | [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) | Release history | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) | Development workflow & guidelines | | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | System design deep dive | | [docs/API.md](./docs/API.md) | tRPC + REST API reference | | [docs/DATABASE.md](./docs/DATABASE.md) | Schema & migrations | | ⭐ [docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md](./docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md) | **50 non-bloat enhancements backlog** | | ⭐ [docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md](./docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md) | **Windows `.exe` + Linux portable app design (RFC)** | | ⭐ [docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](./docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) | **Staged delivery plan (Stages 0–5) with go/no-go gates** | | [todo.md](./todo.md) | Project task tracker | ## 📄 License Distributed under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0** — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE) for details. ---

> **564 tools that actually run. One popup. Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. No framework, no telemetry, no remote code.**

TTB (Tiny Toolbox) is a Manifest V3 browser extension that puts a large collection of small, genuinely working utilities — text, calculations, developer helpers, page tools, data, design, finance, media, security, accessibility — behind one fast, offline-first interface.

Every tool in this release was executed with realistic input and its output graded. Tools that could not work were deleted rather than shipped as placeholders. The full evidence is in **[TOOL_AUDIT.md](TOOL_AUDIT.md)**.

## What's in it

- **564 working tools across 18 categories**, reachable from the popup or side panel.
- **Category rail + search** with keyboard navigation (`↑` `↓` `Enter`), favourites (`★`) and recents.
- **Per-tool inputs** — multi-field tools render exactly the fields they need, including file pickers for media tools.
- **Text, HTML and image output** — rich results render in a sandboxed preview; images render inline with a download link.
- **Destructive actions are gated** — history/cookie/cache cleaners and tab closers are dry-run until you tick the confirmation.

## Runs in your browser

One source tree, assembled per browser with `npm run build`. Every build carries the same catalog; a tool that needs an API the browser lacks is disabled and says so.

| | Chrome / Edge / Brave / Opera | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog, popup UI, per-tool inputs | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Page tools, tab tools, crypto, computation | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Side panel | ✅ `side_panel` | ✅ `sidebar_action` | — |
| History · bookmarks · downloads · cache clearing · fonts | ✅ | ✅ | — not exposed |
| QR / barcode scanning · screen colour picker | ✅ | — | — |

Full matrix: **[BROWSER_SUPPORT.md](BROWSER_SUPPORT.md)**.

## Install

**Chrome / Edge / Brave / Opera** — open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**, **Load unpacked**, pick the folder with `manifest.json`.

**Firefox** — `npm run build:firefox`, then `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` → **Load Temporary Add-on** → `dist/firefox/manifest.json`.

**Safari** — `npm run build:safari`, then convert with `xcrun safari-web-extension-converter`. See `INSTALL.md`.

Prebuilt ZIPs for all four targets are attached to every successful CI run (Actions → *Validate* → Artifacts).

## Development

Vanilla JavaScript, no framework, no build step beyond picking a manifest.

- `npm test` — catalog integrity, dispatcher coverage, registry metadata.
- `npm run audit` — executes every tool and grades the output; writes `tool-audit.json`.
- `npm run build` — assembles `dist/chrome`, `dist/edge`, `dist/firefox`, `dist/safari`.
- `npm run shots` — regenerates the screenshots.

See `TOOL_AUDIT.md`, `BROWSER_SUPPORT.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `USAGE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `WARNINGS.md` and `AUDIT.md`.

> **Status:** Experimental. Aetheris is not currently a production-ready, standards-complete replacement for established browsers. --- ## 📖 About Aetheris Browser is an experimental C++ browser project built on a codebase derived from the Ladybird and SerenityOS browser ecosystem. The repository contains upstream-derived infrastructure, including components and libraries from that ecosystem, alongside Aetheris-specific experiments and modifications. Aetheris is **not** presented as a browser built entirely from scratch. Its work focuses on adapting, extending, simplifying, and experimentally developing browser subsystems on an existing technical foundation. The Aetheris-specific core today is the dependency-free `AetherisRendering` foundation in [`src/rendering/`](src/rendering) with its regression suite in [`Tests/AetherisRendering/`](Tests/AetherisRendering). See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full layout of the tree. ## 🎯 Goals - Explore a smaller and more understandable browser architecture where practical. - Improve memory efficiency and startup characteristics through measurable engineering work. - Develop HTML, CSS, DOM, layout, rendering, resource, and document integration incrementally. - Preserve upstream licensing and attribution requirements. - Prefer coherent, testable changes over speculative architectural rewrites. The project aims to be more resource-conscious than typical Chromium- or Electron-based applications where practical and measurable. These are engineering goals, not guaranteed universal metrics. ## 🧬 Upstream foundation and provenance Aetheris contains code and infrastructure derived from the Ladybird/SerenityOS ecosystem. This includes foundational components visible in the repository such as `AK`, `LibCore`, and other imported browser infrastructure. Aetheris-specific code should be distinguished from upstream-derived code during maintenance and review. Existing upstream copyright notices and licenses must not be removed or replaced by project rebranding. See [`docs/UPSTREAM_ATTRIBUTION.md`](docs/UPSTREAM_ATTRIBUTION.md) for the repository-level provenance policy. ## 🏗️ Current architecture ```text HTML input ──► HTML tokenization ──► DOM │ CSS input ───► CSS parsing ──────────┤ ▼ Style resolution │ ▼ Layout ┌────────────┼────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Block Flex Grid │ ▼ Render tree │ ▼ Paint commands │ ▼ Paint execution │ ▼ Software surface ``` The rendering pipeline currently includes work in block and inline layout, Flex and Grid foundations, positioning, sizing constraints, text layout, clipping, paint ordering, backgrounds, images, fonts, and software rasterization. Feature presence does not imply complete HTML or CSS standards compliance. ## ⚙️ Architectural optimization goals ### 🧠 Resource and memory management Aetheris may evaluate standard techniques such as controlled caches, allocation reduction, compressed resource storage, and secure clearing of sensitive memory where justified. LZ4 or similar mechanisms are implementation options rather than proprietary technology claims. ### 🚀 Selective subsystem initialization The project may explore delayed initialization of expensive subsystems, including scripting, when document requirements permit. Dynamic documents and compatibility requirements make this a design problem that must be validated rather than assumed to provide a universal benefit. ### 🎨 Rendering efficiency Current and future work may reduce redundant paint operations, improve clipping and invalidation, and evaluate accelerated backends where the complexity and dependencies are justified. ## 📊 Size "Minimal" only means something next to other browsers, so the target is stated plainly: **keep the stripped `aetheris` binary as small as possible, with 10 MB as the working reference.** Size is *reported*, not enforced — every size-profile build prints the figure and the drift from the last recorded reference (`Tools/report_binary_size.cmake`), and nothing fails if it grows. The browser is expected to grow as features land; the point is to see it happening. Measured size profile (Release, `-Os`, LTO, stripped), with the comparison that gives it meaning: | Browser | Engine | Size | JavaScript | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Firefox | Gecko | 238–428 MB | yes | | Chromium | Blink | 280–447 MB | yes | | Brave | Blink | ~260 MB | yes | | Epiphany | WebKitGTK | ~95 MB | yes | | NetSurf | own (C) | 4.0–6.9 MB | no | | Dillo | own (C) | ~0.25 MB | **no** | | **Aetheris** | **own (C++20)** | **2.51 MB** | **yes (ES2025)** | So Aetheris sits roughly 40× under a WebKitGTK browser and 100× under Firefox, while still running JavaScript — the thing the smaller engines give up. Dillo remains far smaller, but has no JavaScript and no CSS3, so the two are not the same kind of tool. Sizes for other browsers are installed sizes reported by their distributions and projects; the Aetheris figure is the stripped executable. Those are not identical measures, so treat the table as an order-of-magnitude comparison. Idle memory usage and startup time are not yet claimed. Performance measurements should record the operating system, hardware, compiler, build configuration, enabled features, workload, and measurement method. Future public performance claims should be reproducible. ## 🛠️ Quick start: build and test A typical development workflow is: ```bash cmake -S . -B build cmake --build build --config Debug ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure ``` Reconfiguration is required when CMake configuration or build-registered files change. Otherwise, an existing build directory can be reused. For a dependency-light workflow that skips the upstream tree entirely, use the `Standalone` preset; for a size-first release build, use `StandaloneSize`: ```bash cmake --preset Standalone cmake --build --preset Standalone ctest --preset Standalone cmake --preset StandaloneSize # -Os, gc-sections, LTO, stripped cmake --build --preset StandaloneSize ``` The size profile applies only to the Aetheris targets (`AetherisRendering`, `AetherisRuntime`, `aetheris`); a stripped `aetheris` executable is on the 2.51 MB (2,630,800 bytes) with the current feature set: gumbo HTML5 parsing, CSS layout, bitmap-font text, PNG/JPEG/GIF/SVG/WebP images, HTTPS/TLS, the HTTP client and QuickJS. See the size table above. The `aetheris` executable exposes a small headless command surface: ```bash ./aetheris --smoke-test # init all subsystems, bounded frame loop, exit 0 ./aetheris --fetch # fetch a URL over HTTP, print status and size ./aetheris --render [out] # fetch a URL and render it to a PPM image ./aetheris --eval
