--- ## Requirements - Windows 10 (build 17763+) or Windows 11 - PowerShell 5.1+ (built in to Windows) - Administrator rights - Run `Compatibility-Check.ps1` first (menu option `9`) to confirm your machine meets these --- ## Quick start 1. Extract the ZIP anywhere. 2. Right-click `scripts\00_Ultimate_Master.bat` → **Run as administrator**. 3. Choose option `9` (Compatibility Check) first. 4. Choose option `S` to create a System Restore point (recommended before your first run). 5. Choose option `M` (Performance Snapshot) and label it `Baseline`. 6. Pick a profile (1-8). 7. Optionally take another snapshot (`M`, label it e.g. `AfterGaming`) and run `R` (Compare Two Snapshots) to see real before/after numbers. 8. If you ever want to revert everything this toolkit changed, choose `U` (Undo All Tracked Changes). --- ## Profiles — what each one actually does differently | Profile | Key tweaks | Notably does NOT do | |---|---|---| | **Daily Home** | Disable telemetry, disable Start Menu ads, disable background apps, balanced visual effects, Balanced power plan | No GPU/priority/memory tweaks | | **Gaming** | GPU hardware scheduling, foreground priority boost, network throttling removed, Game DVR off, High Performance power plan | Not recommended for battery-powered laptops | | **Office** | Background-app + Xbox-service removal, explicit balanced priority separation | No GPU scheduling or priority boost | | **Laptop** | USB selective suspend, **disables** HAGS (saves power on hybrid-GPU laptops), Balanced power plan | Never disables hibernation or memory paging | | **Extreme** | Everything in Gaming + hibernation removed; `DisablePagingExecutive` only if RAM ≥ 16GB; Superfetch disabled only if system drive is confirmed SSD | Desktop only | | **Godlike** | Everything in Extreme + Windows Search indexing disabled + Xbox services disabled. **Requires typing `CONFIRM`** because it trades away Start-menu/file search speed | Desktop enthusiast machines only | | **Server** | Disables Search indexing and Xbox services, removes hibernation, favors background-service CPU priority over foreground apps (opposite of Gaming) | No GPU/gaming tweaks | | **Streaming** | Gaming-profile tweaks + `SystemResponsiveness` lowered so capture/encoding software isn't CPU-starved by the foreground game | - | | **Debloat** | Telemetry service + policy + CEIP **scheduled tasks** off, consumer-feature and lock-screen ads off, Copilot and Recall off, Cortana off, Bing/web suggestions in Start off, Widgets feed off, activity history + advertising ID + feedback prompts + app-launch tracking + sync-provider notifications off, Delivery Optimization P2P off | Uninstalls nothing - no Appx or app removal, unlike most debloat scripts | Full tweak definitions live in `scripts/UWO.psm1` under `Invoke-Tweak` and the profile catalog, which is the **single source of truth** for what each profile does: the profile scripts read their tweak list from it via `Get-ProfileTweak` instead of keeping their own copy, so the table above, `Verify-System.ps1`, and what actually runs can no longer drift apart. Read them before running anything you don't understand. For the `Extreme` and `Godlike` profiles, `DisablePagingExecutive` and `DisableSysMain` are listed in the catalog so that `Verify-System.ps1` can verify them, but the profile scripts strip them from the list they run and re-append them at runtime, gated on RAM >= 16GB and SSD detection respectively — so if your hardware doesn't meet the gate, those tweaks are skipped during the run (and `Verify-System.ps1` will then correctly report them as "Not Applied"). --- ## Utilities - **Compatibility-Check.ps1** — real PASS/FAIL checks (admin rights, OS build, PowerShell version, RAM, disk space, System Restore availability) - **Hardware-Detection.ps1** — real CPU/GPU/RAM/disk/motherboard info via CIM - **Performance-Monitor.ps1** — saves a labeled, real snapshot (CPU load, RAM, disk free, top processes) - **Compare-Results.ps1** — diffs two real snapshots you choose; refuses to run with fewer than 2 snapshots - **Cleanup-System.ps1** — clears temp/cache/Recycle Bin and reports the actual GB freed (measured, not estimated) - **Advanced-Modules.ps1** — runs 8 independent tweaks and reports a real success/fail count - **Verify-System.ps1** — checks current registry/service state against what a chosen profile should have applied - **System-Rollback.ps1** — creates a real Windows System Restore point, or opens System Restore - **Undo-All-Changes.ps1** — reads every backup file this toolkit has written and restores every tracked registry value, service, and hibernation setting to its original state - **Cleanup-Backups.ps1** (menu `P`) — prunes old backup JSON files that would otherwise accumulate forever. Conservative by design: a file is deleted only if it is **both** outside the newest 20 files **and** older than 30 days, and backups that have not been undone yet are never touched unless you pass `-IncludePending`. Use `-WhatIf` to preview, `-KeepCount`/`-MaxAgeDays` to change the thresholds; everything pruned is logged --- ## What's new in v6.5.0 The Debloat profile grew from 10 tweaks to 16, borrowing the settings Sophia Script and winutil apply as policy rather than the consumer toggles this toolkit already had. - Consumer-feature ads and lock-screen "spotlight" ads off - Telemetry policy (`AllowTelemetry`) alongside the existing DiagTrack service change - Cortana off - Delivery Optimization peer-to-peer upload off (uploading updates to strangers) - File Explorer sync-provider notifications off Every one is a single documented registry value, so it is backed up and restored exactly like the rest — the catalogue is now **37 tweaks across 9 profiles**, and the catalog test still enforces that each one is both implemented and verifiable. ## What's new in v6.3.0 A feature release that closes the biggest gap against other Windows debloaters while keeping this toolkit's one hard promise: **everything is reversible.** - **Scheduled tasks are now first-class.** Telemetry and CEIP jobs live in Task Scheduler, not in a service or a registry value, so no previous version could touch them. New `Set-ScheduledTaskStateSafe` / `Restore-ScheduledTaskBackupRecord` disable a task, record its previous state, and put it back on undo - a new `ScheduledTask` backup record type alongside Registry, Service, Hibernation and PowerPlan. - **New `Debloat` profile** (launcher option `B`): disables the ten canonical telemetry tasks, plus Copilot, Recall, Bing/web search suggestions in Start, the Widgets feed, activity history, the advertising ID, feedback prompts and app-launch tracking. - **No app removal, by design.** The well-known debloaters delete Appx packages and warn that "not every feature removed can be easily restored". This one changes state that can be restored, and says so. ## What's new in v6.2.0 A correctness-and-polish release driven by an independent code audit. The undo guarantee now holds for **services, power plans and hibernation**, not just registry values. - **Undo now restores services and power plans after a re-run.** Previously, re-running a profile recorded the already-tweaked service start mode / power plan as the "original", and those record types were not de-duplicated — so "Undo All" could leave the machine on the tweaked state. `Set-ServiceStateSafe` and the `PowerPlan*` tweaks are now idempotent, and `Select-BackupRecordsToRestore` de-duplicates services (per service), power plans and hibernation as well as registry values, keeping the earliest recorded original. - **`Verify-System.ps1` now reports `DisableNetworkThrottling` correctly.** The value `0xffffffff` reads back as `-1`; the verifier now uses the same normalising comparison as the write path (`Test-RegistryValueMatch`). - **Service backups are written only after the change succeeds**, matching the registry path. - **Hibernation is state-aware.** If hibernation is already off, nothing is changed and nothing is recorded; undo restores the state that was actually captured. - **`EnableUSBSelectiveSuspend` now does what its name says.** The old version wrote `CsEnabled` (the Connected/Modern Standby flag). It now sets the real per-scheme USB selective-suspend setting for the active power plan, and is verified against the active scheme. - **Importing the module no longer creates folders.** Log/backup/snapshot directories are created lazily on first write, so a read-only utility or a `-WhatIf` preview leaves no trace. - **`VisualEffectsBalanced`** now writes `0` ("Let Windows choose" — the actual balanced default) instead of `3` ("Custom"). - **`Compare-Results.ps1`** validates your snapshot selection instead of silently comparing blanks. - **Launcher renamed** to `00_Ultimate_Master.bat` (no version in the filename). See [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) for the full history. --- ## Permanent / irreversible debloat (cannot be undone) Everything else in this toolkit is reversible by design. This is the one part that is not, and it is kept deliberately separate. `scripts\Permanent-Debloat.ps1` (launcher option `X`) runs debloat actions that **cannot be undone by this toolkit**: | Operation | What it does | Why it cannot be undone | |---|---|---| | Remove consumer Appx packages | Uninstalls a fixed list of built-in apps, installed and provisioned | Removed packages must be reinstalled from the Microsoft Store | | Uninstall the OneDrive client | Runs the OneDrive uninstaller | OneDrive must be reinstalled from Microsoft | | Compact the component store | `DISM /StartComponentCleanup /ResetBase` | Updates already installed can no longer be uninstalled | How it is kept honest: - **No backup record is written.** These are not tweaks - they never enter the catalog and never appear in any profile. - **`Undo-All-Changes.ps1` does not touch them**, and prints a warning at the end telling you how many permanent changes are recorded. - **Typing `I UNDERSTAND` is required** before anything runs. - Every action is appended to an append-only ledger at `%USERPROFILE%\OptimizationLogs\PermanentChanges.log`, so you can see what was done even though you cannot put it back. - **`Cleanup-System.ps1` (menu `C`) is recorded the same way.** Deleting temp files and emptying the Recycle Bin cannot be undone, so it warns first and writes every target it clears to the same ledger. - CI enforces that no irreversible operation is ever part of a normal profile, and that the cleanup script keeps writing to the ledger. ## Safety notes - The previous state of every registry value, Windows service, hibernation setting, and power plan is captured **before** the change and written to a per-run JSON backup file **as soon as the change actually succeeds**. A failed change writes no backup record, so `Undo-All-Changes.ps1` can never try to "restore" something that was never applied. (Services originally in `Boot`/`System` start modes — kernel drivers — cannot be restored via `Set-Service` and are logged with a clear warning instead.) - **Re-running a profile is a no-op for anything that already matches.** Nothing is written and no backup record is added, so a second run cannot record an already-tweaked value as your "original" one. As a second line of defence, undo de-duplicates records across all backup files by their logical target and always restores the *earliest* recorded original. - **Registry keys created by the toolkit are removed again on undo** — but only when the value did not exist beforehand, the key was created by this toolkit, and the key is still empty. A key that something else has since written to is left in place. - `Undo-All-Changes.ps1` supports `-WhatIf` to preview what it would restore without changing anything, and tolerates corrupted/empty backup files without aborting the whole undo run. - Power plans are restored locale-independently: the plan GUID is extracted and stored when it is captured, rather than re-parsed from localized `powercfg` output at undo time. - Backup files are never deleted automatically. Pruning only happens when you run `Cleanup-Backups.ps1` (menu `P`), and by default it leaves every backup that has not been undone yet alone. - The `Godlike` profile requires typed confirmation because it disables Windows Search indexing, which has a real usability cost. - The optional dependency downloader (menu `D`) only opens official vendor download pages — it does not silently run anything, and does not claim to verify file signatures for you. - **No network, no telemetry, no credential access, no persistence.** The toolkit contains no downloader, no `Invoke-Expression`, no scheduled tasks and no security-product changes. --- ## Development The shared engine is the `UWO` module (`scripts/UWO.psm1` + `scripts/UWO.psd1`). Scripts consume it with `Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'UWO.psd1')`; `scripts/Common-Functions.ps1` remains only as a shim that imports the module and re-publishes the old `$Global:*` catalog variables, so anything that still dot-sources it keeps working. Tests live in `tests/` and run with Pester 5: ```powershell Install-Module Pester -RequiredVersion 5.7.1 -Scope CurrentUser Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests ``` The registry tests only ever touch `HKCU:\Software\UWO-Test` and are skipped on non-Windows hosts; logs/backups are redirected to a temporary directory via the `UWO_LOG_ROOT` environment variable, so running the suite never touches `%USERPROFILE%\OptimizationLogs`. Lint with `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path . -Recurse -Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`; both run automatically on `windows-latest` under Windows PowerShell 5.1 in CI (see [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml)). --- ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## License MIT. Accent Oracle

It listens to four seconds of speech and guesses which accent it heard —
on device, with a band on how sure it is.

Open the app →  ·  Landing page  ·  User guide  ·  The twelve  ·  The rule  ·  Support

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

the oracle, having just heard four seconds of someone reading a sentence

--- One HTML file, no build step, no dependencies, no model download — which is also why it works with the network switched off. The page carries a `Content-Security-Policy` with `connect-src 'none'`, so a fetch or a WebSocket is refused by the browser itself rather than by a promise in the footer. The recording is decoded into eight numbers and dropped. A service worker makes the second visit work with the radio off, and the app installs to a home screen like any other app. ## What it does It measures, then compares. Pitch is found by autocorrelation, the first two formants by cepstral smoothing of the spectrum, syllable onsets by positive spectral flux, and the vowel space by the spread of formant values in Bark. Those eight numbers are scored against twelve accent profiles, and the result carries a band rather than a percentage of certainty. | | | |---|---| | accents in the set | **12** | | measurements per sample | **8** | | runtime dependencies | **0** | | network requests at runtime | **0** | | engine tests | **23** | The result screen names an accent and the region that accent is usually heard in, shows the runners-up, and hands you a card: where it is heard, what it is commonly confused with, and one thing worth knowing. There is a challenge mode where the room records a round, the oracle guesses out loud, and the room settles the score. ### The four bands The band is the most important thing on the screen, and two of the four are the app declining to answer. | Band | Meaning | |---|---| | **clear enough** | one profile fits noticeably better than the next — the best case this app offers | | **narrow-ish** | two profiles are close; the winner is a coin that landed your way | | **too close to call** | the top profiles are effectively tied, and it says so instead of picking | | **wide open** | nothing in the set fits this sample well | ### The honest caveat The eight measurements are real. The **profiles they are compared against are hand-set starting values**, not values measured from a labelled corpus — they are ordered the way the literature would lead you to expect, but they are not measurements, and the app says so on screen. [`ACCENTS.md`](ACCENTS.md) has the twelve cards and the exact procedure for replacing the priors with real centroids from Common Voice or VoxCommunis. Until that pass happens, this is a game with a real microphone and honest measurements behind it. That is what the [spec](SPEC.md) asked for. ## The rule The idea this was built from said it in one line, and it is the first requirement rather than a footnote: > Frame it as a fun game, never as a judgment about a person. So the app names an accent, never a nationality; it reports on the speech in that one sample, never on you; and it says which of those it is not doing, on the result screen, every time. A wrong guess has to be cheap and funny, which is a design constraint on the result screen rather than a disclaimer in a footer. ## Run it ```bash node test/engine.test.js # 23 passing, 0 failing python3 -m http.server 8000 # then open http://localhost:8000/docs/play/ ``` Every feature, step by step, is in **[USER-GUIDE.md](USER-GUIDE.md)** — recording, clips, reading the band, challenge mode, installing, microphone troubleshooting, and the release checklist. The app is a single file, so `docs/play/index.html` also opens directly from disk. A microphone needs a secure context, so `http://localhost` works and `file://` may not — the clip button covers that case, and it decodes the file in the page like everything else. ## Platforms Windows, Linux and Android. There is no macOS or iOS build — the app is a web page, and the same page is the product on all three. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page docs/play/index.html the app — engine, interface, cards, support panel docs/play/sw.js the offline shell; bump CACHE on every release docs/play/manifest.webmanifest installable, with the icons beside it docs/play/icon.svg the mark docs/assets/ screenshots, generated badges, the UPI QR, the portrait USER-GUIDE.md every feature, step by step, and the release checklist ACCENTS.md the closed set of twelve, the card copy, the calibration path SPEC.md where this came from and what it must not do test/engine.test.js the engine, lifted out of the page and run in Node tools/ the estate's presentation checks ``` ## Built with Vanilla JavaScript and the Web Audio API. No framework, no bundler, no package manager, no build step — `docs/play/index.html` is the source and the artefact. The engine does its own maths: a radix-2 FFT, cepstral liftering for the formants, normalised autocorrelation for the pitch, spectral flux for syllable onsets, and a Bark-scale vowel space. The tests lift that block out of the HTML and run it in Node against synthesised voices with known pitch, formants and syllable gating. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # AI Bridge [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-3f7a52?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Your browser's AI, inside VS Code. No API key, no second subscription.**
--- You are already signed in to ChatGPT in Chrome. You already pay for it. AI Bridge attaches to that tab over the Chrome DevTools Protocol and drives it from inside VS Code — reading answers, writing edits into your workspace, and keeping a project state that survives a new chat. By default it never launches a browser — it uses the tab you opened. It never asks for an API key. If you would rather it started one for you, `browser.mode: "launch"` does that, with a profile of its own so your normal browsing is untouched.

Chat panel — streamed answers, and edits you accept hunk by hunk

## Why it exists - **No API keys.** Nothing to paste, nothing to leak, nothing to bill. - **Your subscription, your session.** It drives the page you already use, with the model you already chose. - **Edits you can refuse.** Every change arrives as a proposal with a diff; untick what you don't want, accept the rest in one undo step. - **It survives the limit.** When ChatGPT says *"you've reached your limit"*, the context moves to Claude or Gemini and the conversation continues.

Providers — health dots, the model list, and any provider you configure yourself
Router — priority, cooldowns, failover, and a preview of the chain it would try

## Install **From a build:** download the `.vsix` from [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/ai-bridge/releases), then: ```bash code --install-extension ai-bridge-0.20.4.vsix ``` **VSCodium, and any other VS Code fork:** the same `.vsix` installs. Once published, it is also on **Open VSX** — `codium --install-extension ai-bridge`. One difference is worth knowing: VSCodium ships no Copilot, so the chat model picker stays empty there. That is not a fault — use the panel at `Ctrl+Alt+A`, which is the primary interface anyway. And with no Copilot, a **local model** becomes the natural choice: `AI Bridge: Add Local Model` finds Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM on this machine and registers it in one click — no browser, no key, nothing leaving the machine. **From source:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/ai-bridge.git cd ai-bridge npm install && npm run build && npm run package code --install-extension ai-bridge-0.20.4.vsix ```
## Five steps to first use 1. **Open your browser with the debug port on** — close it first, then: `chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222` 2. **Sign in to ChatGPT** in that window, normally. 3. **Attach:** `Ctrl+Shift+P` → *AI Bridge: Attach Browser*. 4. **Check the dot:** `Ctrl+Shift+P` → *AI Bridge: Adapter Health*. Green means the selectors matched. 5. **Ask something:** `Ctrl+Alt+A` opens the chat panel. Try *"rename oldName to normalise in src/format.ts"*. If a dot is red, the site changed its page — press **AI Bridge: Export Breakage Report** and send that file. It contains no conversation text.
## How it works ``` ┌──────────────┐ loopback WS ┌──────────────┐ CDP ┌────────────────────┐ │ VS Code │◄────────────────►│ Bridge │◄────────►│ your browser tab │ │ extension │ 127.0.0.1 only │ (Node) │ 9222 │ ChatGPT / Claude │ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └────────────────────┘ │ │ edits, state, adapters, router, settings, panel RAM watchdog ``` - The **bridge** is a separate Node process on loopback. It holds the CDP connection and the adapters. - The **extension** owns everything that touches your workspace: files, diffs, state, settings. - **Adapters** are selector maps — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or one you add in settings. - A **router** picks the provider, honours cooldowns, and fails over carrying only what changed.
## What it does about tokens Measured, not claimed (`docs/compression-bench.md`): | input | tokens | saved | |---|---|---| | polite one-liner | 34 → 21 | ⇣38% | | terse one-liner | 8 → 8 | ⇣0% | | verbose spec paragraph | 113 → 80 | ⇣29% | | pasted stack trace | 83 → 71 | ⇣14% | | code request | 68 → 59 | ⇣13% | | boot prompt | 975 → 974 | ⇣0% | | repo bundle | 588 → 370 | ⇣37% | Compression helps on verbose prose and repo context, and does nothing for terse prompts. The bigger saving is **not sending context that isn't needed**: repo context is attached only when the question names a file, a symbol or a code term, which avoids a 500–900 token bundle on chatty prompts.
## Features | | | |---|---| | **Three providers, plus your own** | ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini out of the box; any other web chat via a selector map in settings | | **Streaming panel** | Virtual-scrolled, first token measured (~471 ms in testing) | | **Reviewable edits** | Diff card with **per-hunk** accept/reject, one `WorkspaceEdit`, sha-verified, drift-refusing | | **Project state** | Gzipped, encrypted, snapshotted; a ≤4k boot prompt restores DOING/TODO in a fresh chat | | **Locked decisions** | "Never do X" is held even in auto mode, with an explicit override flow | | **Compression** | T0 always (protected spans, glossary), T1 opt-in local model, T2 opt-in provider-side | | **Session rotation** | On a usage limit: boot → new page → inject, with an editable preview first | | **Router** | Priority, per-provider cooldowns, exponential backoff + jitter, pre-warm at 80%, free-model preference | | **RAM watchdog** | 3 s poll, 80% evict + GC, 100% block; low-end mode for 8 GB machines | | **Settings** | Six tabs, every field, inline validation, a live preview on each tab | | **Keyboard first** | `Ctrl+Alt+A` chat · `Ctrl+Alt+,` settings · `Ctrl+Alt+R` rotate · `Ctrl+Alt+S` state · `Ctrl+Alt+C` compression |
## Free-tier API endpoints Besides the three web chats, the bridge can talk to any endpoint that speaks `POST {baseUrl}/chat/completions` — OpenRouter's free pool, Groq, Google AI Studio, Cerebras, GitHub Models, or a local Ollama. These need no browser and no selectors, so they cannot break when a site changes its page. - **Model discovery** from `GET {baseUrl}/models`, or a pinned list when the catalogue is hundreds of models long. - **Structural tool calls** where the endpoint supports them; the prompt protocol where it does not, scrubbed out of the answer either way. - **Real usage numbers.** These endpoints report prompt and completion tokens, so a remaining count is measured rather than guessed. - **Keys stay off disk.** They live in memory for the life of the bridge, or in `AI_BRIDGE_API_KEY_`. Configured over the control plane (`ctl.api.providers.set`); the batch records, including what was taken from where, are in [`docs/batch8/`](docs/batch8/). Two suites cover it: `npm run test:api` (32 checks) and `npm run test:tools` (34 checks). ## What is actually proven This is an experimental project and it would be dishonest to imply otherwise. **Proven** — 942 checks across 35 suites, run on every push: - The bridge, the CDP controller, the watchdog, the router and the state layer. - All three adapters and a fourth custom one, driven end to end **against fixtures**. - Per-hunk edits, the locked-decision guard, drift refusal, one-undo applies. - The boot prompt staying under 4k with every delta present across five failovers. - A deliberately broken fixture failing the contract suite — the suite detects breakage. - The breakage report containing no chat content, checked against known fragments. **Not proven** — and you should know before relying on it: - **Live selectors.** No adapter has run against the real ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Fixtures only. - **The free-tier line** — API transport, tool layer, the fast-path cascade, per-feature routing, the Copilot provider: 196 checks across 9 suites. - **The one-hour memory soak.** Three minutes passes flat; an hour needs real hardware. - **T1 and T2 quality.** Built, guarded, tested for safety — never run against a real model. - **Windows.** The code paths exist; only Linux has been exercised.

Nothing leaves your machine except the prompts you send to the site you are signed in to. - State is encrypted at rest by default and redacted before it is written. - The breakage report is built from an allow-list: host only (no paths, no conversation ids), selectors tried, and tag/attribute **names**. A guard refuses to write it if any chat text appears.
## Development ```bash npm install npm run build # tsc across shared, bridge, extension npm run test:all # 626 checks, 21 suites npm run test:bench # token-savings report npm run soak # idle memory soak npm run package # bundles and builds the .vsix ``` ## Releasing Releases are automatic and version-gated — pushing code alone publishes nothing. ```bash npm run version:bump patch # or minor / major, or an explicit 1.2.3 git commit -am "release" && git push ``` Every push to `main` publishes **two** things: | release | when | what | |---|---|---| | **Latest build** (pre-release) | every push | a fresh `.vsix` from that commit, replaced each time | | **vX.Y.Z** (latest) | only when the version changes | the tagged, tested release | So there is always a downloadable `.vsix`, and version numbers stay meaningful. `docs/` deploys to GitHub Pages on any change to the landing page. app-builder: # app-builder ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **A shared build kit that turns a static web app into two offline deliverables: a portable Windows EXE and an Android APK.** [![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/landing%20page-open-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-builder/) [![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/) [![Offline](https://img.shields.io/badge/offline-yes-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) [![Type: shared build kit](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-shared%20build%20kit-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-builder/) [![Tech: Python + Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/tech-Python%20%2B%20Kotlin-3572A5?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **Landing page:**  ·  **All projects:** A small, reusable kit that turns a **static web app** into two double-clickable, offline deliverables: * a **single-file portable Windows EXE** (`-portable.exe`) — a tiny Python launcher bundled with the app that serves it locally and opens the browser; and * an **Android APK** (`.apk`) — a dependency-free WebView wrapper of the same app. Both work fully offline. A consuming app repo adds **one workflow file** and gets freshly-built artifacts attached to a GitHub Release on every push. --- ## What's in here ``` exe/ launcher.py # serves the bundled app/ on 127.0.0.1 and opens a browser build.py # PyInstaller --onefile build -> dist/-portable.exe requirements.txt # pyinstaller apk/ settings.gradle.kts build.gradle.kts # AGP 8.x + Kotlin plugin (apply false) gradle.properties app/ build.gradle.kts # compileSdk 34 / minSdk 24 / targetSdk 34, signed release src/main/AndroidManifest.xml src/main/java/com/drsamonline/appbuilder/MainActivity.kt src/main/res/values/strings.xml # app label (placeholder, replaced by the workflow) src/main/assets/www/ # <-- the app's HTML is copied here by the workflow keystore/ debug.keystore # shared debug-grade signing key (see below) tools/ verify_exe.py # inspects the built EXE: valid PE, executable, size budget, imports examples/ build-apps.yml # the workflow a consuming repo drops into .github/workflows/ README.md ``` --- ## How a repo uses the kit Add `examples/build-apps.yml` as `.github/workflows/build-apps.yml` in your app repo and set the three values under `with:` to match your layout: ```yaml jobs: app: uses: drsamonline/app-builder/.github/workflows/build.yml@main with: app_name: my-app # -> my-app-portable.exe and my-app.apk app_src: docs/play # folder containing your index.html (+ any assets) deploy_path: docs # folder to publish to Pages ("" = do not deploy) ``` **Call the workflow; do not copy it.** The build, release and deploy live in the reusable workflow, so a fix there reaches every app at once. An earlier hand-copied version of this file drifted and kept `if: always()` on the release job, which *deleted* the published release before recreating it. The reusable workflow runs, on every push to `main` (and on manual `workflow_dispatch`): 1. **`exe` job** (`windows-latest`) checks out your repo **and** this kit, copies `app_src/` into `exe/app/`, runs `python exe/build.py`, and uploads `-portable.exe`. 2. **`apk` job** (`ubuntu-latest`) checks out both, installs the Android SDK packages, copies `app_src/` into `apk/app/src/main/assets/www/`, and runs `gradle assembleRelease` to produce a signed `.apk`. 3. **`version` job** consumes any `changes/` files and bumps `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md`. 4. **`release` job** publishes both artefacts on a single fixed-tag release (`app-latest`) — created **only if it is missing**, then uploaded with `--clobber`. It never deletes the release first, so a failed build leaves the previous one intact. 5. **`pages` job** deploys `deploy_path` after the release lands. A push that touches only root docs/meta (`*.md`, `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, …) is skipped entirely by `paths-ignore`, so a docs-only commit does not run the builder. ### Stable download URLs Because the tag is always `app-latest` and is recreated each run, these URLs are permanent: ``` https://github.com///releases/latest/download/-portable.exe https://github.com///releases/latest/download/.apk ``` Link your landing page to those and the download always tracks the latest build. --- ## The EXE launcher `launcher.py`: * picks a free port on `127.0.0.1`, * serves the bundled `app/` folder with `http.server`, * opens the user's default browser at the URL, prints it, and * runs until the console window is closed / `Ctrl+C`. It resolves its bundled data via `sys._MEIPASS` when frozen by PyInstaller, and falls back to the script directory when run as a plain script. `build.py` builds the EXE with `--onefile`, names it `-portable`, and bundles the app folder as `app`. It uses the correct `--add-data` separator for the platform (`;` on Windows, `:` elsewhere). Set `APP_NAME` in the environment before running it. Every build **inspects the EXE before it ships it.** `tools/verify_exe.py` reads the PE and asserts it is a valid PE, an executable, within a size budget, and imports nothing unexpected — then prints the machine, subsystem, size and imports to the build log, so the record shows what actually shipped. `MAX_EXE_MB`, `REQUIRED_IMPORTS` and `FORBIDDEN_IMPORTS` (and `SIGNED_REQUIRED=1`) tune the assertions per app. --- ## The Android APK The `apk/` project is deliberately minimal and dependency-free (platform framework only — **no AndroidX**): * `compileSdk 34`, `minSdk 24`, `targetSdk 34`, AGP 8.x. * `MainActivity` is a full-screen `WebView` with JavaScript and DOM storage enabled, loading `file:///android_asset/www/index.html`. * The hardware back button navigates the WebView history first. * `INTERNET` permission is declared (some wrapped apps fetch remote assets). The app's HTML lives in `app/src/main/assets/www/` — the workflow copies your `docs/play/` folder there before building. The app label comes from `res/values/strings.xml`; the workflow replaces the `APP_NAME_PLACEHOLDER` token with `APP_NAME`. --- ## Signing key (read this) `keystore/debug.keystore` is a **debug-grade** key (alias `androiddebugkey`, store/key password `android`, CN=Android Debug, validity ~10000 days). * Its only purpose is so that **successive builds can be installed over each other** during sideloading/iteration. * It is **NOT** a Play-Store signing key. Do **not** publish to Google Play with it. It is public in this repository, so it provides no security. * To use your own key, add repository **secrets** and pass them through in the `apk` job's environment: | secret | meaning | | --- | --- | | `KEYSTORE_FILE` | path to the keystore file you stage in the job | | `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` | store password | | `KEY_ALIAS` | key alias | | `KEY_PASSWORD` | key password | `app/build.gradle.kts` reads those env vars and falls back to the committed debug key when they are unset. --- ## Caveats * The APK is **debug-signed** (see above) — fine for sideloading, not for Play. * The EXE is unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run ("More info" → "Run anyway"). Code-signing is out of scope for this kit. * Each run costs ~2 GitHub-hosted runner-minutes (Windows + Linux). A cold Android build is the slower half (SDK + Gradle download). ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # Clip Loom ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Clean it before you paste it — with programs you can read.** [![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-clean%20a%20link-b4482f?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=231d16)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=231d16)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-clip-loom?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16&color=b4482f)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/releases/latest) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-4f7a5c?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-b4482f?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [**Open the tool →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/)
![Clip Loom](docs/shot.png) A link with eleven tracking parameters. Text pulled out of a PDF with three spaces between every word. A paragraph going into a field that will not wrap. Clip Loom does those jobs with **programs you can read in full** — twenty lines of Weft-8 assembly each, running on a machine that lives in the page. ## The five programs | Program | What it does | The idea it uses | |---|---|---| | **Strip the query string** | cut a URL at the `?` | compare each byte with `0x3F`, stop when it matches | | **Squeeze runs of spaces** | `a b` → `a b` | remember the *previous* byte in a register and compare | | **Wrap at 40 characters** | insert a newline every 40 | count down in a register and refill it — the same code for any length | | **Strip query and fragment** | cut at `?` and at `#` | two terminators instead of one | | **One line per sentence** | newline after every `.` | one more comparison in the copy loop | Every program reads one byte at a time from the `CLIPBOARD` port, decides, and writes. No regular expressions, no library, nothing you cannot follow with a pencil. ## Built on the Loom This app does not carry its own computer. `docs/play/weft8.js` is the **Weft-8** from [Jacquard (the Loom)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — byte for byte the same engine, the same one its 102 assertions cover. What this repository adds is a host: a clipboard that hands the machine one byte at a time and collects what it writes. That is the whole design. The machine is shared; the job is a peripheral. ## Run it Open `docs/index.html`, or use the [live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/). The Windows EXE and Android APK are on the [rolling release](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/releases/latest). Your text never leaves the tab: the machine reads it in the page, and the clipboard buttons use the browser's own clipboard API with a plain "select and copy" fallback if the browser refuses. ## Test it ``` npm install node test-node.js # 66 assertions — the machine and every program node tests/page-smoke.js # 9 assertions — the page, driven in jsdom ``` The program suite runs **every example each program ships** on the real machine, then the edges: the empty clipboard, text with no `?`, a run of five spaces, and a 120-character paragraph that must wrap into four lines with no character lost. It also checks the programs **bite**: delete the `?` comparison from program 01 and the example that says the query must go starts failing. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | **Clip Loom** (you are here) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. app-encrypted-case-log: # Encrypted Case Log [![Live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/play/) ![Crypto](docs/assets/badge-crypto.svg) ![Offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![Tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![Dependencies](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) [![Licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE) **Per-patient clinical notes, encrypted on the device. Offline. No account, no server.** Everything lives on the device, encrypted at rest with **AES-256-GCM** (Web Crypto), in **IndexedDB**. The page carries `connect-src 'none'`, so an outbound request is impossible even by accident — there is nothing to send your notes to. | | | |---|---| | **Landing page** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/ | | **Live app** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/play/ | | **Demo vault** (sample records, memory only) | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/play/index.html?demo=1 | | **Source** | https://github.com/drsamonline/app-encrypted-case-log | | **Changelog** | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | | **All projects** | https://drsamonline.github.io/ | ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) The landing page embeds the real app in a frame, driven by guided buttons (`#patients`, `#note`, `#search`, `#locked`) rather than four static pictures. Screens of the app itself, at both widths, live in `docs/assets/app-desktop.png` and `docs/assets/app-mobile.png`; both are produced by `scripts/shot.sh app`, the icon set by `scripts/icons.py`, and the badges by `scripts/badges.py`. `docs/play/icon.png` is committed so the release build picks up the real icon rather than a generated monogram — an offline-first app should not fetch an image service to describe itself. Built with Forge, composing five shared kits: `crypto-kit` (AES-GCM, PBKDF2, key wrap), `case-kit` (the record shape), `search-kit` (ranked search), `export-kit` (save a file) and `web-kit` (shell, storage runtime, PWA). The app is English only, deliberately: it is a clinical tool used in one language, and a half-translated record screen is worse than an English one. ## Run it `docs/play/index.html` is the whole app. No build step, no install. ``` node tests/self-tests.js # 21 tests, no browser needed python3 scripts/icons.py # the PWA icon set, rendered locally ``` Append `?demo=1` to open the sample vault — real crypto over real records, but held in memory, so nothing is written to your device. ## The vault, and what it means for you - You set a **passphrase**. A key-encryption key is derived from it with **PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 600,000 iterations, a random 16-byte salt**. - A random **data-encryption key (DEK)** encrypts the records. The passphrase only **wraps** the DEK — so changing the passphrase never re-encrypts a record. - A **verifier** (a known constant encrypted with the DEK) makes a wrong passphrase fail cleanly instead of silently producing garbage. - A **24-word recovery code** wraps the same DEK, so a forgotten passphrase is survivable. It is shown **once**; rotating it invalidates the old one immediately. > **Without the passphrase or the recovery code, the data is unrecoverable.** There is no > server to reset it, and that is the point — not an oversight. A header written with fewer KDF rounds than the current target is re-wrapped at the higher count on its next unlock. That is the only place the passphrase exists, so it is the only place an upgrade can happen. ## The records One record per blob, a **fresh 96-bit IV every time**, and the record id as **AAD**, so a record cannot be swapped or replayed. The self-tests prove that: a swapped record fails to decrypt, no IV is ever reused, and the ciphertext never contains the plaintext. A patient carries a **short label — initials or a code, not a full name**. The device may be shared, and the label is the field most likely to be seen. Each note carries a **severity from 1 to 4**, and the patient view draws that as a line — inline SVG, no chart library. Deleting is a **tombstone** you can undo until you lock; purging happens on lock. Every save keeps up to **five previous versions**, as the old ciphertexts themselves, so a restore is a decrypt and never a rewrite of history. ## Search, and its ceiling **You cannot search ciphertext.** On unlock the app decrypts every record into memory and builds a transient index with `search-kit`; the index is thrown away on lock. A plaintext index on disk would leak exactly what we encrypted, so there isn't one. The index is built **once per data change**, not once per keystroke, and unlock decrypts in **batches of 250** so a large vault paints early instead of blocking on one pass. Filters for **tag** and a **date range** sit beside the search box. **The honest ceiling is about 50,000 records** — the decrypt-everything-on-unlock step is linear, and past that the unlock becomes slow on a phone. It is not unlimited, and the app does not pretend it is. ## Export and import - **`.ecl`** — a single encrypted archive (the vault header and every encrypted record). It is already encrypted, so it is safe to keep anywhere. The app prints a **SHA-256 of the archive** when it writes one, so a restore can be checked. - **Plaintext CSV** — behind a clear warning, for when you must hand something over, and **CSV import** with a column preview for the reverse direction. - **Import merges by default**: a dry-run count of *new / newer / identical* records, then a merge keyed on record id and timestamp. Replacing the vault is a second, explicit question. - **Print** with a print stylesheet hands a single record over on paper — offline, no PDF library. - A double-clicked `.ecl` opens the app through `file_handlers`, still with no network. The round-trip is tested: **export → wipe → import → identical data.** ## Safety Never persists the DEK; it is held in memory only and cleared on lock. **Auto-locks after 5 minutes idle** (configurable) and on demand, and can lock the moment the tab is hidden. Requests `navigator.storage.persist()` so the database is not evicted, and shows the quota it is using. Optional, and off by default: **destroy the vault after N wrong passphrases**, for a device you expect to be taken. A **decoy vault** is also available — a second passphrase opening a separate, empty vault with its own key. Nothing marks it as a decoy, because a marker would defeat it. A **vault health** panel decrypts every record and reports anything that fails, and the self-tests can be run from the page. The service worker serves the **HTML network-first** (the cache is only the offline fallback) and asks the registration to update on every load, so a shipped release is not hidden behind a stale cache. The footer prints a **version and build stamp**, so "am I on the new one?" is answerable from the page itself. ## Keyboard and type `N` new patient · `/` search · `Ctrl`+`S` save · `L` lock · `S` settings · `Esc` close · `?` the list. # app-endpoints

<!-- shot:start -->

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-endpoints/)
[![download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-endpoints?label=download&color=blue)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-endpoints/releases/latest)
[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-101%20assertions-3f7a52)](test-node.js)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-informational)](LICENSE)

**Find the right free API for a job — offline, with the CORS and auth answers a directory usually
makes you guess** — no accounts, no telemetry, no network at runtime.

Open it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-endpoints/play/> · About it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-endpoints/>

## Why it exists

Every API directory is a list you read. But three questions decide whether an API is usable before
you write a line — **does it need a key**, **can a browser call it at all** (CORS), and **is it
HTTPS** — and in most lists those are footnotes. Here they are filters. The filter is the product.

The idea surfaced three times independently (the open-data survey, the learn-to-code survey, the
productivity-tools survey) before it was built, which is the strongest signal the queue has. It is
**master list #134**; the first commit's message cites #154, which is wrong — this app was already on
the list with a spec, and the backlog's P5 line for it was a duplicate.

**What this is not.** The spec asked for a rate limit on every entry. The source does not state rate
limits, so none are recorded — the app says "listed as free in public-apis" and links out rather than
inventing one. There is no "try it" call, and no URL was checked for liveness: this is a directory,
not a monitor. `QUEUE/app-endpoints.md` in forge records each of these as not built.

## What is here

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/play/endpoints.js` | the engine — `validate`, `search`, `stats`, `savePins`, `loadPins`; pure, no DOM, no request |
| `docs/play/app.js` | the UI — wires inputs to the engine and nothing else |
| `docs/play/data.js` | the bundled directory, **generated** from `data/apis.json` by `tools/build-data.py` |
| `data/apis.json` | the record: 2,214 entries plus the source, licence and fetch date in `meta` |
| `data/SOURCE.md` | where the data came from, its licence, and every curation step with its count |
| `docs/play/search-kit.js`, `export-kit.js` | the kits, copied in, so it runs from `file://` |

## The dataset

2,214 public APIs from the **public-apis** README table — **MIT**, fetched **2026-11-10**.
1,103 need no key; 943 allow CORS; 51 categories. `data/SOURCE.md` records the source, the licence,
the fetch date and every change made to the table, with counts. No free-tier terms are recorded,
because the source does not state them — the app links out and says so rather than inventing them.

`docs/play/data.js` and `data/apis.json` are checked to agree entry for entry by the test suite, so
the bundle cannot drift from the record it claims to be.

## What it does when things go wrong

- **Bad input** — an unknown `auth`, `cors`, `https` or category is refused with the vocabulary it
  accepts, and no result set is produced, so the screen keeps its previous list. A search that
  matches nothing names the filters that emptied it.
- **No network** — nothing changes: the directory is in the page and there is no request to fail.
- **Storage full or unavailable** — a pin that cannot be written is reported as **not kept**, with
  the reason, and still works for the session.
- **Corrupt saved state** — reported as corrupt with an excerpt and a reset; never rendered as
  "you have no pins".

## Test it

```sh
node test-node.js      # 101 assertions, no dependencies, no browser
```

The suite is mutation-tested: removing the auth filter turns 6 red, reporting a corrupt save as
empty turns 3 red, reporting a full disk as saved turns 1 red, and swallowing a bad filter turns 7
red.

# Image Toolkit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**Resize, compress, convert, crop and strip the GPS out of a photo — on your device, with nothing uploaded.** **[Open the app →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-image-toolkit/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-image-toolkit/) · [The rule](#what-it-refuses-to-do) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) Every other "compress my image" page uploads the photo first. This one cannot: there is no server, no account and no network request. The file is read into memory, processed by the code in this repository, and written back out. No build step, no runtime dependency — what is in `docs/play/` is what runs. It installs as an app, it speaks English, Hindi and Gujarati, and `python3 scripts/bundle.py` folds the whole thing into one HTML file that opens from a USB stick. ![The app, after the sample photo has been through it](docs/assets/app-desktop.png) ## What it does | | | |---|---| | **Resize** | contain inside a box, aspect kept, never upscaled, never rounded to zero | | **Crop and turn** | square, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, 9:16; 90°/180°; mirror — and the EXIF orientation is read before the strip, so a portrait photo is not written out sideways | | **Compress** | the highest quality that still fits a byte budget — a binary search, seven encoder calls at the very worst, drawn as a curve | | **Convert** | JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP in; JPEG, PNG or WebP out — or Auto, which encodes two and keeps the smaller (a source that may carry transparency is compared against WebP alone, because JPEG would flatten it) | | **Strip** | EXIF, XMP, IPTC, JPEG comments; PNG `eXIf`/`tEXt`/`iTXt`/`zTXt` — the colour profile is kept unless you say otherwise, and “every metadata block” takes the maker notes too | | **Check** | the *output* bytes are read back: "checked: nothing left" means the file that will be written really has nothing identifying in it | | **Inspect** | before anything is removed, the queue shows what the file says about itself: camera, model, date, and whether there is a GPS block | | **Batch** | paste a screenshot in, queue as many as you like, give any one of them its own settings, leave with one ZIP, one A4 PDF, or a per-file report saying exactly what was done | The pixels are never touched by the strip: everything from the JPEG scan onwards is kept byte for byte, and the PNG colour and image chunks are copied whole. A first visit has no photo to work on, so the app paints one — a 3200 × 2400 landscape, grained so it compresses like a photograph, with a real EXIF block carrying a real GPS fix (19°04′N 72°52′E). It is generated from code by `docs/play/sample.js`: there is no sample file to fetch and nothing bundled as bytes. The sample goes through exactly the path a dropped photo takes. ## The done-means, as the spec states it > A 4 MB photo is resized and compressed to under 500 KB without any network request. `node test-node.js` proves it in pieces rather than asserting it whole: the budget search is driven by a fake encoder whose output shrinks with quality (the way a real one does), so "4 MB → under 500 KB" is a real assertion about the search; and every file that ships is scanned for an external reference, a `fetch(`, an XHR and a remote `@import`, so "no network request" is a fact about the code. What the test cannot prove is how a real browser's canvas encoder sizes a real photo — that is the browser's answer, and the app reports the size it actually got. On the sample it reports **3.29 MB → 286 KB**, 1600 × 1200, GPS gone, checked. ## What it refuses to do, and does not - No upload, no endpoint, no `fetch`, no XHR — asserted across every shipped file, not promised in prose. - No account, no sign-in, no analytics, no telemetry. - No runtime dependency: `imgtool.js` is one file of plain JavaScript with no imports, and the `deps` badge is counted from the files that ship rather than typed. - No build step, no bundler, no framework. - No silent failure: a file that is not an image is refused with the type it reported; a HEIC is named as something a browser cannot draw, with the way out; unreadable metadata is reported as unreadable; a download that cannot be written says so. - A footer counter watches for any request that leaves this origin and stays at zero. ## Run it ```bash node test-node.js # the proof: 206 assertions, no dependencies python3 -m http.server -d docs 8000 # then open http://localhost:8000/play/ python3 scripts/version.py # one version, in every place it is written python3 scripts/icons.py # the icon set, from assets/icon.svg python3 scripts/badges.py # badges, with the counts computed python3 scripts/bundle.py # the whole app as one HTML file python3 scripts/uitest.py # the app in a headless browser: 30 checks python3 scripts/shot.py --help # screenshots of pages that have settled ``` There is no build step. `docs/play/` is the app. `RELEASING.md` is the six-step release. The rolling release carries four things built from the same commit: the portable EXE, the Android APK, the Linux binary, and `image-toolkit.html` — the whole app as one file, which opens from a USB stick with no server at all. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page — its own design, not the app's docs/play/index.html the app docs/play/app.js the view: queue and per-photo settings, results, preview, chart, ZIP docs/play/imgtool.js the engine — sniff, dimensions, EXIF, orientation, strip, check, fit, budget, ZIP, PDF docs/play/i18n.js English, Hindi and Gujarati, one table docs/play/sample.js the sample photo, painted on a canvas when it is needed docs/play/sw.js the offline worker — network-first HTML, cache bumped per release docs/play/manifest.webmanifest docs/play/icons/ generated from assets/icon.svg docs/play/web-kit.js vendored, unmodified — hashed in NOTICE.md and checked docs/play/export-kit.js vendored, unmodified — hashed in NOTICE.md and checked docs/assets/ screenshots and generated badges assets/icon.svg the one master mark scripts/ version, icons, badges, bundle, shot test-node.js the proof ``` Both surfaces are light by default, follow the system preference on first paint, and carry a toggle that is remembered — under separate keys, so setting one never changes the other. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — free for personal, hobby and educational use; commercial use needs a paid licence. # Jacquard ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **The loom you program — an 8-bit machine you can hold in your head.** [![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-drsamonline.github.io%2Fapp--jacquard-d98324?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-jacquard/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=1a1610)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-jacquard/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=1a1610)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-jacquard?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610&color=d98324)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/releases/latest) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-3f7a52?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](LICENSE) [![Offline](https://img.shields.io/badge/network-none-3f7a52?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](#-what-it-refuses-to-do) [![No runtime dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-d98324?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](package.json) [**Open the loom →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) · [Reference card](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/play/#card) · [What it refuses](#-what-it-refuses-to-do) · [Tests](#-the-proof)
--- Automation usually hides behind coloured boxes. Jacquard puts a **real machine** underneath it: a fictional 8-bit CPU, the **Weft-8**, programmed in assembly, with the clock, the calendar, the clipboard and the accelerometer exposed as **memory-mapped peripherals**. You read a register, you act on it — and you can watch every register, flag and byte change while it runs. The whole app is one page and two files it carries with it. No build step, no framework, no network, no account.
``` IN OFFICE_INSIDE ; read the machine's senses CMP R0, R15 JNZ done ; already at the office -> say nothing IN NEXT_EVENT_MIN CMP R1, R2 ; ten minutes or less? JG done OUT NOTIFY ; leave now done: HLT ```
## Contents | | | |---|---| | [The machine](#-the-machine) | the ISA, the flags, the memory map | | [What a program looks like](#-what-a-program-looks-like) | `leave-now`, end to end | | [The proof](#-the-proof) | 118 assertions: 102 for the engine, 16 that drive the page | | [What it refuses to do](#-what-it-refuses-to-do) | the failure behaviour, asserted not promised | | [Run it](#-run-it) | from a USB stick, a laptop, a phone | | [One honest note on the count](#-one-honest-note-on-the-count) | 27 opcodes, not 28 | ## The machine | | | |---|---| | **Registers** | 16 × 8-bit. `R0` is the accumulator — `LDI`, `LOAD` and `IN` all fill it, `MOV` moves it. | | **Flags** | `Z` zero · `C` carry/borrow · `N` negative · `V` signed overflow | | **Instructions** | fixed **two bytes**, little-endian: the opcode, then the operand | | **Operand** | an 8-bit value, address or port — or two registers packed as `a << 4 \| b` | | **Address space** | 256 bytes: ROM `0x00`–`0x7F`, RAM `0x80`–`0xBF`, peripherals `0xC0`–`0xFF` | | **Stack** | 16 deep, with overflow and underflow reported rather than crashed | Because the operand byte carries both registers, `ADD R12, R5` is literally `04 C5`. A program with a known listing assembles to exactly that listing, byte for byte — which is the first thing the tests assert. The peripherals are host callbacks, so the machine is testable with no browser at all: ``` CLOCK 0xC0 LAT 0xC1 LON 0xC2 OFFICE_INSIDE 0xC3 NEXT_EVENT_MIN 0xC4 NOTIFY 0xC5 CLIPBOARD 0xC6 ACCEL 0xC7 RNG 0xC8 AUDIO 0xC9 HALT 0xCA ``` ## What a program looks like `leave-now` ships with the app: notify ten minutes before the next calendar event, unless you are already at the office. It exercises a peripheral read, a comparison, a signed branch and an output — and all four of its paths are asserted. ``` IN OFFICE_INSIDE CMP R0, R15 ; R15 is 0 here JNZ done ; already there -> say nothing IN NEXT_EVENT_MIN MOV R1, R0 ; R1 = minutes to the event LDI 10 MOV R2, R0 ; R2 = 10 CMP R1, R2 JG done ; more than 10 minutes -> wait LDI 1 OUT NOTIFY ; leave now done: HLT ``` The page shows you the registers, the four flags, the program bytes, scratch RAM, and a **weave strip** that lights up the instruction the program counter is standing on. ## The proof ``` node test-node.js # 102 assertions, no dependencies — the engine node tests/page-smoke.js # 16 assertions — the page, driven in jsdom ``` The tests run the **real** engine — `docs/play/weft8.js`, the same file the page loads. Nothing is mocked except the peripherals, which are callbacks by design. - the encoding, byte for byte, including `ADD R12,R5` → `04 C5` - **all 27 opcodes** assembling and running in one program - **five hand-checked branch traces**, including signed `JL` at `-1` vs `1` and `JG` at `127` vs `-1`, where the subtract overflows - carry, overflow, zero and negative — from `ADD`, `SUB`, `SHL`, `SHR` **and `CMP`'s own borrow** - `CALL`/`RET` nesting, `PUSH`/`POP` order, the 16-deep overflow and the empty-stack `RET` - the peripherals, the ROM write refusal, the step limit, an opcode that does not exist - every refusal in the assembler, with the line number it refuses on - **the page itself**: that it loads the engine, that its script parses, and that every example it offers assembles on the machine it ships And `tests/page-smoke.js` boots the real page in jsdom, clicks the real buttons and reads the real DOM: run, step, reset, the weave strip, the device sliders reaching the machine, and a program that does not assemble being refused instead of run. That test exists because a page bug no engine test could see — `vm.h` where it should have been `vm.peripherals`, which made **Assemble & run** throw — shipped once and was caught only by driving the page. jsdom is a **test-only** dependency; the app has none. **Checked to bite**, not just to pass: rewrite `JL` to test `Z` and two branch traces fail; suppress `CMP`'s borrow and the carry assertion fails. ## What it refuses to do | Situation | What happens | |---|---| | The program does not assemble | it is **never run**; the error names the line and the reason — an undefined label, `R16`, an immediate of 300, a program past the 128-byte ROM | | The program loops forever | it stops at the step limit, and the page says it stopped there | | `RET` with an empty stack | an error, not a crash | | A write into ROM | refused **and reported**, rather than silently doing nothing | | Storage is full or unavailable | Save says so, and tells you to export instead; the editor keeps your program | | No network | nothing changes — there is nothing to fetch. The peripherals are simulated on the device | ## Run it Open `docs/index.html`. That is the whole app; `web-kit.js` and `weft8.js` sit next to it, so it works from `file://` and from GitHub Pages. | Where | How | |---|---| | **Browser** | [drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | | **Windows** | the portable EXE on the [rolling release](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/releases/latest) | | **Android** | the signed APK on the same release | | **Anywhere** | copy the folder; there is nothing to install | ## One honest note on the count The spec asks for "a program using all **28** opcodes" and then names twenty-seven: `LDI MOV LOAD STORE ADD SUB AND OR XOR NOT SHL SHR CMP JMP JZ JNZ JG JL CALL RET PUSH POP IN OUT RAND NOP HLT`. The machine has **27**, and this README says so rather than inventing a twenty-eighth to satisfy a number. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | **the Loom** (you are here) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. # Lantern [![live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live%20demo-open%20the%20library-f0b429?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-lantern/demo/) [![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-lantern/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-lantern/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![audit](https://img.shields.io/badge/audit-in%20the%20suite-f0b429?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](tools/audit.mjs) [![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-f0b429?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](LICENSE) [![dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-5fbf8a?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](package.json) [![network](https://img.shields.io/badge/network-none-5fbf8a?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](#what-it-does-when-things-go-wrong) **A whole library, served over your own Wi-Fi, with no internet at any point.** One device — a laptop, a Raspberry Pi, a phone that runs Node — becomes a local content server. Everyone else on the same network opens the address it prints, in a **plain browser**, and browses, searches and reads a bundled library. Nothing leaves the host unless you export it. *Internet-in-a-Box, as an app.* A school, clinic or village gets a searchable library for the cost of one device and none of the connectivity. **[Open the live demo →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-lantern/demo/)** — the real client and the real search code, running in your browser over a pre-built copy of the starter pack. ![Lantern](docs/icon-512.png) ## Get it **[Download Lantern →](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-lantern/raw/main/dist/lantern.zip)** — one `.zip`, about 55 KB. Inside: `start-lantern` for Windows and for Linux, the server, and a starter library. There is no installer and nothing to fetch afterwards. Every tagged release also carries the same bundle as an attached asset, built by `.github/workflows/release.yml`. ## Run it Three steps, no terminal, no account. 1. **Install Node.js** — open [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org), click the big green **LTS** button, keep clicking **Next** until it finishes. It is the only thing you install. 2. **Start Lantern** — double-click **`start-lantern.bat`** on Windows, or **`start-lantern.sh`** on Linux. A window opens and stays open; that window *is* Lantern running. Leave it open. 3. **Tell people the address** — the window prints one, like `http://192.168.1.24:8080/`. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi types it into their browser. Nothing to install on their side. Nothing is sent anywhere, and no internet is used at any point. ## Add your own books A book, a set of notes, or a whole shelf is one JSON file — a **pack**. There is no editor and no build step; the file is the format. 1. **Copy the sample.** Open [`examples/starter-pack.json`](examples/starter-pack.json) in any text editor and save a copy under a new name. It already has the shape: an `id`, a `title`, and a list of `docs`. 2. **Put your text in it.** Each document is a `path`, a `title`, and the text as simple HTML inside `content`. One entry per chapter. ```json { "id": "my-library", "title": "My Library", "docs": [ { "path": "chapter-1.html", "title": "Chapter 1", "content": "

Chapter 1

The text of the chapter goes here.

" } ] } ``` 3. **Import it.** Open the address the host printed, find the **Packs** card, choose your file and press **Import pack**. It is saved on the host, hashed, and searchable immediately. A second pack later is searchable alongside the first — the search box covers the whole library, not one pack. ## Settings There are two, and neither usually needs changing. | | | |---|---| | **the port** | `node server.js 9000`, or edit `8080` in `start-lantern.bat`. Change it when something else already owns 8080. | | **where the library lives** | the `packs/` folder next to `server.js`, one folder per pack with a manifest. Remove a pack from the Packs card or delete its folder; the index drops it on the next start. | ### If you use a terminal ```bash node server.js # or: node server.js 8080 ``` It prints the addresses to open: ``` Lantern is serving 3 document(s) on port 8080 Open on any device on this Wi-Fi: http://192.168.1.24:8080/ No internet is used at any point. ``` Then, on the host, open the Packs card and import `examples/starter-pack.json`. Anyone on the Wi-Fi can now read and search it. There is nothing to build and no dependencies: the host is one Node file with **no runtime dependencies**, and the client is one page with no build step. Node.js itself is the one thing a person has to install, which is why the two launchers exist — they are for people who do not want to see a terminal. ### Or copy one file `dist/lantern.js` is the **whole app in one file** — server, search index and client, with the page and icon carried inside it. Copy it to a machine with Node and run it; there is no folder to keep beside it. ```bash node lantern.js 8080 ``` ## The three parts | | | |---|---| | **the host** | one Node file, zero dependencies: serves the page, the library and the search index | | **the packs** | content, hashed on import and re-verified on every load | | **the reader** | a plain browser on the same Wi-Fi — no app, no account, no internet | ## What it does - **Host mode.** Import content packs into the host; it serves them on the LAN. - **Client.** Anyone on the network opens the address in a browser — no app, no account, no internet. - **Search.** A full-text index over every document in every pack, built on the host. A document containing the whole query as a **phrase** outranks one that merely contains its words. - **Pack manager.** Each pack's **true byte size**, its document count, and one button to remove it — which removes its documents from search at once. - **Usage stays local.** No analytics, no call home, no third-party request in either the host or the page. ## A pack A pack is one JSON file: ```json { "id": "my-pack", "title": "My Pack", "docs": [ { "path": "notes.html", "title": "Notes", "content": "

Notes

" } ] } ``` On import Lantern writes each document and records its **SHA-256 and byte length** in the pack's own `manifest.json`. It re-checks both every time it loads a pack. ## What it does when things go wrong | Situation | What Lantern does | |---|---| | A document path tries to leave the pack (`../`, an absolute path) | The import is refused and the path is named. A request for such a path is refused with 403. | | A file cannot be written (no space, read-only disk) | The pack is **not** added, the files that did not land are named, and nothing half-written is left behind — a reader cannot tell a missing page from a missing chapter. | | A pack's files no longer match its manifest | The pack is moved to `.quarantine/`, reported in the Packs card, and is neither served nor searchable. | | A bundle that is not JSON, or has no documents | Refused with the reason shown. | | No peers, no internet | Nothing changes: the library still opens on the host, and says how many documents it holds. | ## The proof ```bash node test-node.js # 60 assertions node tools/audit.mjs # every claim in this README, checked against the repo node tools/build.mjs # the demo library, the single file and the bundle ``` The suite runs **over real HTTP against a real host**, because the point of a LAN app is that a browser on the network can read it. It uses Node's `http` rather than `fetch`, so the test never depends on the internet's plumbing. What it covers: the host taking a port and answering; the client page being served; import, and the true byte size read back off disk; a document read over HTTP; phrase-first ranking **ahead of documents that only carry the words**; search after a pack is removed; traversal refusal at request and at import; a bundle that is not JSON; a write that fails with `ENOSPC`; a checksum mismatch being quarantined; **the builds** (a second build changes nothing, the bundle carries every file, and the single file copied alone into an empty folder still serves the page and the icon); and the audit itself. **Checked to bite**, not just to pass: with the phrase bonus removed and both traversal guards removed, 10 assertions fail. ## Layout ``` server.js the host — zero dependencies lib/search.js the index and the ranking, shared by the host and the demo page public/ the client: index.html, lan-kit.js, icon.svg docs/ the landing page, the demo, the icon docs/demo/ the live demo (search + reader, over a built copy of the pack) examples/ a starter pack to import tools/build.mjs demo library → dist/lantern.js → dist/lantern-.zip tools/audit.mjs the claims, checked dist/ the built single file and the portable bundle ``` The demo page loads **the same `lib/search.js`** the host runs. A demo that re-implements the search would drift from the app, and a demo that drifts is a lie with a nice font — so `tools/audit.mjs` fails if the demo ever stops using it. ## Built on - [lan-kit](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit) — vendored as `public/lan-kit.js` for the LAN address helpers (`Lan.hostUrl`), so the page and the host agree on what address a phone should open. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin.
