# OPD Register [![Live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/play/) ![Offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![Tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![Dependencies](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) ![Single file](docs/assets/badge-size.svg) [![Licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE) **The daily OPD register, on one page, at typing speed — offline, no account, no server.** Every day of the month is laid out and ready to type into. Counts, department splits and the daily trend update as you write. Print the register for the file, export a day-wise sheet to Excel, and keep several OPD centres apart in the same app. All of it lives in the browser on your device; the page makes no network request at all. | | | |---|---| | **Landing page** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/ | | **Live app** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/play/ | | **Demo** (sample month, memory only) | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/play/index.html?demo=1 | | **Single HTML file** | [`dist/opd-register.html`](dist/opd-register.html) — ~130 KB, opens from a USB stick | | **Windows EXE / Android APK** | [releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-opd-register/releases/latest) | | **Source** | https://github.com/drsamonline/app-opd-register | | **Changelog** | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) · [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) (a ledger: nothing open) | | **All projects** | https://drsamonline.github.io/ | ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) Screens at both widths: [`docs/assets/app-desktop.png`](docs/assets/app-desktop.png), [`docs/assets/app-mobile.png`](docs/assets/app-mobile.png), [`docs/assets/app-sheet.png`](docs/assets/app-sheet.png) (the phone editor), [`docs/assets/app-history.png`](docs/assets/app-history.png) (history in the editor), [`docs/assets/app-week.png`](docs/assets/app-week.png) (the week as seven columns), [`docs/assets/app-slip.png`](docs/assets/app-slip.png) (the printed visit slip), [`docs/assets/app-followups.png`](docs/assets/app-followups.png) (follow-ups due, by department), [`docs/assets/app-search.png`](docs/assets/app-search.png) (the patient list and its sort), [`docs/assets/app-columns.png`](docs/assets/app-columns.png) (Treatment-before-Diagnosis), [`docs/assets/app-notice.png`](docs/assets/app-notice.png) (the one-time offer), [`docs/assets/app-lock.png`](docs/assets/app-lock.png) (the lock screen), [`docs/assets/app-lock-on.png`](docs/assets/app-lock-on.png) (the lock panel when on), [`docs/assets/app-year.png`](docs/assets/app-year.png) (the year on one screen), [`docs/assets/app-import.png`](docs/assets/app-import.png) (import: merge or replace), [`docs/assets/app-conflict.png`](docs/assets/app-conflict.png) (what differs, and which side wins), [`docs/assets/app-csv.png`](docs/assets/app-csv.png) (the spreadsheet column mapper), [`docs/assets/app-conflicts.png`](docs/assets/app-conflicts.png) (resolving differences one field at a time), [`docs/assets/app-print.png`](docs/assets/app-print.png) (the register as it prints, landscape), [`docs/assets/app-printpreview.png`](docs/assets/app-printpreview.png) (the print preview), [`docs/assets/app-printlist.png`](docs/assets/app-printlist.png) (the patient list on paper), [`docs/assets/app-settings.png`](docs/assets/app-settings.png) (display, lock, storage), [`docs/assets/app-digest.png`](docs/assets/app-digest.png) (the printable digest) and [`docs/assets/app-stats.png`](docs/assets/app-stats.png). Badges are drawn locally by `scripts/badges.py`; the icon set by `scripts/icons.py`. Nothing here is fetched from a badge service, because an offline-first app should not need the internet to describe itself. ## Run it `docs/play/index.html` is the whole app. No build step, no install, no dependencies. ``` node tests/self-tests.js # 141 checks, no browser needed (176 more run in a real browser) python3 scripts/build.py # the single-file build -> dist/opd-register.html python3 scripts/badges.py # the README badges ``` Append `?demo=1` for a generated month — real screens, real arithmetic, held in memory so nothing is written to your device. ## What is in it | View | What it does | |---|---| | **Dashboard** | Five KPIs (total, male, female, new, follow-up) with share-of-total; department bars; sex donut; a bar per day of the month; the last days with data (click to open); **follow-ups due in the next 14 days**, with the mobile number; a short "reading" panel — busiest day, new-vs-follow-up, working days with no entry, female share, gyn share. | | **Register** | The month calendar with day statuses and per-day counts; then one section per day: status dropdown, free-text note, patient count, add-row, print-day and clear-day. **Month or week scope** — the week as seven columns you can compare, with a weekly total — a **row filter** across the visible days (or **inside one day**), and a **range of days** marked in one go. Print prints whatever is on screen: the month, or the week on one A4. On a desktop a sticky, column-aligned grid; on a phone a card per patient and a full-screen editor. | | **Statistics** | Day-wise, month-wise or any date range, with 17 selectable columns (summary, departments, sex-within-department, activity). **Year view** — twelve months, a bar each, the annual totals and a *vs target* column on one screen (it prints too). Print, Excel (.xls), CSV — and a **one-page digest** per month: totals, departments, every day in two columns, every week, a note on entries missing a diagnosis, and a signature line. | | **Patients** | Ranked substring search over every month — name, OPD no., age, department, diagnosis, treatment, address — optionally across all locations, sorted newest / oldest / name / OPD. A hit opens that patient in the editor. | | **About & help** | Storage used, patient and month counts, locations, backup and restore, keyboard reference, the counting rules, privacy and licence. | Open a patient and the editor leads with **their previous visits** — date, department, diagnosis, prescription, how long ago the last one was, and one button to copy that prescription into today's row. **Print slip** turns those visits into half a page for the file or the patient. A row can also repeat the last prescription with one click. Clicking a row number opens it; the OPD field offers the **next number in your series** (offered, never applied) and the department field offers the departments this location actually uses. A patient entered on the wrong day can be **dragged** to the right one by its row number. The register's **column order** is a setting (Treatment first, Name first, or default), the dashboard can draw a **daily target** across the trend, and the reading panel counts rows saved **without a diagnosis** — tap it to see only those days. The patient list exports to CSV as it stands on screen, filtered and sorted. Each patient row also carries a **mobile number** and a **follow-up date** — neither of them makes a row a patient, so a stray date can never inflate a total. Rows duplicate with **Ctrl+D** for the next member of the same family, `01/01/1990` typed into Age becomes 35 years, the department field offers the departments this location actually uses, a **range of days** can be marked holiday in one go (and undone), **one day** can be printed on its own, and ages read the way they are said: `8 mo`, not `0`. Smaller things that earn their place: automatic OPD autofill for returning patients, recent patient chips, undo on delete (row, patient, whole day) and on import, dark mode, a save indicator, a storage-full fallback that prunes empty days rather than losing the entry, install-as-app, and a single-file build for a USB stick. ## The counting rules, written down A report nobody can explain is worse than no report, so the rules are in the app (About & help) and here: - **A row is a patient** when any of OPD no., department, name, age, address, diagnosis or treatment is filled. A half-typed row is still saved — nothing is ever thrown away for being incomplete. - **Gynecology is female-only.** Any department containing *gyn*, *obs* or *obstet* is counted as female whatever the sex field says, and is counted once — not twice. - **Under 15 also counts as Pediatrics.** A child entered under Medicine appears in both the Medicine and Pediatrics buckets. Age accepts `5`, `5y`, `1.5`, `6 mo`, `3 days`. - **Day status is a label, not a filter.** Holiday, non-working and no-activity days are excluded from "per active day" averages, but their patients still count in the totals. ## Keyboard `/` search · `N` new patient · `Ctrl`+`D` duplicate · `T` today · `D` dark mode · `1`–`5` sections · `Alt`+`←`/`→` month · `Enter` next row (adds one on the last row) · `Ctrl`+`Enter` add row · `↑`/`↓` move within a column · `Esc` close. ## Your data **IndexedDB** holds every location and every month, in one record. A v2 register saved in `localStorage` is migrated in on first open, and a browser without IndexedDB falls back to `localStorage` automatically — the engine in use is shown in *About & help → This device*. No account, no analytics, no cookie, no network call. Clearing site data erases it, so **export a backup weekly** — the file carries a SHA-256 of its own contents, so a truncated one is refused instead of half-imported. Importing shows a **preview first**: what the file holds, what merging would add, top up or skip, and **which patients differ** — with the choice of keeping what is here or taking the file's version. **Merge** fills empty fields of a patient who is already here and never overwrites a filled one; **Replace** puts the file in place of everything. Both are undoable, both say what they did, and the patients a merge brought in can be found again from one button in *Patients*. **Import a spreadsheet.** A CSV gets a **column mapper**: the header is guessed, you correct it, rows without a date go to a day you choose, and the same preview follows. Quoted commas, CRLF and `dd/mm/yyyy` all survive. The mapping is **remembered for that shape of file**, so next month's export maps itself. **A backup that is getting old says so** — one notice, once a week, with *Export now* and *Later* (which waits three days). And *Test the round trip* in the same panel exports in memory and reads the file back, so the backup path is proven before you need it. **Differences are not swallowed.** When both sides hold a value for the same patient, the preview lists them and the merge leaves a **queue** in the register — *Resolve 3 differences* — where each field can be taken from the file or left as it is, one at a time. **Exports match the register.** The month CSV follows the column order you set, so an export can be edited in a spreadsheet and merged straight back in. The file format is plain JSON and is compatible with the earlier v2 release. **Optional passphrase lock — offered once, never nagged.** While the lock is on, backups are **signed** with an HMAC key derived from the same passphrase (one PBKDF2 pass, two keys), so a file that has been altered is refused rather than merged. On first open the app asks whether to protect the register, with *Turn it on* and *Not now* side by side. Declining is remembered on that device and changes nothing else; the offer never comes back on its own, and the way to change your mind is always in the ⋯ menu (*Lock & privacy*) and in *About & help → Lock*. Forgot the passphrase? The lock screen offers to start again from a backup file, and says plainly that the encrypted register is deleted if you do. **Auto-lock** closes it again: *About & help → Lock → Lock automatically when idle* (never, 1, 5, 10 or 30 minutes) drops the key from memory and shows the lock screen. **An encrypted backup** can be downloaded from the same panel — it is the ciphertext, so it is useless without the passphrase and can be restored on another machine, plain backup or encrypted. Turning the lock on encrypts the whole register with AES-GCM-256, keyed from your passphrase through PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (310,000 iterations, a random 16-byte salt). The plain copy is deleted only after the encrypted write succeeds, and the key is dropped from memory when you lock. A lost passphrase means a lost register — there is no recovery, by design, because a recovery path would be a second way in. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page — its own design, not the app's docs/play/ the app: index.html, assets/, sw.js, manifest, icons/ docs/play/assets/ app.css · storage.js · lock.js · store.js · register.js · dashboard.js · stats.js · search.js · app.js docs/shot.png the screenshot the pipeline captures docs/assets/ screenshots and the generated badges dist/opd-register.html the single-file build (generated) scripts/build.py inlines css + js into the single file scripts/badges.py draws docs/assets/badge-*.svg scripts/icons.py renders the PWA icon set from icon.svg tests/self-tests.js 141 checks over the real source, no browser ``` The app is six classic scripts in one namespace, not ES modules — so it also runs from `file://` inside a WebView and from the EXE's bundled server without a build step. ## Builds One push to `main` builds the portable EXE and the APK, publishes the rolling `app-latest` release and deploys the demo to Pages, all from the same commit — so the live demo and the released binary can never disagree. The pipeline lives in the public [`app-builder`](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) kit; this repo only calls it. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Attribution - **Licence text** — [PolyForm Project](https://polyformproject.org/licenses/noncommercial/1.0.0), PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. - **Icons** — drawn for this app as inline SVG paths and one `icon.svg`. No icon font, no Font Awesome, no Lucide dependency. - **Fonts** — the system UI font stack. Nothing is downloaded. - **Charts** — a donut of two `` elements and a row of `
` bars. No chart library. - **Patient data in the screenshots** — generated by the app's own `?demo=1` month; the names are invented. - **Clinical conventions** (gynecology as female-only, under-15 as pediatrics) follow how the paper OPD register in an Indian district hospital is tallied; they are documented in the app so a reader can disagree with them explicitly. ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin.
app-organon-reader: # Organon Reader [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **The Organon of Medicine in two editions — Boericke\u2019s sixth (1922) and Dudgeon\u2019s fifth (1849) — searchable, bookmarkable and readable with the network off, and switchable while you read.** No account, no server, no telemetry. Open the page and read. - **App:** - **The text — sixth edition:** *Organon of Medicine*, 6th edition (completed 1842), translated by William Boericke, 1922 — public domain. The reading text comes from the **Médi-T transcription** (homeoint.org) of that translation; it is corroborated, section by section, against **three OCR scans** of the printed book, and `tools/extract.py` refuses anything that fails either test. **All 291 sections are present.** - **The text — fifth edition:** *Organon of Medicine*, 5th edition (1833), translated by R. E. Dudgeon, 1849 — public domain. Built by `tools/build-organon5.py` from the **same fifteen Médi-T pages**, which print both editions side by side; the sixth-edition parser skips the fifth-edition blocks by design, and this one keeps them. Corroborated against **three Dudgeon scans** (Wellcome 1893, Internet Archive 1849, Google 1849): median **0.979**, minimum **0.745**, every one of its **294 sections** above the 0.60 floor. **They are different books:** 74 sections are worded differently and §292–§294 exist only in the fifth. - **Built with:** `web-kit`'s storage model, and nothing else. No CDN, no build step, no dependencies. ## What it does **Two editions, and it never confuses them.** The edition selector in the header switches the whole book — text, section list, search and bookmarks. Every section says how the two editions stand: *only in the fifth edition*, *wording differs from the sixth edition*, or *same wording in both editions*. Each edition keeps its own bookmarks and notes, because a note on §153 means a different paragraph in each. It is a reader, not an interpreter. It presents the text, finds a phrase in it instantly, and keeps your bookmarks and notes on your own device. It does not summarise, advise, or explain Hahnemann. Search is phrase search over the bundled text. Type `vital force` and every section that contains it is listed, best match first, each with its section number and the line it matched. Every section is in the left-hand list — click one, or type a number into the § box to jump. In the text you can walk the book with **Next / Previous**, or the ← and → keys, and the reader steps over a section it does not carry rather than stopping dead at the gap. Open a section and you can bookmark it or write a note; both are stored locally and both come back on the next visit. Under each section number the reader names the scan that section was read from. ## What it refuses to do - **It does not merge the editions.** The two bundles are separate files with separate provenance; nothing is blended into one "best" text, and a section is never silently swapped for its counterpart in the other edition. - **It does not renumber the book.** A section exists only where a section mark can be read, and every section records where its text came from. OCR alone reached 255 of 291 — three scans of the same printing lose *different* marks — so the remaining 36 come from the transcription, each accepted only because its wording is found verbatim in the scans (median 98% of its word-runs). Nothing was renumbered, nothing was reconstructed, nothing was taken from another edition or another translation. - **It does not invent a section to fill a gap.** Nothing in the text is paraphrased, reconstructed or generated. - **It does not fetch anything.** No `fetch`, no `XMLHttpRequest`, no beacon, no socket, no off-origin `

# Panchang [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**A daily Indian almanac that computes the day on your device** — and tells you the minute each limb changes. Tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana with their end times; sunrise, sunset, moonrise and moonset; Rahu Kaal, Gulika, Yamaganda and Abhijit; day and night choghadiya; the twenty-four hora; the lunar month in both reckonings, Vikram and Shaka Samvat; the moon's sign and phase; an eclipse flag; festivals resolved from tithi rules; a muhurat finder. No network, no account, no telemetry. **[Open the app →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-panchang/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-panchang/) · [Method](#how-the-panchang-is-computed) · [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-panchang/releases) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) The landing page is not a picture of the app — it embeds the real `docs/play/` in a frame and drives it to a day worth seeing. The app is two scripts and three data files, all in this repository: a shared runtime (`web-kit.js`), the engine (`panchang.js`, self-contained), and the bundled names, cities and festival rules. No build step, no bundler, no package install, no server. ## What it does Pick a date and a place — search a city, tap **Use my location**, or type coordinates. The app computes the day and shows, for each limb, **when it began and when it ends**: ``` Tithi Krishna Amavasya 11:27 → 12:31 Nakshatra Swati pada 1 05:51 → 07:23 Yoga Ayushman 03:25 → 03:01 Karana Chatushpada 11:27 → 23:56 Rahu Kaal (Sunday) 16:37 → 18:02 ``` Every day is addressable, so a panchang can be linked or shared: `docs/play/index.html#d=2026-11-08&lat=19.0760&lng=72.8777&zone=Asia/Kolkata&lang=gu`. | | | |---|---| | headless assertions, `node test-node.js` | **204 passing, 0 failed** | | runtime dependencies | **0** — two in-repo scripts and three data files | | sun–moon elongation vs an independent ephemeris | **better than 0.05°** | | limb boundary accuracy | **a minute or two**, stated rather than hidden | | cities bundled, with real time zones | **118** | | languages | **3** — English, हिन्दी, ગુજરાતી, values translated too | | engine | `panchang.js` 0.4.0 | ## What it must not do, and does not - **No account, no profile, no sync.** There is nothing to sign into. - **No network at runtime.** A test scans every shipped file for a script, link or fetch pointed at another origin; a second test renders the app in Chromium with every host unresolvable. - **No telemetry, analytics or error reporting.** Nothing leaves the device. - **No external font, icon or badge service.** Type is the system face; badges and every icon size are generated in this repository. - **No geocoder.** The city list is a data file. Reverse geocoding offline is not possible without a dataset this app should not carry, so "use my location" snaps to the nearest bundled city. - **No silently stale page.** Every asset is version-tagged and the service worker's cache is named after the release, so a new page cannot pair with an old engine; if it somehow does, the page says so and offers a reload instead of sitting there frozen. - **No silent precision.** Lunar longitude from a reduced series puts a tithi or nakshatra boundary within a minute or two of time, and local tradition differs on ayanamsa and on where a day begins. The day can be read at noon (default), sunrise, or midnight — the app says which. ## How the panchang is computed Entirely on-device, from first principles: - apparent **solar and lunar longitudes** from Meeus, *Astronomical Algorithms* (ch. 25 and 47) — the moon with its E-factor, the additive planetary terms (A1, A2) and its latitude from the largest ch. 47 terms; **ΔT** by the Espenak–Meeus polynomial, so the series are given TT while the API takes UT; - **tithi** and **karana** from the moon–sun elongation, **nakshatra** and **yoga** from the sidereal positions after a **Lahiri ayanamsa** (linear precession from its J2000 value); - **limb boundaries** by bisection on those angles — which is what turns "which tithi is today" into "the tithi changes at 14:52"; - **sunrise and sunset** from the standard sunrise equation with altitude and refraction, plus civil twilight; **moonrise and moonset** by sampling the moon's altitude and bisecting the crossings, using GMST and the moon's own latitude; - **Rahu Kaal, Gulika, Yamaganda, Abhijit** as segments of the real sunrise-to-sunset day, and **choghadiya** and **hora** from the weekday tables; - **the lunar month** amanta and purnimanta, named from the solar sign at the new moon that begins it, and the **samvat** years from the Gregorian date; - **eclipses** from the distance of the moon to the nearer node at the syzygy — "possible", never "visible here", which would need a horizon model this app does not claim; - **festivals** from `{masa, paksha, tithi, at}` rules in `docs/play/data/festivals.js`, not from a table of dates that goes stale. `test-node.js` checks six elongations against an independent ephemeris, the March equinox, Mumbai's sunrise and sunset, Holi and Diwali, the karana table, a 1000-day sweep, polar latitudes, daylight saving in Sydney and London, four published eclipses, ten festivals against their conventional dates, the choghadiya and hora tables, the names tables, the cities, the page's own wiring, and an offline guard. `scripts/offline-check.js` then renders the page in Chromium with every host unresolvable and looks for the day's tithi in the DOM. ## Run it ```bash open docs/play/index.html # the whole app, no install node test-node.js # 204 passed, 0 failed node scripts/offline-check.js # renders with no network (skips if no browser) node scripts/stamp.js # after a VERSION bump: record what shipped ``` ## Download it Every push builds the binaries from the same commit as the demo and attaches them to the rolling `app-latest` release; tagged releases carry the same assets with the changelog. The icon is [here](docs/play/icon-512.png) — `scripts/icons.py` renders every size from `docs/play/icon.svg`, including a Windows `.ico` and the Android adaptive layers, so no hand-made PNG can drift. | | | | |---|---|---| | | **Windows** | `panchang-portable.exe` — no installer, no registry writes | | | **Android** | `panchang.apk` — signed, sideload; no store | | | **Linux** | `panchang-linux` — `chmod +x` and run | ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page — night sky, gold, its own design docs/play/index.html the app docs/play/panchang.js the engine: astronomy, limbs, windows, months, eclipses docs/play/web-kit.js the shared runtime: storage, i18n, CSV, theme, a11y docs/play/data/names.js tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana, masa, rashi in three scripts docs/play/data/cities.js 118 places, each with an IANA zone docs/play/data/festivals.js observances as tithi rules, not dates docs/play/sw.js offline shell — HTML network-first, assets cache-first docs/assets/ screenshots and generated badges scripts/badges.py draws the badges, reading the count from the suite scripts/icons.py renders every icon size from the SVG master scripts/shot.py screenshots the landing page and the app scripts/offline-check.js renders the app with no network, in a real browser scripts/stamp.js records what shipped in BUILD.json, and refuses a stale tag BUILD.json the SHA-256 of every file a browser can fetch ENHANCEMENTS.md what is worth doing next, and what it would cost ``` ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. app-poets-studio: # Poet's Studio ![live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg) ![tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg) ![offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![deps](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) ![dictionary](docs/assets/badge-dict.svg) **Rhyme, metre and fixed forms — a workshop that measures what you actually wrote.** Offline, no accounts, no telemetry, no generator. The whole 124,926-word pronouncing dictionary travels inside the app. [Live app](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-poets-studio/play/) · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-poets-studio/) · [What it refuses to do](#what-it-refuses-to-do) · [Sources](#the-dictionary-and-its-size) · [Enhancements](ENHANCEMENTS.md) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) Master list **#130** · built from `QUEUE/app-poets-studio.md`. ## What it does - **Rhyme finder** — perfect, near and slant rhymes, found by *sound* from a pronouncing dictionary, with a syllable filter. Spelling is not consulted, so `though` and `cough` are correctly told apart and `say` rhymes with `away`. - **Syllable and metre counter** — every line, with its stress pattern shown as a running bar. When the line is regular the metre is named; when it is not, it is not named, and the message names the **foot** that broke and which way the beat falls there. - **The scheme as you are making it** — the gutter letters each line ending A, B, C … in order of first appearance, so you see the rhyme you are actually writing rather than the one you meant to write. - **Fixed forms as constraints that check you** — Shakespearean sonnet, blank verse, terza rima, rubaiyat quatrain, haiku, tanka, limerick, ghazal, and a custom stanza with your own syllable counts and scheme. Each is a live pass/fail with the reason, per line. - **A ghazal in Devanagari or Gujarati** — measured in *mātrā*, not in English phonemes. Every line of a couplet must share the same count, which is the practical test of a shared beher; the script is named under the form. - **Two readings where a word has two** — `record`, `present`, `wind`, `read`, `blessed`, `learned` and their kind keep both pronunciations, and the metre picks the one the line asks for. - **Samples to load** — a sonnet that passes, a haiku, a tanka, a ghazal with a radif, a ghazal in Devanagari, and one haiku that is a syllable long in its first line so you can see the app say so. They live in `docs/play/samples.js`, and the tests assert the verdict each one is there to demonstrate. - **My words** — teach it a name, a dialect form or an invented word by giving its sounds in ARPAbet. It is appended to the dictionary text before parsing, so the metre and the rhyme finder treat it like any other word. It stays on the device. - **Writing journal** — drafts, versions and notes on the device, kept in IndexedDB rather than localStorage so a journal of versions is not up against a 5 MB ceiling: import a journal as well as export it, diff two versions line by line, rename, copy, and undo a delete. Two tabs on the same journal tell each other when one of them saves, so neither silently reverts the other. Export one poem, the whole journal as JSON, or every draft as a ZIP. - **Print** — `Ctrl/Cmd+P` gives the poem and its measure, without the furniture. ## The three rhyme strengths | | | | |---|---|---| | **Perfect** | the same sound from the last stressed vowel | `wall` / `fall`, `day` / `grey` | | **Near** | the same consonant frame, a different vowel | `cat` / `cot`, `love` / `move` | | **Slant** | the same stressed vowel, a different ending | `cat` / `cap` | ## The dictionary, and its size `docs/play/dict.js` carries the **CMU Pronouncing Dictionary** — **124,926 words** and **133,971 pronunciations** — inside the app, so rhyme and metre work with no network and no model. Every pronunciation is kept, not one per word: 8,383 words have more than one reading, and those are the words a poet notices. `fire` measures as one syllable or two, `read` as *reed* or *red*, depending on the line. It ships in a single-character ARPAbet encoding (each phoneme is one printable character at `33 + its index in Poetry.ALPHABET`), which is about half the bytes of the plain text and decodes in one pass. Extra readings of the same word follow the first on the same line, separated by `|`. The derivation is reproducible: `python3 scripts/build-dict.py path/to/cmudict.dict`. The tab that separates the word from its phonemes is what marks a line as encoded, so a plain `word P1 P2` dictionary can still be pasted in by hand — which is exactly how **My words** works. Around thirty elided and archaic forms the dictionary has never met — `dimm'd`, `ow'st`, `grow'st`, `wander'st`, `ne'er`, `o'er`, `'tis`, `heav'n` — carry a hand-written pronunciation in `poetry.js`, so a real sonnet is not marked inexact for its apostrophes. The dictionary is BSD-2-Clause and its licence travels with it in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). ## The mātrā counter A syllable in Devanagari or Gujarati is a written unit, not a vowel phoneme: a consonant carries its inherent *a* (1 mātrā), a mātrā sign replaces it with its own weight, and a halant kills it — so `कल` is 2, `काल` is 3, and `क्` is 0. Anusvara and chandrabindu nasalise the vowel they follow and add nothing. The ghazal uses that count directly. Two lines that share a beher share a mātrā count, so that is what the form checks, line by line, and reports. Urdu script is deliberately **not** counted: its short vowels are not written, so a mātrā count there would be a guess dressed up as a measurement. ## What it refuses to do - **Write the poem.** There is no generator, no prompt box, no suggestion engine. - **Guess at a word it does not know.** An unknown word is named in the line and counted as one syllable, and the line is marked inexact — a metre count that is quietly wrong is worse than one that says it is unsure. - **Call an irregular line regular.** A metre is only named when at least 60% of its feet fit; otherwise the pattern is shown and the name is left off. - **Reach the network.** No `fetch`, no `XMLHttpRequest`, no socket, anywhere in the app — and a test asserts it. ## Run it Open `docs/play/index.html`. That is the whole app — the kits, the samples and the dictionary sit next to it, so it works from `file://` and from GitHub Pages. ``` node test-node.js # 136 assertions, no dependencies node test-ui.mjs # the page in a real DOM (needs jsdom, harness only) node scripts/build-single.mjs # one self-contained dist/poets-studio.html bash scripts/icons.sh # the icon set, from docs/icon.svg python3 scripts/badges.py # the badges, drawn locally bash scripts/shot.sh app sonnet bash scripts/release-notes.sh --dry-run ``` Over http(s) the app also **installs itself**: `sw.js` caches the six files once, so afterwards it opens from an icon with the network off. The page is served network-first and the cache name is bumped on every release, so a new build is never hidden behind a stale cache; the footer prints a build stamp so "am I on the new one?" is answerable from the page itself. Keyboard: `Ctrl/Cmd+S` save, `Alt+R` rhyme finder, `Alt+1…9` pick a form. ## How it is built | | | |---|---| | `docs/index.html` | the landing page — its own design, with the app embedded live | | `docs/play/index.html` | the app — one page, no build step | | `docs/play/poetry.js` | the engine: syllables, stress, rhyme, metre, forms. Works in the browser and in Node, so the tests test the app | | `docs/play/dict.js` | the bundled dictionary | | `docs/play/samples.js` | the poems the app can load, with the verdict each one demonstrates | | `docs/play/web-kit.js` | shell, storage, theme, i18n, CSV | | `docs/play/export-kit.js` | files and ZIP off the device | | `docs/play/sw.js` | the service worker: network-first HTML, cache-first assets | | `docs/play/manifest.webmanifest` | install metadata and the icon set | | `docs/icon.svg`, `docs/icon-glyph.svg` | the mark, and the mark without its ground | | `docs/play/icon.png` | the icon the release builds take: the kit reads it from the app directory | | `scripts/` | badges, icons, the dictionary, screenshots, release notes and the single-file build — all local | | `packaging/app-poets-studio.desktop` | the Linux launcher entry, with its icon | | `docs/play/icon*.png` | the icon the builds take — launcher PNGs, and the adaptive layers Android masks | | `changes/`, `VERSION` | the changelog is written with the change, not reconstructed later | | `ENHANCEMENTS.md` | what is shipped, what is left, and why the rest is not done | Deep links open a case directly: `play/#/sonnet`, `#/tanka`, `#/haiku-off`, `#/ghazal`, `#/ghazal-hindi`, `#/rhyme/though`. The landing page drives the embedded app with the same slugs over `postMessage`, so switching sample never reloads the dictionary. The form checks are deliberately honest about the difference between a *dictionary* stress and a *verse* stress: CMUdict marks `is` and `a` as primary stressed, which no one beats in a line, so a line is allowed to depart from the ideal pattern in up to 20% of its syllables rather than being held to a perfection no real sonnet has. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # app-story-engine

<!-- shot:start -->

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-story-engine/)
[![download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-story-engine?label=download&color=blue)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-story-engine/releases/latest)
[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-141%20assertions-3f7a52)](test-node.js)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-informational)](LICENSE)

**A book the reader moves through: choices, carried state, and a map of where you have been** — offline, no accounts, no telemetry.

Read it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-story-engine/play/> · About it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-story-engine/>

## Why it exists

A "choose your own adventure" app usually forgets what you chose: the branches are a tree of
screens and the reader is a click. This one makes **the state the story**. What you pick changes
what you carry; what you carry decides which doors are still open; and the trail shows every
passage you have been through, in the order you went through them — return visits included.

## What is here

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/play/story-engine.js` | the engine — `compile`, `newGame`, `choicesFor`, `advance`, `trail`, `save`, `load`, `createStore` |
| `docs/play/book.js` | *The Fifth Mile* — the book that ships with it, as data |
| `docs/play/index.html` | the reader — passage, choices, closed doors, the trail, the state you carry |
| `docs/index.html` | the landing page |
| `test-node.js` | `node test-node.js` — 141 assertions over the real engine and the real book |

## The four things it promises

1. **A choice leads to a different passage.** Two choices at one passage go to two different
   passages. A choice that does not exist is refused **with the passage shown**.
2. **The same choices produce the same ending.** The engine has no clock, no dice and no `eval`.
   Replay and you get the same state, the same trail, the same ending.
3. **The trail is every passage, in order.** A return visit is recorded again, not collapsed into a set.
4. **A failure is reported, never smoothed over.** A full disk stops the *saving*, not the reading.
   A corrupt save is reported with the passage it claims and offered for export — the app never
   resumes at the beginning and calls it your place.

## Run it

Open `docs/play/index.html`. That is the whole app — the two kits it uses sit next to it, so it
works from `file://`, a USB stick, or GitHub Pages.

```bash
node test-node.js          # 141 assertions
```

# Thermals [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**What each classical source actually says about a remedy's thermal reaction — in its own words, with the source named — and where those sources do not say the same thing.** **[Open the app →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-thermals/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-thermals/) · [The rule](#the-extraction-rule) · [Sources](#the-three-sources) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) *The pipeline above keeps this screenshot of the live demo current. A curated set — desktop, phone, landing page — lives in [`docs/assets/`](docs/assets) and is what the landing page uses.* Light and dark, toggled from the header and remembered; the system preference decides the first paint. Offline, no accounts, no server, no network at any point. One page, no build step, no runtime dependencies — the four kits it uses are vendored. ## What it does Look up a remedy and read what every bundled source says about its thermal reaction, each statement quoted verbatim against the source that wrote it. Above the quotes sits a summary **computed from those quotes**: | Summary | When | |---|---| | `sources agree (n)` | two or more bundled sources speak, and all of them point the same way | | `sources disagree` | two or more speak and they point opposite ways | | `one source only` | exactly one bundled source speaks. **This is the common case and is never agreement** | | `unclassified` | no bundled source carries a thermal statement for that remedy. It carries no quote and no summary | A **dated note** is a temporary shift — an acute fever, a pregnancy, a proving — with an end date. When the date passes the note stays visible, marked expired, and the constitutional quotes are untouched. | | | |---|---| | quoted sentences (rows) | **164** | | remedies in the index | **366** | | remedies with at least one statement | **115** | | remedies with no statement in any source (`unclassified`) | **251** | | sources | **3** | | remedies carried by two sources | **12** | | remedy names unresolved | **0** | | quotes repaired from the page image | **6** |

## What it must not do, and does not - It never assigns, derives, averages or infers a thermal state. One row is one remedy, one source, one verbatim sentence. - It never derives a classification from rubric counts or grades. - It never selects or prescribes a remedy, and it does not decide anyone's thermal state. - `ambithermal` is not a state this app looks for: no bundled source uses the word. - A remedy no source speaks about is `unclassified` — no quote, no summary. ## The extraction rule It ships with the data, because the row count is a property of it. A **thermal statement** is a sentence in a source's own words containing one of these phrases, as whole words, case-insensitively: `chilly` · `chilliness` · `always cold` · `feels cold` · `feels hot` · `cold feeling` · `cold-blooded` · `warm-blooded` · `always warm` · `cold constitution` · `hot constitution` · `warm constitution` · `cold patient` · `hot patient` 1. **Modality lines and modality sections are excluded** — a modality is what changes a state, not what the state is. 2. **Fragments under 12 characters and paragraphs over 400 are excluded.** 12 and not 20 because *"Chilly disposition."* — Jahr 1847, Cistus — is 19 characters and is exactly the statement this app exists to show. 3. **The sentence is kept verbatim.** Whitespace is normalised; nothing else is paraphrased, reordered, merged or trimmed. 4. The set is deliberately narrow: a bare *cold* or *heat* is not in it, because in this corpus those words are overwhelmingly water, air, a room, a modality or a fever. `tools/extract.py` applies the rule; `tools/make-bundle.py` turns the result into the bundle the page loads; `node test-node.js` checks the output. ## The three sources | Source | Gives | Notes | |---|---|---| | **Open Materia Medica** — © Dr. Sohil Momin, BHMS, 2026 | 109 rows across 82 remedy pages | the estate's own plain-language materia medica, quoted with the copyright holder's permission | | **Manual of Homoeopathic Medicine** — G. H. G. Jahr, trans. P. F. Curie, 1847 | materia medica text | public domain, via `homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json` | | **Homoeopathic Therapeutics of Diarrhoea** — James B. Bell, 7th ed., 1906 | materia medica text | public domain, checked against a [second scan of the same edition](https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.94901) | `repertory/repertorium-publicum-2008/` in the JSON repository is GPL v3 and is **not** bundled. ## Correcting the names The transcribed books are OCR. Some remedy names arrive damaged (`NTJX VOMICA`), some merged with the next remedy, and some are really chapter headings. `tools/names.py` corrects what an authority confirms and says so where none does. **Authorities**, all free and named in `data/reference-names.json`: Open Materia Medica's 344 curated names, the repertory remedy index, and the Internet Archive's numbered index of Jahr's *Manual* (1847). | outcome | entries | |---|---| | confirmed — the printed name is already a known name | **79** | | corrected from a named authority (26 of them readings the owner confirmed directly) | **47** | | settled by a second scan of the same book, from the entry's own symptoms | **10** | | readable, kept as printed (a remedy the reference does not carry) | **132** | | **not bundled** — two remedies the transcription ran together | **27** | | **not bundled** — not a remedy (chapter heading, page artefact, fragment, duplicate) | **7** | Every correction carries its evidence in `data/name-overrides.json`, and the app shows the name the transcription printed next to the correction, so a reader can check it rather than trust it. ## Repairing the texts `text_damage` marks a quote that carries a swallowed page number, a broken word or a stray mark. Where the damage can be repaired **from the page itself**, it is: `tools/text-repair.py` pulls the scan's page-level OCR, finds the page carrying the sentence, and repairs only what the page witnesses — `sen-` + `sitiveness` → `sensitiveness`, `alw'ays` → `always`, and a page number swallowed into the prose. Six quotes are repaired this way, each keeping the transcription's own words beside it and showing its page number. **No quote currently carries a damage flag**, and the ones that were never damaged no longer say they were. ## Run it ```bash node test-node.js # 567 assertions python3 -m http.server -d docs 8000 # landing page + app, or just open docs/index.html ``` Regenerating the data needs the two source repositories side by side: ```bash python3 tools/names.py --fetch # rebuild the name reference (needs archive.org) python3 tools/names.py # apply it -> data/name-map.json python3 tools/text-repair.py --fetch # page-level OCR of the Bell scan python3 tools/text-repair.py # repair damaged quotes -> data/text-repairs.json python3 tools/extract.py src/open-materia-medica src/materia-medica-json data python3 tools/make-bundle.py python3 tools/badges.py # the local SVG badges node test-node.js ``` ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page (this project's own design) docs/play/index.html the app itself docs/play/thermals.js the logic the page and the tests both use docs/play/data/bundle.js the bundle: rows, remedies, the rule, the counts docs/play/vendor/ web-kit, search-kit, case-kit, export-kit (vendored) docs/assets/ screenshots and the generated badges data/ rows, remedies, name map, reference, text repairs tools/ extract, names, text-repair, make-bundle, badges test-node.js the suite ``` ## Kits **web-kit** (storage, and whether a write landed) · **search-kit** (ranked lookup across the quoted sentences) · **case-kit** (the dated-override record) · **export-kit** (getting the bundle and the notes off the device). ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # Weft Puzzles ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Six small programming puzzles, solved on a real 8-bit machine.** [![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-play%20it-4fd1e0?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=0a2342)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=0a2342)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342&color=4fd1e0)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/releases/latest) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-5ee0a0?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-ffb454?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [**Play it →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) · [The machine it runs on](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard)
![Weft Puzzles](docs/shot.png) A robot on a grid, five puzzles, and a machine with sixteen registers, four flags and twenty-seven instructions — **and no `if` statement**. So you build one, out of `CMP` and `JZ`. That is the whole point of the puzzles: the constraint is the lesson. ## The six puzzles | # | Puzzle | What it teaches | |---|---|---| | 01 | **First thread** | `LDI` puts a number in the accumulator, `OUT MOVE` hands it to the machine | | 02 | **Step around** | four moves, three directions — a straight line is not always the answer | | 03 | **Until you stand on it** | `LOAD` reads a port; `CMP` + `JZ` are how a machine decides | | 04 | **Feel for the wall** | `BUMPED` is the machine's own feedback — a loop that reacts | | 05 | **The whole weave** | a level can ask for more than arrival: collect both flags first | | 06 | **The long way round** | three bump loops in a row — a program is a shape you repeat | Each puzzle ships a **working solution**, and the test suite runs every one of them on the real machine. A puzzle nobody has solved is a puzzle nobody knows is solvable — so that is asserted, not assumed. ## Built on the Loom This app does not carry its own computer. It runs the **Weft-8** from [Jacquard (the Loom)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — `docs/play/weft8.js` is that engine, byte for byte the same file, and the same one its 102 assertions cover. What this repository adds is a *world*: `docs/play/world.js` puts the machine inside a grid and hangs seven ports off it, at `0xD0` and up so they never collide with the Loom's own `0xC0`–`0xCA`: ``` POS_X 0xD0 POS_Y 0xD1 UNDER 0xD2 MOVE 0xD3 BUMPED 0xD4 DONE 0xD5 BEEP 0xD6 ``` So the machine is unchanged, and the puzzle is a peripheral — which is exactly how a real 8-bit computer met the world. ## Run it Open `docs/index.html`, or play the [live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/). Windows EXE and Android APK are on the [rolling release](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/releases/latest). ## Test it ``` npm install # jsdom, test-only node test-node.js # 69 assertions: the machine, the world, and every level's solution node tests/page-smoke.js # 12 assertions: the page, driven in jsdom ``` The engine suite asserts that the machine is still the Loom's (two-byte encoding, 27 opcodes), that the world obeys its own rules (walls refuse a move and set the bump flag, flags are taken once, the checker knows a level with a flag left is not solved), that **every level's reference solution solves it in under 400 steps and fits the 128-byte ROM**, and that wrong answers are refused — walking into the wall, stopping one square short, and guessing a corridor's length blind. The page suite boots the real page, picks puzzles, runs programs, peeks at the solution and checks the page says *Solved* — because a page that does not work is not a puzzle. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | **Weft Puzzles** (you are here) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # art-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **The art primitives Forge was missing.** Zero dependencies, one file, no assets. palette · pixel canvas · draw ops · undo · dithering · median-cut · sprite sheets · isometric · sketch loop
--- ## The two halves - **STATIC pixel art** — an indexed palette, a pixel canvas that scales with **nearest-neighbour** (smoothing off by default — the classic trap), draw ops, a delta undo stack, dithering, median-cut quantisation, sprite sheets, and the isometric mapping. - **LIVE generative visuals** — a frame loop (`Art.sketch`) you can run on its own or drive from `game-kit`'s fixed timestep, so a sketch is reproducible from a fixed step. Both, from one kit. ## What's in it | | | |---|---| | `palette` | an indexed palette from a Lospec-style list, with `swap`, `cycle` and `nearest` | | `canvas` | an indexed pixel buffer: `set`, `line`, `rect`, `ellipse`, `fill`, `mirror` | | `scale` | nearest-neighbour upscaling (never smooths) | | `history` | a bounded undo/redo stack that stores **deltas, not whole frames** | | `dither` | ordered (Bayer) and Floyd–Steinberg | | `quantize` | median-cut to N colours, so a photo becomes pixel art | | `spriteSheet` / `sliceSprite` | a sheet + JSON atlas, with a slicing round-trip | | `tilemap` | a grid of tile ids (`-1` = no tile, so tile `0` stays legal): `get`/`set`, pixel→tile by **floor**, `fillRect`, a capped iterative `floodFill`, 4-bit `autotile` masks, and `toCanvas(tiles)` | | `anim` | a timeline over frames: `at(t)` is a **pure function of time**, `pingpong` without repeated endpoints, `fps 0` frozen instead of `NaN` | | `generate` | a **seeded** sprite generator (`Art.rng`, mulberry32) that is mirror-symmetric by construction, never empty, and rebuilds an asset folder from one number (`generateSet`) | | `iso` | the cartesian ↔ isometric coordinate mapping | | `sketch` | a setup-once / draw-every-frame loop | ## Usage ```js var Art = require("./art-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.Art var pal = Art.palette("1a1c2c 5d275d b13e53 ef7d57"); // a Lospec-style list var c = Art.canvas(32, 32, pal); c.rect(4, 4, 24, 24, 2, true).ellipse(16, 16, 10, 10, 3, true); var big = Art.scale(c, 8); // nearest-neighbour, crisp var hist = Art.history(c, { limit: 100 }); // undo/redo over deltas hist.begin(); c.set(0, 0, 1); hist.commit(); hist.undo(); var pal2 = Art.palette(Art.quantize(pixels, 16)); // median-cut a photo var sheet = Art.spriteSheet([frame0, frame1]); // sheet + atlas // 1.1.0 — a level, its timeline, and a seeded creature to put in it var map = Art.tilemap({ w: 20, h: 12, tileW: 16, tileH: 16 }); map.floodFill(0, 0, 1); // lay a floor var walls = map.autotile(); // N=1 E=2 S=4 W=8 per tile var level = map.toCanvas(tileCanvases); // compose it into one canvas var hero = Art.generate({ seed: 2026, w: 16, h: 16, density: 0.8 }); var walk = Art.anim([hero, Art.generate({ seed: 77, w: 16, h: 16 })], { fps: 8, pingpong: true }); walk.at(0.3); // the frame for that moment, always ``` ## Licence position (read this) Everything here is **reimplemented from published technique**; permissive reference projects are named only in comments, and **no code is copied**. In the survey behind this kit: Aseprite is not open source (learn, never copy); Data-Pixels and pixel8 carry **no licence**; six tools are copyleft — none of their code is used. The permissive references (piskel, Pixelorama, PixelCraft, poxi, and the isometric mapping from isometric-contributions) are cited as ideas. ## Tests ``` node test-node.js 86 passed, 0 failed ``` Covers the spec's required cases — a **nearest-neighbour scaling** case, a **dithering pattern** case, a **median-cut** case with a known input, a **sprite-sheet export round-trip**, a **tilemap** case (floor, flood-fill bounds, autotile masks), a **timeline** case (pure `at(t)`, pingpong without repeated endpoints) and a **procedural sprite** case (same seed, same sprite; mirror symmetry; never empty) — plus the palette, every draw op, the bounded delta undo stack, the isometric mapping and the sketch loop. All headless. The 1.1.0 additions were **mutation-tested ten ways** and all ten are caught by an assertion (floor→truncate in `at`, a flood fill that re-fills, swapped E/W autotile bits, `toCanvas` ignoring the tile id, pingpong repeating its endpoints, rounded instead of floored time, mirroring only on even widths, dropping the non-empty guarantee, ignoring the body shape, and `Art.version` drifting from `VERSION`). ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. The primitives a **panchang** (Indian almanac) needs — and nothing app-specific: - **Julian day**; **solar** and **lunar longitude** (Meeus); - **ayanamsa** (Lahiri, approximate); **sunrise / sunset / solar transit**; - **moon phase** and illumination; - the derived **tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana** — from the sun–moon longitude. ```js const p = Astro.panchang({ y: 2026, m: 10, d: 23, h: 6 }, { lat: 28.6139, lon: 77.2090 }); p.tithi.name; // "Shukla Dwadashi" p.nakshatra.name; // "Purva Bhadrapada" p.sun.sunriseUTC; // -> add your timezone offset ``` ## Verified against published values ``` node test-node.js 13 passed, 0 failed ``` - Sun apparent longitude vs **Meeus 25.b**: `199.90894` (published `199.90895`). - Moon longitude vs **Meeus 47.a**: `133.16000` (published `133.162655`). - Delhi sunrise/sunset, midsummer: `05:24` / `19:22` IST. - Tithi/nakshatra/yoga/karana ranges and the tithi–elongation relation. ## Accuracy — read this Solar and lunar longitude are good to about **0.01–0.05°**, which puts a tithi/nakshatra boundary within roughly **a minute of time**. # audio-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Synthesis, theory, patterns and notation.** Zero dependencies, one file, no audio assets. synthesis · ADSR · filters · noise · mixer · music theory · patterns · notation · sonification · mastering
--- ## The rule this kit exists to state **Game music is PATTERNS, NOT FILES.** A Forge game ships as one file with no assets. A pattern is a few kilobytes of data and plays through WebAudio; an audio file is megabytes. `game-kit` should adopt this rule: generate the music, do not ship it. ## What's in it | | | |---|---| | `music` | notes, intervals, transposition, 12 scales, 11 chords — the arithmetic every musical feature needs | | `synth` | a pure **ADSR** envelope, an oscillator voice with an optional filter, a noise source, and a small mixer | | `seq` | a **pattern sequencer**: rows × channels of notes, flattened to timed events and scheduled through WebAudio | | `notation` | a staff **layout** — each note's position, so a renderer just draws it | | `sonify` | map the bytes of any file to sound | | `master` | **honest** mastering helpers: a loudness measure, a match gain, and a peak limiter | | `time` | **deterministic time**: a seeded PRNG with stable forks, a tempo **map** (rubato, ritardando), and human timing jitter | | `sched` | a lookahead **scheduler with a watchdog** — a throttled tab must not end a song halfway | | `texture` | seven synthesised **ambient beds** (rain, wind, fire, vinyl, ocean, stream, hum) | | — | `synth.harmonics()` keeps partials under Nyquist; `synth.softClip()` is a master safety curve | Everything is generated in code or stored as pattern data. **No audio assets are shipped.** ## What changed in 1.1.0 Four things learnt building a full generative composer on this kit: 1. **Determinism is a feature, not a detail.** `A.time.seeded(seed)` gives the same stream everywhere, and `fork("drums")` is stable per label — so one track can be locked while the rest is re-rolled. 2. **Tempo moves.** `A.time.map([{beat:0,bpm:80},{beat:16,bpm:90}])` with `secondsAt`/`beatAt`/`bpmAt`. Every beat→second conversion in a real piece has to go through it, or note *lengths* drift the moment the tempo changes. 3. **Static is usually aliasing, and clicks are usually corners.** `synth.harmonics()` clamps partials under Nyquist; `synth.softClip()` is a `tanh` curve for the master, because a hard clamp is a corner and a corner is a click. 4. **A scheduler needs a watchdog.** `setInterval` stops in a throttled tab; `A.sched()` notices and keeps ticking. ## Usage ```js var A = require("./audio-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.AudioKit // Theory — no audio needed A.music.scale("C4", "major"); // -> [60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71] A.music.chord("A4", "minor"); // -> [69, 72, 76] A.music.parse("A4").freq; // -> 440 // Synthesis — on a user gesture (the browser rule) var ctx = new AudioContext(); var v = A.synth.voice(ctx, { type: "square", freq: 440, filter: "lowpass", cutoff: 900 }); v.play(ctx.currentTime, 0.5, { a: 0.01, d: 0.1, s: 0.7, r: 0.3 }); // A pattern: a few KB of data, not a file var pat = A.seq.pattern([ ["C4", null, null, "E4"], ["G4", null, "B4", null] ], { bpm: 120, rowsPerBeat: 4 }); A.seq.play(ctx, pat, { type: "square" }); // Notation layout A.notation.layout(["C4", "D4", "E4"]); // -> { notes: [{x, step, ...}], width } ``` ## Notes - **No autoplay.** Every node is built from a context you create on a user gesture. - **Everything is reimplemented.** References (the tracker tradition, Orca, MuseScore, matchering, binary-synth, Neothesia) are named in comments; **no code is copied**, and the copyleft ones are technique only. - **The mastering helpers are a matching aid, not a replacement for an engineer** — say so in any app that uses them. ## Tests ``` node test-node.js 42 passed, 0 failed ``` Covers the spec's required cases — an **ADSR envelope shape**, a **scale/chord construction**, a **sequencer scheduling** case (notes land on the right beats), and a **notation layout** — plus note parsing, transposition, sonification and the mastering helpers. All headless: the theory, the envelope maths and the scheduling are pure, so they test with no audio context. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # audit

[![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-3f7a52


![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)
The change log for the drsamonline fleet — **78 repositories, 105 workflow files, 10 scheduled jobs**.

Every audit, fix and correction lands here, with the evidence. Nothing in this repo is a plan for
later; if it says a thing was done, the `log/` entry that claims it carries the before-and-after.

## Why this exists

The fleet grew faster than its bookkeeping. Licence badges drifted from their LICENSE files, new
repos fell into an "Other / New" bucket, landing pages stopped offering downloads, and the audit
files that documented all of it were scattered across five unrelated repos. This repo is the single
place where the state of the fleet is measured, the change is recorded, and the next run can prove
what moved.

## Layout

    log/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md   one file per session
    reports/<YYYY-MM>-<slug>/          a measurement or a plan, with its evidence beside it
    state/                             machine-readable snapshots, refreshed by tools/collect.py
    tools/collect.py                   read every repo into state/
    tools/diff.py                      compare two snapshots, print only what changed
    tools/licence_check.py             licence badge vs LICENSE file, all repos
    tools/fix_licence_badges.py        make a badge say what its LICENSE grants
    tools/presentation_audit.py        landing page, app, badges, shots, support block, per repo
    tools/verify.py                    the repo-presentation skill's gate, copied verbatim

Four report sets live here so far: `reports/2026-11-fleet-audit/` (the whole estate read end to
end), `reports/2026-11-forge-release/` (the plan to ship the control plane as one release),
`reports/2026-11-presentation-audit/` (all 100 repos against the presentation skill, with the delta
each one still needs) and `reports/2026-11-manifest-design/` (seven rounds of design and review for
per-file provenance and drift-aware healing). A report is a measurement or a plan; the log entry is
the decision. Neither
is a substitute for the other.

## The rule

**A change is not done when it is pushed. It is done when it is read back from the API and the
batch's verification passes.** The log entry records the verification, not the intention.

Every log entry uses the same six headings, in this order:

    ## What I looked at
    ## What was wrong
    ## What I changed
    ## Evidence
    ## What I deliberately did not do
    ## Next

The fifth one matters most. A log that only records what changed hides the decisions that were
made by *not* changing something, and those are the ones that get re-litigated later.

## Read state through the API, never through raw

`raw.githubusercontent.com` serves a cached copy that lags minutes to hours behind a commit. In this
fleet it has twice made finished work look broken:

- a `build.yml` that already contained the icon wiring was served without it
- 14 landing pages that had just been repaired were served in their old, broken form

Both times the API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`) showed the truth immediately.
**Use the API to decide whether something worked.** Use raw only for bulk reading of files that
have not changed in the last hour. Where a URL matters, fetch actual bytes and check the status.

## Running it

    gh auth login                      # or GH_TOKEN in the environment
    python3 tools/collect.py           # ~5 minutes for 78 repos
    python3 tools/licence_check.py     # exits 1 if any badge is wrong

`licence_check.py` runs weekly on a Monday at 03:31 UTC and commits the fresh snapshot. That cron is
deliberately clear of every other job in the fleet — the current set is:

    Mon 03:17  update-profile        Mon 03:23  skills/refresh
    Mon 03:31  licence-check (this)  Tue 03:47  dashboard/refresh
    Tue 04:00  metrics               Tue 04:12  Matneo/blog
    Tue 04:22  Matneo/store          Tue 06:00  control-panel/scan
    Wed 05:00  app-builder/kit-tests 1st+16th 03:00 store-images, 03:37 refresh-hub

## Conventions

- **One commit per repo.** Repos are independent; there is no shared release train, and a
  cross-repo change cannot be reverted per repo.
- **A script fixes a class of defect; a human decides a class of question.** Encoding a space is
  a script. "Is this repo MIT or PolyForm?" is not.
- **Never let a sweep invent a licence.** If a badge and its LICENSE disagree, the sweep stops
  and the repo goes to the decision batch.
- **Test against the real response shape and the broken state.** Two repairs in this log failed
  because they were tested against cached data and against a clean page instead of the damaged one.

# Awesome Single-File Tools [![Awesome](https://cdn.rawgit.com/sindresorhus/awesome/d7305f38d29fed78fa20e105be61d1284d73385f/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome)

> A curated collection of zero-dependency, local-first, single-file HTML tools, productivity widgets, and platform frameworks designed for digital sovereignty, total privacy, and ultimate portability.

Single-file HTML tools run natively in any modern browser—requiring no server setup, no `npm install`, no complex build pipelines, and zero telemetry. Just double-click, inspect, edit, and maintain full ownership of your software and data.

---

## 📜 Manifesto & Philosophy

- **Local-First & Offline-Ready**: Your data remains on your physical device. No hidden network requests.
- **Zero External Dependencies**: Everything needed (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) lives within a single file.
- **Intellectual Sovereignty**: Pure software you can inspect, modify, fork, and preserve indefinitely.
- **Citizen Developer Friendly**: Highly readable, hackable code that can be customized in any standard text editor.

🌐 *Explore the ecosystem showcase at [Crystal World Project Homepage](https://crystal-world-project.github.io/crystal-world/index-en.html).*

---

- [Knowledge Management & PKM](#-knowledge-management--pkm)
- [Utilities & Productivity](#-utilities--productivity)
- [Media, Graphics & Creation](#-media-graphics--creation)
- [Developer Tools & API Clients](#-developer-tools--api-clients)
- [Contribution Guidelines](#-contribution-guidelines)
- [License](#-license)

---

## 🌟 Featured Anchor Project
### 🧸 [Teddy Wiki Lite](https://crystal-world-project.github.io/crystal-world/teddy-wiki-lite.html) `v1.3`
An ultra-lightweight, zero-dependency, single-file HTML personal wiki & knowledge management tool inspired by TiddlyWiki.
- **Key Features**:
  - Embedded multi-tag AND query filtering engine (`Array.every`).
  - Seamless Edit/View markdown parsing interface.
  - Safe inter-iframe communication protocol via `postMessage`.
  - Self-contained JSON storage ready for multi-dimensional knowledge matrix integration.
- **Organization**: [crystal-world-project](https://github.com/crystal-world-project)

---

## 🧠 Knowledge Management & PKM

- **[TiddlyWiki Classic / Standalone](https://tiddlywiki.com/)** - The legendary single-file non-linear personal web notebook and pioneer of the single-file paradigm.
- **[Teddy Wiki](https://crystal-world-project.github.io/crystal-world/index-en.html)** - A standalone in-memory single-file HTML wiki & personal knowledge base system.
- **[Teddy Wiki Lite](https://crystal-world-project.github.io/crystal-world/teddy-wiki-lite.html)** - Compact, single-file HTML markdown wiki with multi-tag query capabilities.
- **[Three Shifts, Six Inversions — Knowledge Graph](https://0603wangxiao.github.io/36wx/kg/)** - A 386 KB single-file Canvas knowledge graph of a self-authored analytical framework (three shifts, six inversions, hexagrams, verse) *(Chinese / Interactive Eastern Philosophy Framework)*; zoom, pan, and click any node to read its definition and source. Zero external requests — runs fully offline.
- *(Additional single-file outliners, journaling templates, and flashcard tools welcome)*

---

## 🛠️ Utilities & Productivity

- *(Single-file Kanban boards)*
- *(Local Pomodoro timers & Habit trackers)*
- *(Offline calculators & decision matrix engines)*

---

## 🎨 Media, Graphics & Creation

- **[Bento Slides](https://bento.page/)** - An open-source, local-first presentation tool packed into a single HTML file containing the deck, editor, presenter mode, and interactive charts.
- **[Nano Blake](https://crystal-world-project.github.io/crystal-world/nano-blake.html)** - A single-file HTML slideshow & video memo engine featuring smooth Ken Burns animation effects and Web Speech API audio integration.

---

## 💻 Developer Tools & API Clients

- **[Crystal Dock](https://crystal-world-project.github.io/crystal-world/crystal-dock.html)** - An ultra-lightweight single-file modular meta-platform using iframe sandboxing and `postMessage` protocol to connect isolated web tools without build steps.
- *(In-browser RegEx testers & HTML sandboxes)*
- *(Single-file REST API clients & GitHub API GUI managers)*
- *(JSON formatters & offline base64 / token encoders)*

---

## 🤝 Contribution Guidelines

We warmly welcome submissions of single-file tools and apps! To be listed, a tool must satisfy the following criteria:

1. **Single File Structure**: Entire application logic (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) must reside within one standalone `.html` file.
2. **Local-First**: Complete functionality must be preserved offline without requiring external servers or APIs (except optional user-configured tokens).
3. **Zero Critical CDNs**: No dynamic external script fetching that degrades functionality if offline.
4. **Data Privacy**: No background analytics, tracking, or telemetry.

# backup [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Snapshot a repository before it changes — so a merge can never lose the code that was there.** A reusable GitHub workflow + a zero-dependency script. Compressed, timestamped, rotated, and never full.
--- ## What it does Before a merge replaces a repository's code, `backup` takes the **state that is about to be replaced** and stores it, compressed, in a **dumps** repository: ``` dumps/ drsamonline__ml-kit/ 2026-10-24T103000Z/ ml-kit.tar.gz 2026-10-24T110000Z/ ml-kit.tar.gz drsamonline__case-kit/ 2026-10-24T103000Z/ case-kit.tar.gz ``` One folder per repository (`owner__repo`), one folder per backup named with the **date and time**, and inside it the repository as a `.tar.gz`. ## The two rules that keep it safe 1. **It never fills up.** Each repository keeps the newest **100** backups (configurable). Past that, the **oldest is deleted** to make room for the new one — so the most recent work is always present and the store stays bounded. 2. **It never stops.** When a dumps repository passes its **size cap** (800 MB by default), the next one is **created automatically** — `dumps`, `dumps-2`, `dumps-3`, … — and the backup continues there. A full repo can never block a backup. ## How to wire it in — before every merge Add this to any repository's workflow. It runs on a pull request, so it snapshots the **base commit** — the code as it is *before* the merge: ```yaml name: backup on: pull_request: jobs: backup: uses: drsamonline/backup/.github/workflows/backup.yml@main with: keep: 100 # optional max_mb: 800 # optional secrets: BACKUP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BACKUP_TOKEN }} ``` One secret, **`BACKUP_TOKEN`**, is required: a token with `contents: write` on the dumps repositories and `contents: read` on the source repository. (`GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped to a single repository, so it cannot write to the dumps repo.) Run it by hand too: ```bash GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --repo drsamonline/ml-kit --ref main GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --repo drsamonline/forge --ref main --dumps dumps --keep 100 ``` ## Read this before you make the dumps repo public **A dumps repository holds your source code.** If *any* repository you back up is private, its dumps must be private too — a public dumps repo would publish that code. `backup.py` therefore creates new dumps repos **private by default**; pass `--public` only when every source repository is already public. ## The options | flag | default | what it does | |---|---|---| | `--repo` | — | the source repo, `owner/name` | | `--ref` | the default branch | the ref to snapshot — pass the **PR base** to capture the pre-merge state | | `--dumps` | `dumps` | the dumps repo name | | `--owner` | the source owner | who owns the dumps repo | | `--keep` | `100` | backups kept per repository; the oldest beyond it are deleted | | `--max-bytes` | `800 MB` | the dumps repo size cap before rolling to a new repo | | `--public` | off | create new dumps repos public (read the warning above) | | `--restore-test` | — | do not back up: unpack one dump and compare it with the commit it holds | | `--at` | the newest | with `--restore-test`, which snapshot to restore | | `--manifest` | — | do not back up: regenerate the dumps repo's `manifest.json` from its tree | ## The manifest is derived, not written by hand `/manifest.json` is regenerated from the dumps repository's own tree — after every backup, and on demand: ```bash GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --manifest --dumps dumps ``` It was hand-written once, on the store's first day, and never again: it went on claiming one repository was backed up while the store held 78. A derived index cannot drift, and if it is wrong then the tree it was derived from is wrong too. It is verified on the way in exactly as a dump is — the stored blob sha is compared with the sha of the bytes written — and a manifest that cannot be written **fails the run**, because a derived index allowed to go stale quietly is the defect this replaces. The one thing it does not record is the commit each dump holds. That is inside the tarball; `--restore-test` reads it. ## Proving a backup can actually be restored A backup that ran is not a backup that restores. This unpacks one dump and compares it, file for file, with the commit the dump names — every file's git blob sha against the repository's own tree at that commit. It exits 0 only on an exact match: ```bash GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --restore-test --repo drsamonline/forge GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --restore-test --repo drsamonline/forge --at 2026-10-27T124846Z ``` ``` read 0.69 MB; the API's stored blob sha is 81bbcaf0af unpacks clean (gzip CRC verified): 349 files, taken at 57d64d93c932 PASS EXACT RESTORE - 349 files match drsamonline/forge@57d64d93c932 file for file ``` It also fails on a truncated dump, on a dump whose top directory names a different repository, and on a tree GitHub truncated — an incomplete comparison is never a pass. Run it from the workflow by dispatching `backup` with `restore_test: true`. ## Verified ``` python3 tests/test_backup.py 50 passed, 0 failed ``` The tests cover the decisions that must be right — rotation keeps the newest N and deletes the oldest, the timestamp sorts chronologically, and a **full dumps repo rolls over to a new one**. Disabling rotation makes **4** of them fail. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence MIT.
