--- ## 🆕 What's new in 4.6.2 **Cross-audit with [neon-runner](https://github.com/drsamonline/neon-runner), and two things adopted from it.** - **The next frame is scheduled before any work runs.** neon-runner has always done this; it's a stronger guarantee than scheduling afterwards, because the following frame is booked even if the error guard itself fails. - **Pad opacity**: a `FADE` button in the pad editor cycles 100% → 70% → 45%, so the on-screen controls can stop covering the play area. The audit also confirmed what neon-runner does *not* need: it has no undefined-variable bugs (the class that froze Eon for two releases), and it already wraps text by measured width. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.6.1 **Cutscene and perk text now stays inside its panel.** Text was wrapped by *character count*, which is only correct for one font size in one panel width — on a 220 px portrait view a 26-character line is wider than the dialogue column, so it ran past the panel edge. Both now wrap by measured pixels. The cutscene panel is also anchored inside the play band rather than straddling into the letterboxed ground, and the three perk cards **stack full width on a phone** instead of being squeezed into ~49 px columns.
 
## 🆕 What's new in 4.6 **A HUD that reads, and pickups that show what they are.** - The HUD is **one panel**, sized to its own content: hearts, power gauge, grenades, lives and the weapon, instead of five things scattered across three corners — with the weapon chip no longer clipped against the bottom edge. - **Lives and combo used to both render as `X2`.** Lives now has its own glyph and row. - **Pickups have icons**: a rifle silhouette, a diverging fan for spread, three stacked rounds for machine, a sparked beam for laser, a teardrop for flame — and each box takes the weapon's colour, so it says which gun before you read anything. - Hearts are solid rather than thin outlines; foreground silhouettes are a tint with a rim instead of 82% black shapes that read as holes in the ground; the boss bar no longer overflows the portrait view. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.5.1 **Hotfix — the game froze the first time you got hit.** `playerHurt` referenced a variable that didn't exist (a mistake from the AEGIS perk in 4.4), so the first hit threw, and the throw killed the animation loop: a permanent freeze on the last rendered frame. Fixed. Two structural changes came out of the audit: **the animation loop can no longer die** — the whole frame is wrapped and the next frame is always scheduled, so any future error costs one frame instead of the game — and **endless mode no longer opens on the campaign cutscene**, which had been stopping the first wave from spawning. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.5 **LAN co-op.** Two players, same Wi-Fi, no internet, no accounts. ```bash node server.js # prints the address to open on both machines ``` Both players open the printed URL, player one picks **HOST**, player two picks **JOIN**. It runs on [`lan-kit`](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit) (SSE + POST, zero dependencies). It is **lockstep**: both machines run the same seeded simulation and exchange only 9-bit input masks per frame, with a 12-frame delay line. No world state is ever sent — which works because the simulation was already deterministic and the replay system had already proven that masks reproduce a run exactly. Verified with two independent headless browsers against a real host: same frame, same score, same position for both players, frame delta 0. **Honest limits.** In this 2-core sandbox a two-browser session without LAN runs at 30 fps and with LAN at roughly 8–17 fps — lockstep is correct but lossy under CPU and round-trip pressure. I have not been able to measure it on real hardware over a real Wi-Fi LAN, so I can't promise a smooth 60. Pause is disabled in LAN (it would desync) and cutscenes are skipped. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.4 **A perk after every era.** Eight of them, one pick from three, and the run gets shaped by your choices instead of just getting longer.
| Perk | Effect | | :-- | :-- | | **Overcharge** | all weapons hit 25% harder | | **Rapid** | weapons cycle 20% faster | | **Vitality** | +1 max health, and a full heal now | | **Scavenger** | +1 grenade capacity, and 2 in hand | | **Momentum** | the power gauge fills 35% faster | | **Phantom** | dash recovers 35% sooner | | **Aegis** | take 20% less damage | | **Reserve** | +1 life | They stack, they are never offered twice, and they carry across every era — so a run that picked Overcharge three times plays differently from one that took Aegis and Vitality. ## 🆕 Earlier releases - **4.3** — the touch pad layout editor: drag and resize both clusters, remembered per device. - **4.2** — three new bosses: The Drowned Relay, Orbit Wreck, The Last Second. - **4.1** — per-era weather, one jump button, every heading auto-fits the screen. - **4.0** — three more eras, story cutscenes with an in-engine renderer, power gauge and combo, controls rebuilt around auto-fire, a credit roll. - **3.1** — Windows EXE and Android APK built by CI through `app-builder`, a redesigned landing page, a separate demo page. - **3.0** — endless mode: escalating waves, a boss every fifth wave, a rising score multiplier. - **2.8** — auto-fire, on by default on touch, with a wider portrait view. - **2.7** — every menu tappable, pause as a real menu. - **2.6** — rebindable controls, per player, persisted. Full detail for every version is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## 🆕 What's new in 2.3 **74% fewer draw operations per frame** — 2,210 down to 573, measured by counting canvas calls rather than trusting a stopwatch. Same pixels, a quarter of the work. - **Ground is baked, not redrawn.** Each stage's floor, speckles and props are rendered once into 1024 px chunks and blitted from there. The live path is still in the file behind `?legacyground=1` so the two can be compared — the baked version matches it to within one pixel on 0.24% of pixels (sub-pixel rounding at chunk edges). - **Text is cached.** Every HUD string used to be drawn as dozens of `fillRect` glyphs each frame; now each unique string is rendered once into a tiny canvas and blitted. That alone was 1,400 of the 2,210 operations. - **Broad-phase bullets** skip enemies they cannot reach before doing box maths. - **A seed you can pin.** `?seed=4242` makes a run reproducible end to end — cosmetic randomness now routes through the seeded stream too, which is the groundwork for replays. - **A frame meter.** `?fps=1` overlays fps, frame ms and entity counts; `?bench=600` times 600 update+render pairs and prints the average into the title bar. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 2.2 **Bosses fight back with three attacks each, on their own clocks** — not one scripted loop.
- **The Warden** now drops **ceiling debris** on your position — three rocks (five in phase 2), each telegraphed for 42 frames by a shadow on the ground and a falling marker line, so you always know exactly where not to stand. - **The Glacier Wraith** summons **swarm darts** on its own timer, separate from its ice-shard fan. Kill them or eat them. - **The Eon Heart** fires **rotating beams** — a 70-frame dashed telegraph, then a live beam that sweeps across the arena for 150 frames. Phase 2 sends two, counter-rotating.
**A weak point that rewards aiming.** The Warden's core takes **double damage** — a body shot does 4, a core shot does 8, with a `CORE` popup when you find it. Bosses are no longer a matter of holding fire at the biggest rectangle on screen. Every hazard is a real entity with its own telegraph, damage box and lifetime, so they work in co-op too and can be dodged with the dash's i-frames. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 2.1 **Two players, one screen.** Press **2** on the title screen. Player one takes the arrows and `Space`/`Z`; player two takes `WASD` and `,` `.` `/` `;` `'`. Two gamepads also work — the second pad becomes player two automatically.
- **Shared camera** frames both players and follows their midpoint. - **Soft leash** — wander too far and you are nudged back toward your partner at 3 px a frame. No teleporting, no rubber-banding snap. - **Revive instead of death.** Go down and you have six seconds; a partner standing close for about a second brings you back at one heart. If nobody reaches you, you bleed out. - **A life is only lost when nobody is left standing** — both down means the run restarts at the last checkpoint together. - Enemies, turrets and bosses all target **whichever commando is nearest**, and contact damage is checked against both. Also in this release: the **brute's shoulder charge** is now telegraphed and on a 150-frame cooldown instead of firing whenever it is close, and **downed players no longer fall through the floor** (they were unreachable, so revive could never trigger). --- ## 🆕 What's new in 2.0 **New verbs.** **Dash** (Shift) with i-frames and a 42-frame cooldown, **melee** (V) — a short arc that finally solves "enemy standing on top of me" — and **grenades** (G), three per life, thrown with an arc, bouncing, five-damage in a 42-pixel radius. All three have touch buttons. **Four new enemy archetypes.** **Sniper** paints a laser sight on you for 42 frames before firing. **Swarm** darts fly straight at you. **Brute** is armoured, heavy and shoulder-charges. **Shielder** carries a front plate that stops your fire dead — you have to flank or jump it. **Telegraphs.** Every shooter now winds up for 16–42 frames before it fires, with a visible cue, so a death is something you could have read. **Hit-stop.** Three frames of frozen world on melee and grenade hits — the world stops, you do not, so a press during the freeze is never swallowed. **Difficulty tiers.** Recruit (6 hearts, 5 lives, half damage), Commando (as before), Eon (2 hearts, 1 life, 1.5× damage taken, tougher enemies). **A settings screen** (O or from pause): difficulty, colour scheme, reduce motion, flash intensity, HUD size, music, sound effects, auto-fire. Every option persists. **Accessibility.** Three colour schemes including deuteranopia and high contrast, which recolour hostile fire — the thing that actually matters in a bullet-hell moment. Reduce-motion kills shake, flashes and scanlines. Flash intensity is a slider, for photosensitivity. **Local leaderboard and lifetime stats** — top five runs on the title screen, runs/kills/time kept in `localStorage`. **Installable.** A service worker and manifest ship alongside the game: install it once and it launches with the network off. Sharp pixels on retina via a DPR-aware backbuffer, plus fullscreen (F) and a screen Wake Lock while you play. --- ## 📱 On a phone
  
**The canvas fills 100% of the screen in both orientations**, measured at 390×844, 360×640, 412×915, 768×1024, 844×390, 640×360 and 1440×810. Landscape keeps the 16:9-to-21:9 view and fills the screen edge to edge. Portrait switches to a **square logical view (270×270)** — a 16:9 band on a phone held upright is only a quarter of the screen and the sprites end up tiny. The canvas then takes the full screen height, the play area sits at the top where your eyes are, the earth continues below it with strata and grit, and the thumb pads overlay that lower band so nothing is wasted. The play area is 78% larger than it was in 1.2 (219 px tall → 390 px on an iPhone), and the title and settings screens reflow for the narrow view instead of overflowing. If you want the widest possible view, rotate: landscape shows 584 world pixels of width against portrait's 270. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 1.2 - **Phone support, properly.** The canvas is now `position:fixed; inset:0` and owns the viewport. On a 390×844 phone the game used to be a 215-pixel band floating in page padding with a desktop keyboard hint beneath it; it now fills the screen in landscape and lays out as band-plus-thumbs in portrait. - **Pause moved out of the play area** — bottom centre in landscape, a thin strip at the top in portrait, so it never covers the game. - **Visual-viewport sizing** — the layout listens to `visualViewport` resize and scroll, so the address bar collapsing no longer leaves the game mis-scaled. - **Whole-number scale snapping** when it costs less than 12% size, for crisper pixels. - Desktop keyboard hint now fades after nine seconds instead of sitting over the game. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 1.1 - **Curved, hand-drawn sprites.** Every character was rebuilt from stacked rectangles into rounded caps, arcs, ellipses and bezier limbs — helmets, visors, shoulders, knees and boots all have real silhouettes now, while the game stays pixel-pure on the 480×270 grid. - **Enemy variation.** One rig, many looks: each era reskins the same enemy silhouette (ember → frost → core), spawns get ±6% scale jitter, and roughly one in eight is an **elite** in gold with ~1.8× health. - **Widescreen.** The logical viewport follows your window's aspect ratio from 16:9 up to 21:9, so ultrawide and 16:10 screens fill properly instead of letterboxing. Boss arenas keep a fixed 16:9 footprint and the camera centres them, so a wide screen sees the walls rather than the void. - **Readability pass.** Enemy bullets got dark rims, glow and motion trails; screen-edge arrows point at enemies you cannot see; the background dims 18% during boss fights. - **Better feel.** Corner correction — you now slide around a ledge instead of bonking your head on it — plus rounded platforms and ground edges that no longer read as knife cuts. --- ## Contents - [Play it](#-play-it) — **[live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/eon-commando/play/)** - [Screenshots](#-screenshots) - [Why it is interesting](#-why-it-is-interesting) - [Controls](#-controls) - [The three eras](#-the-three-eras) - [Weapons](#-weapons) - [Enemies and bosses](#-enemies-and-bosses) - [How it works](#-how-it-works) - [Project layout](#-project-layout) - [Build and test](#-build-and-test) - [Roadmap](#-roadmap) - [License](#-license) --- ## ✨ Why it is interesting - **One file, no network.** `index.html` is the game. No CDN, no fetch, no `localStorage` requirement — high scores simply save if storage is available. - **No assets at all.** Every sprite is drawn from rectangles and paths at runtime. Every sound is synthesised from oscillators and noise buffers. The HUD font is a 5×7 bitmap defined as strings. - **Manual fire, classic rules.** No auto-aim, no regenerating health. Four hearts, three lives, and you lose your weapon when you die — back to the rifle. - **Coyote time and jump buffering.** Six frames of coyote time, seven of buffered input, variable jump height. It feels like a 16-bit game, not a web demo. - **Three stages, three bosses, two phases each.** Half health changes the fight: wider spreads, summoned drones, faster spirals. - **Fixed 60 Hz simulation.** An accumulator drives physics, so a 144 Hz monitor does not make the commando run faster. - **Touch and keyboard, same code.** On-screen pads appear only on touch devices; gamepads work through the Gamepad API. --- ## 🎮 Controls | Action | Keyboard | Touch | Gamepad | | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | | Move | `←` `→` / `A` `D` | Left D-pad | D-pad / left stick | | Aim up | `↑` / `W` | D-pad up | D-pad up | | Aim down (mid-air) | `↓` / `S` | D-pad down | D-pad down | | Duck | `↓` while standing | D-pad down | D-pad down | | Jump | `Space` `X` `K` | **A** | A / cross | | Fire | `Z` `J` `Ctrl` | **B** | X / square | | Dash | `Shift` `L` | **»** | RB / R1 | | Melee | `V` `C` | **M** | X / square | | Grenade | `G` `B` | **G** | B / circle | | Settings | `O` | from pause | — | | Daily run | `D` (title) | — | — | | Unleash | `E` | ⚡ (when ready) | Y / LB | | Jump (auto-fire on) | `↑` or `Space` | ▲ | A | | Duck (auto-fire on) | `↓` | ▼ | down | | Rebind keys | `O` → Controls | — | — | | Watch last run | `R` (title) | — | — | | Fullscreen | `F` | — | — | | Pause / menu | `P` `Esc` | ❙❙ button | Start | | **Player 2** | `WASD` + `,` `.` `/` `;` `'` | — | second pad | | Mute | `M` | — | — | Hold jump for the full arc, tap it for a short hop. Aiming is eight-directional: hold a direction while firing. --- ## 🕰 The three eras | # | Era | Setting | Boss | | :-: | :-- | :-- | :-- | | I | **ASHEN DAWN** | The burning city at dusk — long sightlines, chasms, rooftop turrets | **THE WARDEN** | | II | **GLACIER EON** | The frozen vault — narrow ledges, more air than ground, drone swarms | **GLACIER WRAITH** | | III | **EON CORE** | The heart of time — tight platforms, dense fire | **THE EON HEART** | Each stage is hand-laid: ground segments with real chasms, one-way platforms, checkpointed respawns, and an arena at the end where the camera locks and the gate shuts behind you. --- ## 🔫 Weapons | Weapon | Cadence | Damage | Behaviour | | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | | **RIFLE** | medium | 1 | Default. Always with you, always reliable. | | **SPREAD** | slow | 1 ×3 | Three pellets in a fan. | | **MACHINE** | very fast | 1 | Jittery, forgiving, melts anything static. | | **LASER** | slow | 3 | Punches through three targets. | | **FLAME** | fastest | 1 | Short reach, wide cloud, burns through crowds. | Pickups float in capsules: **weapons**, **repair** (2 hearts) and **Eon shards** (+500). A fatal hit drops you back to the rifle — the classic run-and-gun tax. --- ## 👾 Enemies and bosses | Enemy | Behaviour | | :-- | :-- | | **Grunt** | Patrols, stops to shoot, reverses at ledges | | **Runner** | Charges when it sees you, leaps the gaps | | **Drone** | Hovers on a sine wave, drifts over your head, drops bombs | | **Turret** | Fixed, tracks you, fires aimed shots | | **Jumper** | Hops toward you, shoots mid-leap | | Boss | Phase 1 | Phase 2 (below half health) | | :-- | :-- | :-- | | **The Warden** | Walks the arena, 3-way spread, ground shockwave | 5-way spread, faster cadence, quicker stomps | | **Glacier Wraith** | Flies, aimed bursts, fan of ice shards | Calls in drones, wider shard fan | | **The Eon Heart** | Four-armed spiral, aimed volley | Six-armed spiral, faster, summons runners | --- ## ⚙ How it works | System | Implementation | | :-- | :-- | | **Loop** | Fixed 1/60 s step with an accumulator; render once per animation frame | | **Rendering** | One 480×270 canvas, integer-scaled with `image-rendering: pixelated` | | **Art** | Rectangles and paths — the commando, enemies, bosses, skylines, props | | **Text** | A 5×7 bitmap font defined as `#`/`.` strings, drawn pixel by pixel | | **Audio** | Web Audio: square/saw/triangle oscillators, noise buffers, a look-ahead sequencer | | **Music** | Per-era tracks — bass, lead and noise drums — scheduled against the audio clock | | **Input** | One action set merged from keyboard, pointer pads and the Gamepad API | | **Camera** | Lerped horizontal follow, clamped to the stage, locked during boss fights | | **Save** | `localStorage` for high score and mute, wrapped so private mode never throws | ### Zero dependencies There is no `package.json` to install, no bundler, no framework, and no asset pipeline. The shipped `index.html` makes **no network requests of any kind** — not for fonts, not for images, not for analytics. Load it once, unplug the network, keep playing. --- ## 🗂 Project layout ``` eon-commando/ ├── index.html ← the game (built, self-contained, ~243 KB) ├── build.py ← src/ → index.html ├── src/ │ ├── 00_head.html ← document, CSS, touch pad markup │ ├── 10_core.js ← constants, maths, storage, URL params │ ├── 20_audio.js ← chiptune synth + the era tracks │ ├── 30_input.js ← keyboard / touch / gamepad, canvas scaling │ ├── 40_art.js ← 5×7 font, the commando, enemies, bosses │ ├── 50_content.js ← weapons, enemy stats, the three stages │ ├── 60_entities.js ← physics, AI, bullets, particles, boss patterns │ ├── 70_game.js ← state machine, stage flow, camera, scoring │ ├── 80_render.js ← parallax eras, world, HUD, screens │ ├── 90_main.js ← canvas setup, fixed-step loop, demo harness │ └── 99_tail.html └── docs/ ← GitHub Pages root ├── index.html ← landing page ├── play/index.html ← the game, served live └── shots/*.png ← screenshots ``` --- ## 🛠 Build and test The build is a concatenation — no toolchain, no dependencies, Python 3 only: ```bash python3 build.py # src/ -> index.html python3 tests/test_index_page.py # the build is reproducible, and / is served ``` That is the entire build. The test is there because `index.html` is the product, not a page: on 2026-11-05 a bulk page sweep deleted it and nothing failed, so the download link 404'd and `node server.js` answered `/` with "not found". To check a change without opening a browser, the game exposes a deterministic demo harness through URL parameters: ```bash # 400 simulated frames of era I, then freeze the frame index.html?shot=1&stage=1&demo=400 # drop straight into a boss fight index.html?shot=1&stage=3&warp=2520&demo=320&right=0 ``` `?demo=N` runs N fixed steps with scripted input, `?warp=X` teleports the commando, `?shot=1` strips the page chrome for screenshots, and `?debug=1` writes the game state into the document title. Every screenshot in this README was captured with those flags in headless Chromium. --- ## 🗺 Roadmap ### Shipped - [x] Six eras with distinct palettes, hazards and parallax - [x] Five weapons, nine enemy archetypes, three bosses with second phases and arena hazards - [x] Dash, melee and grenades; hit-stop; attack telegraphs - [x] Chiptune music and sound effects, synthesised at runtime - [x] Keyboard, touch pads and gamepad, with rebindable keys per player - [x] Two-player local co-op with revive - [x] Difficulty tiers, settings, colour schemes, reduce-motion, HUD scaling - [x] Curved sprite art, per-era palettes, scale jitter, elite variants - [x] Widescreen 16:9 → 21:9; portrait fills the screen with a closer view - [x] Readability pass: bullet rims and trails, threat arrows, background dimming - [x] Performance: 573 draw ops/frame, down from 2,210 - [x] Replays (196 chars for 900 frames) and a daily seed - [x] Auto-fire with a ±31° assist, on by default on touch - [x] Installable PWA, offline, zero dependencies ### Next, in order - [x] **Endless mode** — escalating waves, boss every fifth wave, rising multiplier - [x] **Touch pad layout editor** — drag the pads anywhere, resizable, persisted - [x] **Perks between eras** — 8 perks, one pick from three after each era, stacking - [ ] **Android APK / Windows EXE** via [`app-builder`](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) - [ ] **LAN co-op** via [`lan-kit`](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit) (SSE + POST, local host) - [ ] Optional CRT shader toggle --- ## 🤝 Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. # Feather

![Feather opening a comic](docs/assets/app-comic.png) **A read-only document viewer that opens before you blink.** Small, portable, cross-platform, summoned by a keystroke. No editing, no annotation, no cloud, no plugins. One window, one document, nothing else. [![CI](https://github.com/drsamonline/feather/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/feather/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-orange?logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [The plan](docs/plan.html) · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/feather/) · [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
--- ## Status This repository is at **M0 — the spike**. The engine path is being proven before any window code is written, because the plan's first question is not "does it look good" but "how long does it take to open a document and draw page one". | Piece | State | |---|---| | Format router (extension + magic bytes) | done, tested | | `Document` trait — the contract every format implements | done | | Byte-budgeted LRU tile cache | done, tested | | PDF pipeline (hayro, pure Rust, Apache/MIT) | done — renders real pages | | Image pipeline — one picture, one page | done | | Comic pipeline — CBZ, natural page order | done | | XLSX workbooks — grid, not pages | done | | DOCX documents — read as blocks, reflowed | done, approximate | | PPTX decks — text at the file's own coordinates | done, text only | | ODT / ODS / ODP — OpenDocument, same pipelines | done | | Six Office formats, three pipelines | docx/odt · xlsx/ods · pptx/odp | | PSD — the composite a layered file ends with | done, 8-bit RGB and greyscale | | CBR (RAR comics) | in-process, no helper needed — via the UnRAR decoder, see `LICENSE-UNRAR` | | EPUB pipeline — reflowed text, its own layout engine | done, first cut | | Text and Markdown — same engine, one file | done | | `feather` CLI — `info` and `render` | done — measures the budget | | Scroll model — page geometry, visible range, zoom anchoring | done, tested | | Window — open, fit to width, scroll, zoom, page | done — first light | | Tile cache in the draw path, render thread, stale-work cancellation | done | | Pages as a grid of tiles, with a raster ceiling for huge pages | done | | Session model — tabs, pinning, dedupe, per-tab reading position | done, tested | | Single instance — a second launch becomes a tab, not a window | done | | Tab strip — labels, active chip, click to switch | done | | Multiple windows | next | | Desktop integration — .desktop, registry, MIME candidates | done (Linux, Windows) | | Global shortcut — Ctrl+Alt+F summons the window | done | | Tray icon | deferred — see below | | EPUB, images, comics, Office read mode | later | | Desktop integration — .desktop, registry, MIME candidates | done (Linux, Windows) | | Global shortcut — Ctrl+Alt+F summons the window | done | | Tray icon | deferred — see below | | EPUB, images, comics, Office read mode | later | ## Try it ```sh cargo build --release ./target/release/feather info some.pdf ./target/release/feather render some.pdf 1 -s 2.0 -o page1.png ``` And the window itself: ```sh cargo run --release -p feather-app -- some.pdf ``` | Key | Does | |---|---| | `↓` `↑` / `PgDn` `PgUp` / wheel | scroll | | `←` `→` | previous / next page | | `+` `-` | zoom around the centre of the screen | | `1` | fit to width | | `Home` `End` | first / last page | | `]` `[` | next / previous tab | | drop a file on the window | open it (several files → several tabs) | | click a tab | switch to it | | `Ctrl+Alt+F` (anywhere) | summon the window | | `o` | open a document — the system picker, starting where you were | | `n` | open this document in a window of its own | | drag over text | select it (EPUB today) | | `c` | copy the selection | | `/` | search the document · `Enter` next · `Esc` closes | | `p` | pin or unpin the current tab | | `w` | close the current tab (refused if pinned) | | `Esc` `q` | quit | There is no toolbar. There is nothing on a toolbar. The window never rasterises. A worker thread owns the document and draws pages into a byte-budgeted cache; the window only blits what is already there, so a 400-page PDF scrolls without freezing and a fast flick drops the pages it has already left behind instead of queueing them. Text is selectable where a pipeline can say where the words are — drag to select, `c` to copy. EPUB can; PDF cannot yet, because hayro hands back a page image and extracting positioned words from it is the next piece of work. A viewer that pretends to select in a PDF it cannot read would be worse than one that does not. The tab strip is the only permanent chrome: one chip per document, the active one lit, a pin marked with `*`. Labels are drawn with the system's own sans face — fontdb finds it, fontdue rasterises it — so no font is embedded and the binary does not grow. Latin only for now; a real shaper is its own block. Open a second file while the viewer is running and it becomes a tab in the running window rather than a second window — the first launch owns a loopback port and later launches hand their path to it. Pinned tabs sort left and refuse to close. Tiles are keyed by document as well as page, so two tabs of the same PDF can never share a bitmap. Pages are cut into a grid of 512-pixel tiles, so the cache can evict a corner rather than a page. And a page whose raster would exceed 32 megapixels — a 20,000-pixel scan, a poster-sized vector drawing — is rendered at a lower rung of the zoom ladder and stretched on screen: you lose sharpness, not the process. `render` prints its own timings to stderr: ``` read 1.2 ms · open 0.4 ms · render 38.1 ms · total 39.7 ms page 1 of 412 · 1190×1684 px at 2.00x · 214633 bytes png → page1.png ``` A one-page fixture lives at `tests/fixtures/minimal.pdf`, and CI renders it on every push — so the first green build is proof that the engine works on Windows, Linux and macOS, not a claim in a README. Those four numbers are the project. §8 of the plan sets the ceiling: first page of a 50 MB PDF in under 150 ms, binary under 20 MB, cold start under 300 ms. CI prints the binary size on every push so the number cannot drift quietly. ## The shape of the code ``` crates/ feather-core/ Document trait · format router · tile cache · scroll model · session (zero dependencies) feather-pdf/ PDF pipeline on hayro (pure Rust) feather-image/ still images, CBZ and CBR — the last through UnRAR C++, the only C++ in the tree feather-text/ glyph rasterisation, shared by the window and the pipelines feather-epub/ reflowable text: strip, wrap, paginate (EPUB, Markdown, txt, DOCX) feather-sheet/ workbooks: XLSX read as a grid, one sheet to a page feather-slide/ decks: PPTX slides drawn at their own coordinates feather-cli/ the spike: info + render, with timings feather-app/ the window: winit + softbuffer + two font crates ``` `feather-core` has **zero dependencies** and does not know what a pixel looks like on screen. The UI will hold a `Box` and never match on a file extension again — that single rule is what stops a fourteen-format viewer from becoming fourteen special cases in the window code. Adding a format means one enum variant, one router arm, one `Document` impl, and one line in the `open_document` factory. Nothing else in the tree changes — `feather-image` was added to prove it, and the window did not learn what an image is. ## Why hayro and not MuPDF MuPDF would give more formats in one binary, but it is AGPL — the only such dependency in this estate, and awkward beside a licence whose point is a retained attribution. hayro is Apache/MIT, pure Rust, read-only by design, and cross-compiles to Windows ARM64 without a second machine. The cost is that EPUB reflow is ours to write. §12 of the plan argues this properly. **One exception, stated rather than buried:** `feather-image` compiles RARLAB's UnRAR C++ so that CBR opens without a helper installed. That is the only C in the tree, it means the workspace is no longer pure Rust, and it carries a non-OSI licence — see [LICENSE-UNRAR](LICENSE-UNRAR) and [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md). ## Picking up where you left off Close the window and the tabs, their pins and your place in each one come back next time. The file lives where the platform expects — `$XDG_STATE_HOME/feather` on Linux, `%APPDATA%\Feather` on Windows, `Application Support` on macOS — so an application installed read-only can still remember. A document that has since been deleted is dropped quietly rather than stopping the viewer from opening. ## Multiple windows `n` opens the current document in a window of its own, and `feather-viewer --new-window file.pdf` does the same from a shell. That is a second *process*, not a second window in the running one — the window state (surface, viewport, selection, cursor) is owned by the application rather than by a window, so an in-process second window is a refactor of all of it rather than a flag. The trade is explicit: a separate window pays for its own cache and render thread, and its global shortcut registration fails because the first process already holds the key. ## Summoning `Ctrl+Alt+F` from anywhere brings the window up — un-minimised, focused, on top. That is the honest version of "open the document selected in the file manager": no desktop exposes the shell's selection to a third party, so the shortcut raises the viewer and the path can be pasted or dropped into it. On Wayland the registration fails and Feather says so once, rather than silently doing nothing. **The tray icon is deferred, on purpose.** `tray-icon` needs GTK on Linux, which would pull a few hundred megabytes of development libraries into a build that currently needs none — for a status icon. The right Linux answer is a StatusNotifierItem over D-Bus (`ksni`), which is a self-contained piece of work rather than a dependency swap, and it is not in this milestone. ## Roadmap What is released, what is next, and what each thing is waiting on: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | https://ko-fi.com/matneo | | PayPal | https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN | | Books | https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc | | Everything else | https://drsamonline.github.io/ | | Email | sohilmomin2000@gmail.com | ## Format engines Why Office, slides, PSD and CAD are not in the viewer yet, which of the ArtCraft engines would change that, and what each costs: [docs/format-engines.md](docs/format-engines.md). ## Decisions The choices that were not obvious, and the evidence that settled them — shaping, PDF text, CBR, the tray, in-process windows — live in [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md). ## Your own typeface ```sh FEATHER_FONT=/path/to/YourFont.ttf feather-viewer document.pdf ``` The viewer sets a page in whatever face you name, instead of asking the system for one. A bad path prints what it could not read and falls back to a system face rather than leaving you with a blank page and no explanation. It exists for two reasons: a reader may prefer a different face, and a rendering test needs one fixed face — the same page scored 0% against a baseline rendered on one machine and 14% on another whose fonts differed, which is no way to run a regression check. ## Looking at it without a display ```sh feather-viewer --screenshot out.png document.pdf feather-viewer --screenshot page41.png --page 41 comic.cbr ``` `--page` is 1-based, like every page number a person says. Builds the frame through the same function the window uses — the surface is taken out of the application for the duration of a frame — and writes it as a PNG. No window, no display, so it works in a container. CI renders two screenshots on every push and keeps them as artifacts; a frame that comes out suspiciously small fails the build, because that is what a blank page looks like. ## Download Prebuilt binaries are attached to [releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/feather/releases): Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64 and macOS arm64, each with a SHA-256 beside it. The archives contain the single binary, the licence and this README — there is nothing else to install. ## Registering with the desktop ```sh packaging/linux/install.sh # ~/.local/bin + a .desktop entry ``` ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging\windows\install.ps1 ``` Both register Feather as a *candidate* for the formats it can open — PDF, EPUB, CBZ/CBR and images — and neither seizes the default. Choosing the default is the user's job, in their own settings, where they can also undo it. macOS is not automated yet; [packaging/macos/README.md](packaging/macos/README.md) says what a bundle would need and why notarisation is the real blocker. ## Read the plan first [docs/plan.html](docs/plan.html) — sixteen sections: the engine decision, the requirement ledger, the format matrix, Office and ODF in five honest tiers, the ecosystem sweep, the crate picklist, the performance budget, the audit log of what earlier drafts got wrong, and a triage of twenty reference projects. ## Licence MIT. The controls every app in this fleet hand-rolls — inputs, selects, a date picker, OTP boxes, uploads, checkboxes, switches, sliders, rating, toggles, colour pickers — with one API and one validation pass. ## Use it ```js var F = require("./form-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.Form var name = F.input({ label: "Name", required: true }); document.body.appendChild(name.wrap); // label + control + help + error line name.value(); // read name.set("Ada"); // write, without firing a change name.on("change", fn); // listen F.bind(name, someSignal); // two-way with a ui-kit signal ``` ## What it does - **Text** — `input`, `textarea`, `password`, `search`, `number` (reads as a number or `null`), `date`, `datePicker` - **Choice** — `select`, `autocomplete` (type to filter, click to pick), `checkbox`, `switch`, `radioGroup`, `slider`, `rate`, `toggleGroup` (single or multiple), `otp` - **Wider** — `calendar` (Monday-first month grid, ISO dates), `upload`, `colorSwatches`, `colorPicker`, `imageSelect`, `editableText`, `hotkey` - **Layout** — `field` wrappers with label, help text, required marker and an error line wired by `aria-describedby`; `group` as a `fieldset`; `submitFooter` - **`F.validate(values, rules)`** — `required`, `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, and a custom `validate` that returns `true` or a message. Errors are messages, because the message is what the user has to read - **`F.showErrors(controls, result)`** — paints those messages onto the controls and sets `aria-invalid` - **`F.values(controls)`** — collect a named set of controls into one object - **`F.bind(control, signal)`** — two-way binding to anything callable with `.update()`, so `ui-kit` stays optional rather than a dependency Every control returns the same shape — `el`, `wrap`, `value()`, `set()`, `on()`, `disable()`, `invalid()` — so a form can be built, validated and reset without special-casing any of them. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 108 passed, 0 failed ``` The tests run against a small DOM written inside `test-node.js` (createElement, appendChild, setAttribute, addEventListener, dispatch), so the kit exercises the same code paths in Node that it does in a page. The measured case for it: date pickers appear in 18 files across 5 sampled apps, checkboxes and switches in 14 files across 5, sliders in 2. This kit is the whole transfer path: it **moves bytes** (a systematic LT fountain code) and **wraps them** (a self-describing 22-byte header with two CRCs). It absorbed `optical-kit` on 2026-11-12, which carried the encoder and a second, incompatible 17-byte frame beside this one — two definitions of "a self-describing frame" used by the same three apps (`helioprism`, `blinkcode-ai`, `BLINKTRANSFER`), drifting apart. ## What it gives you - **A 22-byte self-describing header** — magic, version, transferId, k, blockSize, totalLength, a payload CRC-32, the symbol id, and a header CRC-16. A receiver can lock onto *any* frame, mid-stream, with no separate header code. - **Strict validation of untrusted input** — a decoded frame is bytes from a camera; a corrupt or crafted header is dropped, not allowed to allocate. - **A rateless `FountainCollector`** — absorbs symbols in any order, tolerates duplicates, restarts when the transfer id changes, and verifies the payload checksum when it assembles. - **Byte/checksum utilities** — CRC-16/CCITT, CRC-32, a seeded PRNG, XOR/concat helpers and size formatting. ## Use it Drop `frame-kit.js` next to your code and load it, then use the global `Frame`: ```html ``` The collector sits over a fountain decoder (the codec lives in `optical-kit`). Pass the decoder factory, or omit it to use `optical-kit`'s decoder if it is loaded: ```js const rx = new Frame.FountainCollector(LTDecoder); // your decoder rx.add(Frame.parse(bytes, { magics: [0xb7] })); rx.progress; // 0..1 rx.assemble(); // Uint8Array, checksum verified — or throws ``` ## API | | | |---|---| | `Frame.pack(opts)` | Build a frame from `{ magic?, transferId, k, blockSize, totalLength, payloadCRC\|checksum, symbolId, data }`. | | `Frame.parse(bytes, opts?)` | Parse and validate; `opts` = `{ magics?, label? }`. # Helioprism ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **One app. Two kinds of light.** Move a file between two devices using only a screen and a camera — no network, no cables, no pairing. Helioprism carries the same rateless frame stream over **two physical transports** and picks the right one for the job. [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-7c3aed)](LICENSE) [![Commercial licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/commercial-licence%20available-22c55e)](COMMERCIAL.md) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/drsamonline/helioprism)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/commits) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/helioprism)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/stargazers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/drsamonline/helioprism/total)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/releases) [![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-06b6d4)](https://drsamonline.github.io/helioprism/play/) **[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/helioprism/play/)**  ·  **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/helioprism/)**  ·  **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/releases/latest/download/helioprism-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/releases/latest/download/helioprism.apk)
--- ## The two transports | | **QR** | **SpectraCode** | |---|---|---| | Physical layer | monochrome QR modules | 36-colour cells, 5 bits each | | Per frame | ~1.4 KB | ~5.1 KB | | Strength | any camera reads it; any scanner reads a tiny file | far more capacity per frame | | Best for | small files, cheap optics, maximum compatibility | larger files | Both carry the **same** frame format and the **same** rateless fountain stream, so a missed frame costs one more symbol rather than a whole loop. The magic byte in each frame says which layer carried it, so the receiver **auto-detects** — point one receiver at either code and it works. ## How it works ``` files ─▶ container ─▶ fountain symbols ─▶ frames ─▶ QR or colour matrix │ files ◀─ container ◀─ collector ◀─ frame ◀─ camera ─┘ ``` - **Selection engine** — auto-picks QR for small payloads and the colour transport for large ones, or you choose. - **Compatibility mode** — a small text file can go out as one plain QR that any third-party scanner reads. - **Offline-first PWA** — installable; after first load it never touches the network. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism.git cd helioprism npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm test # both transports, end to end npm run build # production bundle into docs/play/ ``` Open the dev URL on both devices (or install the PWA). On one, **Send** and pick files; on the other, **Receive** and point the camera. ## Project layout ``` src/ index.html styles.css main.js sw.js transports/ index.js registry + selection engine qr.js QR transport (monochrome) spectra.js SpectraCode transport (colour) lib/ container.js shared multi-file container fountain.js shared LT fountain codes frame.js shared frame format + collector (per-transport magic) qr/ QR encode (qrcode-generator) / decode (jsQR) spectra/ arithmetic coder, match model, Reed-Solomon, colour matrix, optical decoder workers/ optical decode worker for the colour transport tests/ frame, fountain, selection + both transport loopbacks tools/ build.mjs, dev.mjs, serve.js docs/ landing page + built demo (GitHub Pages) ``` ## Testing ```bash npm test ``` Both transports are tested end to end in Node: files → the transport's real `render()` (into a mock canvas) → pixels → the transport's `decodeFrame()` → collector → files. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence Helioprism is **free for personal, academic, hobby and non-profit use** under the [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](LICENSE). **Commercial use needs a paid licence** — see [COMMERCIAL.md](COMMERCIAL.md). --- ## What this is A personal reflection app that runs entirely in your browser. You enter a name and a birth date once; it derives your numerology profile, your sun sign, today's lunar phase, and your biorhythm cycles, then keeps them on one screen you can open every morning. It is **not** a dashboard of tables. Every number is computed from your input rather than looked up from a hard-coded list, and the whole thing — stylesheet, scripts, icons, logic — fits in a single 193 KB file that works with the Wi-Fi off. ## What it is not Honesty is part of the product, so it is part of the README too. | It is | It is not | | --- | --- | | A reflective exercise with a vocabulary for things you half-know | A diagnosis or a medical device | | Arithmetic you can check by hand | Evidence — biorhythm in particular has failed validation since the 1970s | | A reason to notice your own energy | A prediction of your future | | Free and uncommercial | A prescription of anything, for anyone | There is no homeopathy content in this project. An earlier prototype carried a remedy table derived from birth-date arithmetic; it was removed in v2.0.0 because a date of birth cannot select a constitutional remedy, and because a tool that names suicidal ideation in its output must route people to a human, not to a protocol. ## Screens | | | | --- | --- | | **Today** — moon, biorhythm, your number | **Numbers** — power, personal year, name, personal days | | **Sky** — sun sign, 30-day chart, lunar calendar | **Couple** — two dates, one honest read | | **Oracle** — a card, not a prophecy | **Report** — one printable page |

Uses the native share sheet where the browser has one. - **Export as Markdown or RTF** — the whole reading as plain text. RTF opens in Word, Pages, LibreOffice and Google Docs; Markdown opens anywhere. No PDF, no binary format. - **Multiple profiles** — keep more than one person's dates on the same device. - **Printable report** plus a plain-text copy button, and a compact A5 card mode. - **Keyboard shortcuts** — `1`–`8` jump between screens. - **"Why this number?"** — the arithmetic behind your power number, shown on request. - **Backup and restore** as a JSON file you own. - **Installable PWA** with a service worker, and a single-file build for everything else. ## Privacy - **No network requests at runtime.** No fonts, no CDN, no analytics, no telemetry. You can verify it: open DevTools → Network, use the app, and watch it stay empty. - **One storage key** in `localStorage`, unencrypted, on your device. *Erase everything* in the Profile screen removes it. - **No account, no sync, no server.** There is nothing to sign up for because there is no backend. ## Install ### 1 · Web / PWA Open **[drsamonline.github.io/holistic/app](https://drsamonline.github.io/holistic/app/)** and use your browser's **Install** or **Add to Home Screen**. It caches itself and works offline afterwards. The landing page is at **[drsamonline.github.io/holistic](https://drsamonline.github.io/holistic/)**. # homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json

[![License: Free to use, attribution required](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Free%20to%20use,%20attribution%20required-yellowgreen)](LICENSE)

## Repertorium Publicum (2008) — complete, graded


![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)
`repertory/repertorium-publicum-2008/` holds a **complete, fully graded** open
repertory: **74,480 rubrics**, **735,460 remedy links**, **669 remedies**, 41 chapters.

Unlike the `kent-1897/` extraction, every remedy link carries a grade (1–3):

| grade | links |
|---|---|
| 1 | 465,287 |
| 2 | 198,591 |
| 3 | 71,582 |

Sourced from the [OOReP](https://github.com/nondeterministic/oorep) open repertory
database (repertory token `publicum`).

**Please note:** this is *not* Kent's 1897 first edition. It is *Repertorium Publicum*
by Vladimir Polony (2008), a Kent-derived repertory with its own chapter structure
(separate *Clinical*, *Appetite*, *Blood* and *Heart & Circulation* chapters) and its
own additions. It is licensed **GPL v3** as part of the OpenRep source code — not
public domain. See the dataset README for details.

## The Organon, in two editions

`treatise/` holds the *Organon of Medicine* as a **treatise** — numbered paragraphs, no
rubrics, no remedies — in both public-domain English translations:

| file | edition | translation | paragraphs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `organon-6th-1922.json` | sixth (completed 1842) | William Boericke, 1922 | 291 |
| `organon-5th-1849.json` | fifth (1833) | R. E. Dudgeon, 1849 | 294 |

Each paragraph carries its text, its printed footnotes, the source it was read from and
the fraction of its 12-letter sequences found verbatim in OCR scans of **that edition**
(median 0.976 for the sixth, 0.979 for the fifth; floor 0.60). The two are different
books — 74 paragraphs are worded differently and §292–§294 exist only in the fifth — and
they are kept as separate volumes, never merged.

## The public-domain collection

**70 volumes (1847–1932)** — 16 repertories, 6 materia medicas and 40 treatises:
**352,063 repertory rubrics**, **1,429,263 remedy links** of which **751,907 carry a
grade**, 39,770 materia medica symptoms and 5,392 sections of prose, every string verbatim
from its source.

Knerr's 1896 repertory (131,685 rubrics, 43 chapters) and Kent's 1897 are split by chapter
with an `index.json`; Gentry's concordance is split A-Z by concordance keyword, 25 files
plus `index.json`; the rest are single files. Each book carries a QC report under
`data/processed/<slug>/qc_report.md` with its verbatim-fidelity rate.

Two figures worth reading carefully, because they are not what they look like. **Kent's
1897 repertory is entirely ungraded** — 59,114 rubrics and 353,000 links, every grade null
— while the graded links come from Knerr and from Repertorium Publicum. And the totals in
`catalog.json` were recounted from the files themselves on 2026-11-04, having previously
omitted every split volume: remedy links were 613,588 short and rubrics 34,531 short.

no install, no build step, no server required to run. Sparked by
[Show HN: Bento](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49008211) and the
broader "single-file web app" (SFWA) niche (TiddlyWiki, Hyperclay, Decker,
and a growing list of GitHub projects tagged `single-file`).

Name: **iamsingle.app** (pun on "single-file app" / "I am single").

## What's here

```
index.html                          the site itself — build_pages.mjs inlines entries.json/stars.json/sizes.json into
                                     every generated page, so it's self-contained (works over file://, no fetch needed);
                                     falls back to fetching data/*.json if that inline data is ever missing

data/entries.json                   the directory's data — never touched directly by a submission PR, see below

package.json                        marks this a Node/Vercel project (api/submit.js needs it)
```

## How submissions merge without conflicting

Early on, every submission PR contained a full rewritten copy of
`data/entries.json` (the new entry appended to the end). That meant two
PRs open around the same time would both edit the same lines of the same
file — a textbook git merge conflict, every time, requiring the same
manual fix (rebuild the entry on top of current `main`, force-push,
re-merge) by hand.

Now a submission PR only ever adds one new file, `data/pending/{slug}.json`,
holding just that one entry. Two PRs can never collide, because they're
never editing the same file. The actual fold into `data/entries.json`
happens after a PR merges, via `promote-pending.yml` — it always reads
`data/entries.json` fresh off current `main`, appends the entry, and
deletes the consumed pending file. If two merges land close together, the
workflow's `concurrency` group queues the second run to start only after
the first finishes, so there's no race on the shared file either.

## How the site works

- Static, three files at runtime: `index.html` + `data/entries.json` +
  `data/stars.json`. No backend.
- **Star ranking + GitHub pill**: for entries with a `repo` field, star
  count and repo creation date come from `data/stars.json`
  (`{repo: {"stars": N, "created": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}`), a snapshot refreshed
  daily (and right after any merged submission) by the `snapshot-stars.yml` workflow
  (`scripts/snapshot_stars.py`, authenticated with the default
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` for a 5000/hr rate limit). The site does not call the
  GitHub API live per visitor — that was the original design and it
  doesn't scale past a handful of concurrent visitors sharing an IP. Each
  card shows a small pill with a GitHub icon (links to the repo), the
  star count, and the repo's creation month/year.
- **Sort options**: stars, "date created" (the repo's own GitHub creation
  date, from `data/stars.json`), "date added" (when the entry was added to
  *this* catalog, from each entry's `added` field), or name. `added` is
  stamped automatically by `api/submit.js` at submission time; entries from
  before this field existed keep whatever date was backfilled from git
  history when it was introduced.
- **Submission form**: POSTs directly to `api/submit.js`, which opens the PR
  itself via the GitHub API — see "Submission backend" below. A manual
  "file it as an issue" link is kept as a fallback if the API is down.
- **Featured badge**: an entry with a `featured` field
  (`[{"platform", "url", "title", "points"}]`) shows a badge next to its
  category tags. For `"platform": "Hacker News"` this renders as an
  orange HN-branded pill (Y mark, ▲ point count) linking to the thread;
  `points` is a static snapshot from when the entry was added, not
  live-refreshed — HN scores are effectively frozen once a story ages off
  the front page, so there's no daily-refresh job for this the way there
  is for stars. Other platform values fall back to a plain text badge.
  Nothing sets `featured` automatically — see `scripts/check_hn_featured.py`
  below for how a maintainer finds candidates to confirm.
- **Check badges**: each card shows `passed/total` from the entry's `checks`
  array, if present. Click the badge to expand the itemized pass/fail/skip
  list. Entries with no `checks` (hand-curated, never gone through a PR)
  show no badge — that's intentional, not a bug.
- **Detail pages**: clicking an entry's name goes to `/entry/{slug}` (a
  slugified version of its name) instead of straight to the live demo — a
  client-side view, still rendered by `index.html`, with a bigger header,
  Share/Visit buttons, stat cards (GitHub stars, created date, repo, security
  audit score), and the full checks list. `vercel.json` rewrites any
  `/entry/:slug` request to `index.html` so a hard refresh or a shared link
  works, not just in-app navigation. There's no server-side rendering, so a
  shared link's social-preview card falls back to the generic site-wide
  `og:image`/description, not per-entry content — the page itself renders
  correctly once loaded, this only affects unfurled link previews.

## Submission backend (`api/submit.js`)

A Vercel serverless function. Validates the form POST, then opens a PR
adding one new file under `data/pending/` directly via the GitHub API —
no GitHub account needed on the submitter's end, and no manual
issue→PR conversion by a maintainer. It still reads `data/entries.json`
once, read-only, to reject an obvious duplicate URL before opening the PR.

Needs one env var set on the Vercel project (not committed anywhere):

- **`GITHUB_BOT_TOKEN`** — a fine-grained PAT scoped to *only* this repo,
  with **Contents: write** and **Pull requests: write** permissions. Don't
  reuse a broad personal token here — this one lives in Vercel, not a CI
  job gated by manual review, so it should carry the least privilege that
  still works.

Also enforces a 100/day submission cap (`DAILY_SUBMISSION_CAP` in
`api/submit.js`), counted via GitHub's own PR history — no extra
infrastructure needed. Caps PR/branch spam from a public, unauthenticated
endpoint.

The heavier checks (`security_scan.py`: repo clone, `detect-secrets`,
`semgrep`) are *not* run here — too slow for a synchronous request. Those
still require a maintainer to manually run "Review submission" from the
Actions tab before merging. A honeypot field (`hp`) provides basic bot
resistance on top of the daily cap.

## How the review pipeline works

**Manually triggered** by a maintainer (Actions tab → "Review submission" →
Run workflow, entering the PR number) — not automatic on every incoming PR.
This is deliberate: the script below runs with `contents: write` /
`pull-requests: write`. Automatically checking out an untrusted PR's own
branch and running its scripts with that access is a classic GitHub Actions
"pwn request" — a submission PR could modify `scripts/*.py` itself and
exfiltrate the token. Instead the workflow always runs the scripts from the
base branch, and pulls only the PR's `data/pending/*.json` file(s) as plain
data via `git show` — the PR's own code is never checked out or executed.

Per pending entry:

1. **`collect_pending.py`** — gathers every `data/pending/*.json` file the
   PR added into a single list for the scripts below.
2. **`security_scan.py`** — heuristic only, not a guarantee:
   - if `repo` is set: shallow-clones it, runs `detect-secrets` (leaked
     credentials) and `semgrep` (`p/security-audit`, `p/javascript` rulesets).
     Only `ERROR`-severity semgrep findings that aren't explicitly
     low-confidence fail the check: `p/security-audit` is a high-recall audit
     ruleset meant to surface things for human review, so a raw finding count
     is noise rather than a verdict. Lower-severity hits are still counted in
     the check's detail text, so a noisy entry isn't presented as spotless.
   - always: fetches the live `url` (http/https only; internal/private hosts
     refused, and re-checked on every redirect hop) and regex-tests the raw
     HTML/JS for the literal presence of `eval(`, `new Function(`, decode→eval
     chains, decoded content written into the DOM, `sendBeacon` calls — these
     are presence checks on fetched text, not argument/taint analysis, so a
     `fail` means "found, needs a human look," not "confirmed dangerous"
   - a page over the 20 MB read cap is reported `skip`, never `pass` — a
     truncated body matches no patterns and would otherwise be
     indistinguishable from a clean result
   - each test reports `pass` / `fail` / `skip` individually — no prose summary
   - `scripts/test_security_scan.py` covers the above (`python3
     scripts/test_security_scan.py`, stdlib only)
3. **`merge_checks.py`** — writes the results into a `checks` array on the
   matching pending file (matched by `url`, not `name`, which isn't unique)
   and rewrites that `data/pending/*.json` file in place — never
   `data/entries.json` directly, see "How submissions merge without
   conflicting" above.
4. **`check_hn_featured.py`** — searches HN's free Algolia API
   (`hn.algolia.com/api`, no auth) for stories matching the entry's
   repo/URL/name. Common project names produce false positives (e.g.
   searching "Bento" also surfaces an unrelated Steam Deck keyboard), so
   results are only ever *candidates* in the PR comment — nothing writes
   to the entry's `featured` field automatically. A maintainer confirms a
   real match and adds it by hand.
5. The workflow commits and tries to push that change back to the PR branch
   — this only works for PRs from branches in this repo; `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't
   push to a fork's branch, so fork PRs rely on the PR comment instead.
6. A PR comment posts the same pass/fail list per entry, plus any HN
   candidates, for reviewers who don't want to open the diff.
7. Once the PR merges, `promote-pending.yml` folds the (now checks-annotated)
   pending file into `data/entries.json` and deletes it — see above.

### Known limitations worth reviewing

- `security_scan.py`'s pattern tests are regex-based and will miss anything
  even lightly obfuscated. Treat every `pass` as "nothing obvious found,"
  not "verified safe." `semgrep`/`detect-secrets` versions aren't pinned in
  the workflow — consider pinning once this is stable, so results don't
  shift silently on a tool update.
- GitHub's unauthenticated API rate limit (60/hr/IP) applies to the live
  star-ranking calls from visitors' browsers. Fine at current scale.
- The SSRF guard re-checks every redirect hop, but it validates a host by
  resolving it and then reconnects by name — so a DNS record that changes
  between those two steps (rebinding) could still slip through. Closing that
  means pinning the connection to the validated IP, which `urllib` can't
  express without reimplementing TLS hostname verification.
- Nothing re-scans an entry *automatically* after its PR merges. A live URL is
  checked once and never again, so a project that fixes its dependencies keeps
  its old verdict until someone asks for a re-check:

      node scripts/screenshot.mjs --refresh <slug>[,<slug>]   # re-measure some
      node scripts/screenshot.mjs --refresh-all               # re-measure everything

  That re-does the screenshot, size, QR eligibility and network profile for
  those entries, then `build_pages.mjs` regenerates their badges. A scheduled
  version still wants a guard against a network blip flipping a certified
  entry to failed — see the note on downgrades below.
- There's no check for whether an app phones home. `sendBeacon` is
  pattern-matched, but `fetch(`/`XMLHttpRequest`/WebSockets/remote
  `<script src>` are not, and regex is the wrong instrument for it anyway —
  intercepting requests in the headless browser that already loads every
  entry (`scripts/screenshot.mjs`) would be both more accurate and a more
  meaningful badge than anything in the current set.

## If you rename the site

Update in one pass:
- `<title>` and `.kicker` / `<h1>` text in `index.html`
- the wordmark text in `assets/logo.svg` (re-render `logo.png` after editing)
- `OWNER`/`REPO` constants at the top of `api/submit.js`, and the fallback
  issue link in `index.html`'s submit-section, if the repo name changes too

## Deploying

Needs Vercel (or another host that runs `api/*.js` as serverless functions)
— `api/submit.js` means this is no longer a pure static site. Set
`GITHUB_BOT_TOKEN` as a project env var (see "Submission backend" above)
before the submission form will work; the catalog itself renders fine
without it.

The test suite fails if a `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket` or `EventSource` appears in the file, or if an external script, stylesheet, font or image is added. | | 📤 **No silent uploads** | Files are read with `FileReader` and written with `Blob` and `a[download]`. There is no server to send them to. | | 📊 **No telemetry** | Nothing is counted, profiled or reported. | | 👤 **No account** | There is nothing to sign into. | | 🔗 **Almost no outbound links** | Exactly one page has them: Support, where Ko-fi, PayPal, the book store and the email address are links you may choose to click. The page loads none of them. | ## Where the tools came from Kitbox began as one file with 239 tools. It has grown in two passes, all rewritten to run inside this page: | From | Brought over | |:--|:--| | `export-kit` | Store-only ZIP writer (local headers, central directory, CRC32) | | `compress-kit` | GZIP compress and decompress over Compression Streams | | `crypto-kit` | AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-SHA256 keys; file encryption and sealed notes | | `astro-kit`, `app-panchang` | Julian day, Meeus solar and lunar longitude, Lahiri ayanamsa, tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana, rahu kaal, planetary hours | | `app-image-toolkit` | EXIF and GPS reading, and metadata stripping that leaves pixels untouched | | `ml-kit` | tf-idf keyword ranking and cosine similarity | | `TTB`, `All4ONE` | Statistics, regression, sig figs, fuel and electricity cost, pricing, savings, debt payoff, ULID, base32/base58, HMAC, MD5, CIDR, MIME, Markdown, config parsing, .gitignore, vCard, ICS, message links, tap tempo, meeting cost | ## Accuracy, honestly - 🌗 **The panchang** uses the Meeus solar and lunar series with an approximate Lahiri ayanamsa. Tithi and nakshatra boundaries land within roughly a minute of a published almanac; **they are approximations, and local tradition may differ.** The test suite pins the solar and lunar longitudes to the published Meeus worked examples. - 🩺 **Health, finance and science calculators** use standard public formulas. They are general-purpose tools, not professional instruments — nothing here is a substitute for medical, financial or legal advice. - 🔐 **MD5** is included for legacy checksums only. It is not collision-resistant and must never be used for passwords. - 🔑 **File encryption** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for Web Crypto, and a lost passphrase cannot be recovered. - 👟 **Shoe sizes and flight carbon** are rules of thumb. They compare choices; they do not fit a shoe or audit an airline. ## Tests ```bash npm ci npm test ``` 243 checks, run against the real file in jsdom: - every tool renders — 493 of them - tool ids and names are unique - all 50 routes resolve - the ported astronomy matches Meeus 25.b and 47.a; Delhi's midsummer sunrise and sunset land where they should - MD5, CRC32, base32 and base58 match their published check values - the new arithmetic is pinned: A4 at 300 DPI, 18% GST, molar volume at STP, projectile range, C1V1, GSM vs UCS-2 - the support page carries the real UPI id and an inline QR - user text is escaped, never parsed as markup - the file loads nothing external and calls nothing over the network ```bash node tools/check-badges.js # the badges above are checked against the app python3 tools/badges.py # redraw them if a number changes python3 tools/shots.py # retake the screenshots (needs chromium) ``` CI runs all of that plus: the badge numbers against the app, `ALL_TOOLS.md` and the landing page against the registry, `docs/` against the markdown, `MANIFEST.json` against the tracked files, the roadmap against the plan, a scan for `eval`/`new Function`/`document.write`/`javascript:` URLs, and a size budget. # Kosh

**The file workbench of the CHCE family.** Split, squeeze, archive, verify and inspect — one engine, a CLI and a local web UI. Where a CHCE engine is installed, Kosh drives it across a process boundary instead of reimplementing it. ```bash kosh engines # which CHCE engines are here, and their versions kosh scan photo.raw # would the engine help? answered from a sample kosh optimize photos/ --level 2 --strip # PNG/ZIP/GZIP/JPEG, losslessly smaller kosh pack project/ -o project.kosh # verified container kosh split backup.img --size 700M -o parts/ # parts that prove themselves kosh verify project.kosh # is it intact? (no extraction) kosh ui # the same engine in a browser ``` ![The Kosh interface](docs/screenshot.png) ## Where it sits in CHCE CHCE (Holistic Compression Sources) is a source vault (`HCS`), the native engine built from it (`ziptastic`), the orchestrator that chains binaries (`heavenzip`), and the coordinator (`compfactory`). Kosh is the **workbench**: the thing you point at a folder before and after the engine runs. It does not implement BWT, rANS or PPMd, and it will not pretend to — it does container-level work that the engine deliberately does not: | job | who does it | | --- | --- | | Strongest possible ratio on a payload | `ziptastic` (`.dr`), driven by `kosh pack --engine ziptastic` | | Chaining prebuilt binaries into a pipeline | `heavenzip` (`.hzpkg`), driven by `kosh pack --engine heavenzip` | | Re-compressing what is already compressed (PNG, ZIP, GZIP) | **Kosh** `optimize` | | Splitting, joining, archiving, verifying, inspecting | **Kosh** | A CHCE stream is recognised, not decoded: `kosh scan file.dr` reports the magic, version, original size and block count, and points at the decoder. Two tools that both claim the same magic would be worse than one that defers. ## What it is actually good at Format-aware, lossless re-compression. It parses the container, throws away the redundant encoding, and rebuilds it byte-identically. | case | before | after | cut | engine | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | PNG saved by a fast encoder | 113,356 | 31,170 | **72.5%** | zopfli | | Screenshot PNG, already level 6 | 4,344 | 3,727 | 14.2% | zopfli | | `notes.txt.gz` | 1,790 | 1,080 | 39.6% | zopfli | | ZIP of text, level 1 | 5,782 | 4,998 | 13.6% | zopfli | | JPEG with 4 KB of EXIF | 44,514 | 43,526 | 2.2% | strip | Pixels, archive entries, names, timestamps and order survive; only redundant encoding and (with `--strip`) metadata go away. Every row above is reproduced by `pytest` or by `kosh optimize` on the file described. ## Codecs, measured `kosh bench` generates a fixed corpus (seed 20261111) and runs every codec on the same bytes. This is the output, not a claim: | file | raw | gzip -9 | xz -9 | zip -9 | kosh zstd 19 | kosh brotli 11 | kosh lzma 9 | best | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | noise.bin | 1.00 MB | 1,000,328 | 1,000,108 | 1,000,426 | 1,000,471 | 1,000,445 | 1,000,545 | xz -9 | | prose.txt | 453.68 KB | 53,462 | 46,204 | 53,560 | 46,829 | 48,591 | 46,637 | xz -9 | | records.csv | 634.52 KB | 167,778 | 77,252 | 167,880 | 100,429 | 63,624 | 77,687 | kosh brotli 11 | | service.log | 2.62 MB | 267,951 | 115,948 | 268,053 | 136,998 | 109,521 | 116,386 | kosh brotli 11 | Brotli wins on records and logs; `xz` wins on prose. Kosh is a container and a codec choice, not a new entropy coder, and the table says so. The full run, with speeds, is in [`docs/FINDINGS.md`](docs/FINDINGS.md). ## What it is not - **A better `xz`.** On prose it is 1.4% behind, because it is calling the same LZMA2. Use `ziptastic` when the last percent matters. - **Fast at maximum.** Zopfli runs at roughly 20 KB/s on image data. Kosh uses it up to 1 MB of payload, then falls back to `zlib -9` and names the engine in the report. Level 3 overrides that up to 4 MB and can take a minute per image. - **Lossy.** It never re-encodes a photo. It removes redundant encoding, not data. - **A reader for `.dr` or `.hzpkg`.** It recognises the magic and defers to the engine that owns the format. - **Networked.** The web UI binds to `127.0.0.1`, uploads to a local session directory, and makes no outbound request. ## Install ```bash pip install -e . # core + CLI + web UI pip install -e ".[dev]" # + pytest, pillow kosh doctor # checks every codec with a live round-trip ``` Python 3.10+. Wheels on Linux, macOS and Windows: Typer, Rich, Zstandard, Brotli, Zopfli, NumPy, FastAPI, Uvicorn. ## Commands | | | | --- | --- | | `kosh optimize PATH…` | Re-compress PNG/GZIP/ZIP/JPEG losslessly. `--level 1–3`, `--strip`, `--dry-run`, `--backup`, `--jobs` | | `kosh pack PATH… -o FILE` | Container with a table of contents and per-entry SHA-256. `--codec zstd\|brotli\|lzma\|store`, `--engine ziptastic\|heavenzip` | | `kosh unpack FILE -o DIR` | Restore, verifying every entry. `--only PATH` | | `kosh split FILE --size 700M` | Parts plus a manifest. Also `--parts N` | | `kosh join PARTS -o FILE` | Reassemble and prove it matches the original | | `kosh archive create/list/extract` | zip, tar, tar.gz, tar.zst, tar.xz, .kosh | | `kosh verify FILE` | Integrity check without extraction (`--quick` for structure only) | | `kosh info FILE` | Header, manifest digest and physical block table | | `kosh scan FILE` | Real type by magic bytes, entropy, sample ratio; knows CHCE streams | | `kosh bench` | Reproducible comparison against gzip -9, xz -9, zip -9 | | `kosh doctor` | Installation self-check, including a round-trip | | `kosh ui` | Local web interface on 127.0.0.1:8765 | Every command takes `--json`. ## The container `.kosh` is a CHCE-family *container*, not a CHCE bitstream: its own magic, its own format, documented in [`docs/FORMAT.md`](docs/FORMAT.md). Blocks compress independently so packing and unpacking parallelise; the table of contents carries a manifest digest so damaged metadata is caught before it is trusted. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Where to read next | | | |---|---| | [`docs/ORIGINALS.md`](docs/ORIGINALS.md) | what the five Windows tools do, and what replaced them | | [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | how the engine is put together | | [`docs/FINDINGS.md`](docs/FINDINGS.md) | every measured number, and what was rejected | | [`docs/FORMAT.md`](docs/FORMAT.md) | the container, byte by byte | | [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md) | every planned enhancement, its exit test and its open decisions | | [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) | what each version changed | ## Licence MIT. lan-kit: # lan-kit [![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/lan-kit/) [![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) **The shared LAN core for drsamonline apps.** Zero dependencies. A local room with a real-time channel, for apps that run on a Wi-Fi network with **no internet**. The transport behind the LAN apps (`Chalk`, `Canteen`, `Blackboard`, `Rally`) — extracted from `HMS` so it isn't re-implemented per app. ## Why SSE + POST (not WebSocket) A WebSocket needs a framing library. Server-Sent Events and plain POST are built into every browser and Node, so a room needs **no dependencies at all**: - **server → clients:** `GET /events` (SSE) - **clients → server:** `POST /send` - **health:** `GET /health` ## Use it **Host (Node, zero deps):** ```js const { createHost } = require("./lan-host.js"); const host = createHost({ room: "canteen", app: "canteen", pin: "4821", history: 50 }); const port = await host.listen(0); // 0 = any free port host.onMessage((m, board) => console.log("got", m, "on", board)); host.broadcast({ hello: "room" }); // everyone host.broadcast({ line: "x" }, "board-2"); // one board host.snapshot("board-2", { doc: [] }); // catch a joiner up ``` **Client (browser):** ```js const c = Lan.client({ url: Lan.hostUrl(8080), board: "main", // optional: which board to join pin: "4821", // optional: the room's PIN onOpen: h => console.log("joined", h.room), onSnapshot: s => console.log("caught up", s.doc), onMessage: m => console.log("got", m) }); c.send({ from: "me", text: "hello room" }); c.send("a bare string is a message too"); ``` `Lan.roomCode()` makes a short code (no 0/O/1/I/L); `Lan.hostUrl(port)` builds the URL for the current LAN (and still works from `file://`, where there is no hostname); `Lan.health(url)` asks a host who it is; `Lan.scan()` looks for rooms on the subnet. ### Boards A client that names a board hears **that board plus the room-wide messages**. A client that names none hears everything — which is what every app already got, so nothing that worked before changes behaviour. `board` is routing, not content: it is stripped from the message before broadcast. ### The PIN Set `pin` on the host and every `POST /send` must carry it or it is refused with `403 {"ok":false,"error":"pin"}`. The client sends it automatically when given one. **The PIN never reaches the room.** It rides on every POST, so the host deletes it from the message before broadcasting — otherwise the secret is published to exactly the people it was meant to keep out. `/health` reports `pin: true` or `false`, never the value. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 42 passed, 0 failed ``` Covers the transport (listen, SSE connect, client count, POST broadcast, the hello event, the observer callback, the health endpoint, a clean close), boards (a message reaches its own board, not another, and reaches a client that named none), snapshots, the PIN (refused without it, refused with the wrong one, accepted with the right one, **and never broadcast**), and the client against a stubbed browser (a bare string becomes a text message, an object is sent as it is, the pin rides on every POST, `hostUrl` survives `file://`). `Lan.health` and `Lan.scan` are tested against real sockets, including a dead host, which must resolve to `null` rather than throw. The suite is mutation-tested: removing `delete msg.pin` turns 1 red, ignoring the board filter turns 1 red, and removing the pin check turns 4 red. ## What it is not Not a security boundary. The PIN keeps a stranger on the same Wi-Fi out of a room; it is not authentication, it is not encrypted, and it travels in clear text on the POST that carries it (which is why it is stripped before the broadcast, and why the host never echoes it). Anyone who can watch the network can read it. Do not send secrets over a LAN room. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. LEXORA

Layered EXact-text Repository & Adaptive compression architecture
Canonicalize text conservatively, then compress it with guaranteed byte-exact recovery — decode(encode(C)) == C for every input.
