Phase 1 prototype — no releases and no stable API yet; install from a source checkout. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 © 2026 Dr. Sohil Momin.

--- > **Project status: Phase 1 prototype in development.** Documentation (Batches A–E) complete/drafted; > early implementation code exists (canonicalization, Zstd core baseline, `.lxz` v0 container, benchmark harness, > CLI app, experimental PySide6 GUI milestones M1–M3). > Nothing here is a shipped or released feature. See [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) for the verified state. > **Badge honesty note:** the CI badge reflects the real workflow in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, but > **GitHub Actions runs are paused by owner decision 2026-10-17** (free-tier minutes exhausted; OQ-15) — > the badge shows the last historical run, not current state; verification gate is local (`pytest -q` + linkcheck > before every commit). The *Tests* badge is a > static snapshot of the locally verified suite (101 passed, re-verified 2026-10-17), not a live measurement. > **Last verified:** 2026-10-17 against the current working branch (see git history). --- ## What is LEXORA? LEXORA is a text-cleaning and **exact-compression** system for document collections (TXT, PDF, optionally OCR'd scans). It: 1. **Ingests** TXT and PDF files (OCR optional for scanned pages). 2. **Canonicalizes** the extracted text conservatively into deterministic UTF-8 bytes (this step *may* be lossy relative to the source, by design). 3. **Compresses** those canonical bytes with **guaranteed byte-exact recovery**: `decode(encode(C)) == C` for every input. The core invariant: **canonicalization may lose information relative to the original source; compression after canonicalization must never lose a single byte.** ## Why? Generic compressors (Zstandard, XZ, Brotli) treat text as opaque bytes. Document collections contain structure — repeated boilerplate, templates, records, multilingual text (English, Hindi, Gujarati) — that a compressor can exploit if it is allowed to *learn* representations safely. LEXORA's goal is to beat frozen generic baselines on total stored size while preserving strict correctness and running on low-resource hardware (~4 GiB RAM). ## Goals - Byte-exact losslessness after canonicalization — always, provably, via round-trip verification. - Conservative, versioned canonicalization with golden test vectors. - Cost-driven codec/candidate selection: every candidate competes against pinned baselines, and **every serialized byte counts** in the cost model. - Operate within a ~4 GiB RAM budget with bounded, streaming/block-based processing. - Multilingual support: English, Hindi (Devanagari), Gujarati. ## Non-goals (current scope) - Reconstructing original OCR output or source PDF layout bit-for-bit. - Claiming any performance advantage over Zstd/Brotli/XZ/PPMd before reproducible benchmark evidence exists (**no LEXORA-vs-baseline evidence exists**; the only published numbers, Revision R1, are baseline-vs-baseline on a Tier-1 smoke corpus — see [docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md](docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md)). - Being a general-purpose archive format. ## Features by maturity | Status | Capability | |---|---| | **Implemented** | Conservative canonicalizer (`src/lexora/canonicalize.py`), Zstd core baseline (`src/lexora/zstd_core.py`), `.lxz` v0 container (`src/lexora/container.py`, ADR-0007), **nine CLI verbs** (`canon`/`zround`/`pipe`/`pack`/`unpack`/`verify`/`inspect`/`batch`/`doctor` — see [docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md](docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md)), benchmark harness (`benchmarks/harness.py` + `corpus.py`, reproducible per [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md)), test suite (**492 passed, 1 skipped**, verified 2026-10-29). **Every core path streams** — encode, decode and canonicalization are flat in document size (measured: 126 MiB / 35 MiB / 35 MiB peak) | | **In progress** | GUI milestones M1–M3 landed & offscreen-tested but **not released**; ADR-0011 decided the GUI becomes a *client of the CLI* (process separation) and that implementation has not started — it needs a Qt-capable machine. Corpus **meets** the ≥1 GiB benchmark requirement (2395 files / 1.054 GiB, OQ-8); what is missing is a protocol-scope run and owner sign-off. GitHub Actions paused by owner (OQ-15) — local gate is `pytest -q` + linkcheck | | **Planned** | TXT/PDF ingestion; experimental candidates (dictionaries, Re-Pair, bounded token PPM, numeric/record coding, template+residual); `.lxdb` database mode; optional encryption profile; GUI stretch items (batch queue, drag-and-drop, shortcuts) | ## Architecture overview (proposed) ``` TXT/PDF ──▶ Extraction (optional OCR) ──▶ Canonicalization (versioned, deterministic) ──▶ Compression (byte-exact, cost-selected codec) ──▶ .lxz archive (.lxdb later) ◀── decode ◀── verify: decode(encode(C)) == C enforced at build time ``` A normative specification (`docs/SPECIFICATION.md`) and detailed architecture documents exist as drafts (Batch B). To contribute, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); the release process is documented in `docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md` (no releases exist yet). ## Supported inputs & current limitations - **Design targets:** `.txt` (UTF-8/other encodings), `.pdf` (text-layer first; OCR for scanned pages), scripts: Latin, Devanagari, Gujarati. - **Current reality:** byte-level canonicalization of raw text streams is implemented (rules CAN-R01/R02/R05 of the v0 rule set); TXT/PDF *file ingestion* is not implemented yet. Build scope is English-only per owner directive 2026-10-16 (Hindi/Gujarati deferred, not blocking). ## Installation / Quick start Install from a source checkout (no published package exists): ```bash pip install -e . # core (Qt-free): zstandard pinned range, Python >=3.12,<4.0 pip install -e ".[dev]" # + pytest for the test suite pip install -e ".[gui]" # + PySide6 for the experimental GUI (opt-in extra, ADR-0008) ``` Then try the CLI — `lexora --help` for the eleven subcommands, all documented in [docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md](docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md): ```bash lexora doctor # install health, incl. a live round-trip self-test printf 'alpha\r\nbeta\r\n' > in.txt lexora canon --in in.txt --out canon.txt lexora pack --in canon.txt --out a.lxz # default zstd level 9 (ADR-0012) lexora verify --in a.lxz # audit: structure + every block's SHA-256 lexora inspect --in a.lxz --verify # readable summary + accounting identity lexora unpack --in a.lxz --out back.txt lexora batch --in DIR --out-dir OUT --op canon # a whole tree, per-file JSON report lexora zdecode --in frame.bin --out back.txt # raw zstd frame, the mirror of zround ``` ### Query it like a database The archive is also a **searchable, compressed store** — SQLite holds the index, lexora holds the compressed text, and only the documents you ask for get decoded: ```bash lexora db init --root myarchive lexora db add --root myarchive --in book.txt --path "books/book.txt" --meta lang=en lexora db add --root myarchive --in paper.pdf --path "papers/paper.pdf" # PDF text layer lexora db add --root myarchive --in scan.pdf --path "scans/scan.pdf" --ocr # scanned lexora db search --root myarchive --query whale --filter lang=en lexora db get --root myarchive "books/book.txt" --out back.txt ``` Measured on 19 Gutenberg books (19.4 MB): payload **6.5 MB** (ratio 0.335), index **7.6 %** of the text, query **0.34 s**, single-document retrieval **0.47 s**. Design and trade-offs: [ADR-0016](docs/ADR/ADR-0016-queryable-archive.md) · usage: [docs/QUERY_ARCHIVE.md](docs/QUERY_ARCHIVE.md). There is a GUI for it: `lexora-gui`, then **Query archive…** in the ribbon. The GUI launcher `lexora-gui` requires the `[gui]` extra and exits 2 with guidance without it. ## Build & test commands Verified in-container (2026-10-29): ```bash python3 -m pytest -q # 492 passed, 1 skipped (~30 s; includes fuzz + interruption suites) QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -m pytest -q # same, incl. offscreen GUI widget tests (needs pyside6 + libegl1) python3 scripts/linkcheck.py # docs integrity gate — ALL INTERNAL LINKS OK ``` ## Benchmarks **LEXORA has now been measured against both frozen baselines — at smoke scope, not verdict scope.** The acceptance gates are defined in the blueprint (Pass ≥ 10%, Partial ≥ 3% smaller total stored size vs. the best frozen baseline) and formalized in `docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md`. R4, three splits, 172 files / 78.6 MiB, 3 reps (draft, awaiting owner review): | system | ratio | |---|---| | `lexora` (shipped default, level 9) | 0.3352 | | `lexora19` | **0.3090** | | `zstd19` (baseline) | 0.3109 | | `xz9` (baseline) | **0.3068** | So the pipeline sits **between** the two baselines: a small, consistent advantage over zstd-19 (167 of 172 files smaller) and a small, consistent deficit against xz-9 (xz wins every file). **Neither is a gate verdict**: the corpus now meets the ≥1 GiB requirement but no protocol-scope run has been done, and the honest reading is in [docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md](docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md). Reproduce it from [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md). ## Security & privacy notes - No security guarantees are claimed and no formal review has been performed. - **What is tested:** deterministic fuzz suites throw truncations, byte flips, end-drops and random blobs at seven reader entry points and assert that every mutant either decodes to the original bytes or raises `ContainerError` — never another exception and never a wrong answer; the reader enforces absolute limits (LIM-01/LIM-02) rather than trusting a header's declared caps; the atomic-write guarantee is verified against real SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL. - Design intent: decoders enforce resource limits (bounded blocks, memory caps) to survive hostile archives; sensitive/clinical corpora must not train shared dictionaries by default. - Vulnerability reporting instructions live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation index - [docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md](docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md) — what this unreleased tree contains, its limits, and what a release would need - [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md) — reproduce every measurement from a clean checkout - [docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md](docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md) — LEXORA vs both baselines, and what the numbers do not say - [docs/DEPENDENCY_LICENCE_REVIEW.md](docs/DEPENDENCY_LICENCE_REVIEW.md) — third-party obligations under PolyForm Start at **[docs/index.md](docs/index.md)**. > A curated list of tools and software that embrace the **local-first** philosophy: your data lives on your device, works offline by default, and syncs only when you choose.

## Why Local-First?

**Local-first** software keeps your data on your own hardware. The network is optional, not required. This means:

- **Privacy** -- Your data never has to leave your device. No third-party servers scanning your notes, files, or conversations.
- **Speed** -- No round-trips to a remote server. Everything loads instantly from local storage.
- **Ownership** -- You control your data. If a company shuts down, your files are still right where you left them.
- **Offline** -- Works on a plane, in a cabin, or anywhere without Wi-Fi. The internet is a feature, not a dependency.

This list collects the best tools that respect these principles -- from note-taking apps and office suites to encryption utilities and developer libraries.

# 🔒 LockHTML ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Turn any file into a PIN-protected document — optionally viewable only once.** AES-256-GCM · PIN-protected · one-time view · cross-platform · offline · nothing leaves your device. [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/lockhtml?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&color=22d3ee&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/stargazers) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/lockhtml?style=for-the-badge&color=22d3ee&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyPI-not%20published-lightgrey?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-22d3ee?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](#) [![CLI + GUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/interface-CLI%20%2B%20GUI-22d3ee?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](#) ### 🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/lockhtml/)  •  🚀 [Live demo — open the app](https://drsamonline.github.io/lockhtml/play/)  •  🧭 [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/) **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases/latest/download/lockhtml-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases/latest/download/lockhtml.apk)
--- **LockHTML** takes an ordinary file — an HTML page, a PDF, a photo, anything — encrypts it with a key derived from a PIN, and gives you back a single self-contained `.html` file. Anyone who opens it is asked for the PIN; enter it and the document appears. Choose **one-time view** (or a view limit, or an expiry date) and it stops opening once the conditions are met. No server. No accounts. No uploads. The locked file is a normal web page you can email, message or put on a USB stick — and the GUI works **offline** once loaded. ## ✨ Features - 🔐 **Argon2id** (memory-hard) by default, with **PBKDF2-SHA256** as a lighter alternative. - 🔑 **Recipient mode (X25519)** — lock a file to someone's *public key* so only they can open it, with no shared secret; add a PIN on top if you want two factors. - 🕳️ **Hidden volume** — a second PIN that opens entirely different content, so the file has a plausible cover story. - 🎛️ **Auto-calibrated KDF** — `--auto-kdf` times this machine and picks the strongest Argon2id cost that still unlocks quickly. - 🐢 **Constant-memory save** — for large streaming files, decrypt straight to disk chunk-by-chunk (Chromium), instead of building the whole file in memory. - 🔄 **age interop** — read and write ordinary [age](https://age-encryption.org/v1) files (X25519 recipients), so you can open a file the `age` tool encrypted and vice versa. - 🧩 **Shamir secret sharing** — split the key into *n* shares so any *k* holders (and no fewer) can open it. Give five people a share; any three can open it. - 🧂 **Keyfile support** — optionally require a second file in addition to the PIN. - ✍️ **Ed25519 signing** — sign a locked file so recipients can verify it came from you and wasn't altered. - 🎭 **Duress PIN** — a second PIN that opens a harmless decoy document instead. - 👁️ **View limits** — one-time, *N* views, a "do not open before" time, and an expiry time. - 💧 **Watermarking** — overlay recipient-specific text to trace a leaked copy. - 📦 **Any file type** — HTML renders inline; everything else is offered as a download. - 🗂️ **Two containers** — a single self-contained file for documents, or a chunked **streaming bundle** for very large files (video, disk images) at constant memory. See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). - 🌐 **Browser GUI** — a single self-contained HTML file, installable as a PWA, fully offline. - 🖥️ **Cross-platform CLI** — one command on Windows, Linux and macOS. - 🔁 **Reversible** — `lockhtml unlock` recovers the original with the PIN. - 🌍 **Localised viewer** — English, हिन्दी and ગુજરાતી unlock screens. - 🧩 **Zero runtime for the recipient** — any modern browser opens a locked file. ## 🚀 Quick start ### GUI (no install) Open the live app → **** — or run it locally with the CLI. Drag in your file, set a PIN, download the locked copy. It works offline after the first load. ### CLI ```bash pip install lockhtml ``` ```bash # Lock one file with a PIN lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 # One-time view, Argon2id, with a watermark lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --one-time --watermark "For A. Sharma" # Expire it and cap the views lockhtml lock plan.pdf --pin 4821 --max-views 3 --expires 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z # Require a keyfile as a second factor lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --keyfile team.key # Sign it so the recipient can verify authenticity lockhtml keygen -o sign.pem lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --sign sign.pem # Lock to a person's public key (no shared secret) lockhtml keygen --type x25519 -o alice.pem # writes alice.pem + alice.pub lockhtml lock report.html --to alice.pub -o report.locked.html lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --key alice.pem # Add a duress PIN that opens a decoy page lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --decoy-pin 0000 # Split the key: 5 shares, any 3 open it lockhtml lock report.html --shares 5:3 lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --shares report.locked.shares.txt # Hide the real file behind a cover, and tune the KDF to this machine lockhtml lock cover.html --pin 4821 --hidden-pin 0000 --hidden-file real.html --auto-kdf lockhtml unlock cover.locked.html --pin 0000 # opens the hidden content # Lock a whole folder lockhtml lock ./contracts --recursive --pin 4821 --outdir ./locked # Read and write standard age files (interoperates with the `age` tool) lockhtml keygen --type age -o key.txt lockhtml age-encrypt report.pdf -r age1abc… lockhtml age-decrypt report.pdf.age -i key.txt -o report.pdf # Large file: streaming container (viewer + sidecar .bin, constant memory) lockhtml lock holiday.mp4 --pin 4821 --stream # Recover the original lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --pin 4821 -o report.html # Open the browser GUI lockhtml gui ``` > **Tip:** share the PIN (and keyfile) over a *different* channel than the file. ## 🖥️ The GUI One self-contained HTML file (`lockhtml/gui/index.html`) — no server, no build step, works offline: - **Lock tab** — drop in any files, set a PIN (or generate a passphrase), and use the advanced panel for the KDF, view limits, expiry, watermark, keyfile and duress PIN. - **Unlock / Verify tab** — open a locked file with its PIN to preview and recover it. Because it's plain HTML + Web Crypto (+ a bundled Argon2 WASM), it runs identically in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS. The hosted copy is a **PWA** — installable, and cached for offline use. ## 📸 Screenshots
**The GUI — every option, straight from your browser**

**A locked file asks for the PIN before revealing anything**
## 🔬 How it works 1. Your file is encrypted with **AES-256-GCM**. 2. The key is derived from your PIN with **Argon2id** (or PBKDF2-SHA256) and a random 16-byte salt. 3. If a **keyfile** is used, it is mixed in as a pepper (a post-KDF HMAC), so the PIN alone is not enough. 4. If you **sign**, an Ed25519 signature over the ciphertext is embedded with your public key. 5. The salt, IV and ciphertext are embedded as JSON inside a small *viewer* page. 6. Opening the file runs the viewer, which asks for the PIN and decrypts **in the browser**. The plaintext never leaves the device. ``` locked.html = viewer shell + { kdf, params, salt, iv, AES-256-GCM(ciphertext), limits, watermark, sig } ``` The full format is documented in [`docs/FORMAT.md`](docs/FORMAT.md). The CLI (Python) and the GUI (JavaScript) implement the same format, so files lock and unlock interchangeably across both — enforced by CI on every push. ### 🔑 Recipient mode Instead of a shared PIN you can lock a file to someone's **X25519 public key**, so only the holder of the matching private key can open it. A fresh ephemeral keypair is generated per file, the ECDH secret goes through HKDF-SHA256, and the result encrypts the file with AES-256-GCM. Because the shared secret is already 256 bits of entropy, no slow KDF is applied on top — and you can still layer a PIN (and a keyfile) on top for two factors. It works in the streaming container too. ```bash lockhtml keygen --type x25519 -o alice.pem # private (keep) + alice.pub (hand out) lockhtml lock big.mp4 --to alice.pub --stream ``` ### 🔄 age interop LockHTML reads and writes standard [age](https://age-encryption.org/v1) files, so it interoperates with the `age` tool. Supported: the v1 header and its MAC, `X25519` recipients and identities, the 64 KiB STREAM payload, and multiple recipients per file. Not supported: `scrypt` passphrases, the ML-KEM hybrid and P-256 tagged recipients, and ASCII armor. ```bash lockhtml keygen --type age -o key.txt # an age identity; prints the recipient lockhtml age-encrypt report.pdf -r age1abc… # -> report.pdf.age lockhtml age-decrypt report.pdf.age -i key.txt -o report.pdf ``` age uses ChaCha20-Poly1305, which Web Crypto does not expose, so this is **CLI-only** — the HTML viewer and GUI cannot open age files. Interoperability is verified against the reference implementation in both directions; see [docs/AGE.md](docs/AGE.md). ### 🧩 Shamir secret sharing Split a file's key so that any *k* of *n* holders can open it and no fewer can. A random 32-byte seed is split with Shamir's scheme over **GF(256)**; the seed feeds HKDF-SHA256 to produce the AES key. The shares are written to a `.shares.txt` file that you distribute **separately** — the locked file alone cannot be opened. It works in the streaming container and can be combined with a PIN and a keyfile. ```bash lockhtml lock report.html --shares 5:3 # writes report.locked.html + report.locked.shares.txt lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --shares some-three.txt lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --share --share --share ``` ### 🚀 Launchers (no install needed) The repo ships small launcher scripts that run the CLI straight from the checkout — handy on a machine where you have not `pip install`ed anything: | Platform | CLI | GUI | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./lockhtml.sh …` (or `sh lockhtml.sh …`) | `./gui.sh` | | Windows | `lockhtml.bat …` | `gui.bat` | They find Python 3.9+, prefer a local `.venv`, check the two dependencies, and give a clear message if something is missing. On Windows the `.bat` files are directly runnable; on Unix, mark them executable once with `chmod +x lockhtml.sh gui.sh` (or just run them through `sh`). ### 🕳️ Hidden volume A locked file can carry more than one payload. The **cover** content opens with the main PIN, and a second PIN opens **hidden** content — different bytes entirely, with no indication in the file that it exists. This is the same idea as the duress PIN, generalised: you can add several hidden slots. ```bash lockhtml lock cover.html --pin 4821 --hidden-pin 0000 --hidden-file real.html ``` A hidden volume is **plausible deniability, not proof of absence**: someone who knows the format can see that extra encrypted slots exist, they just cannot read them. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ### 📦 Containers and size limits The default **embedded** container puts the ciphertext inside the HTML as base64. That is the most convenient form — one file the recipient can just open — but memory use is roughly **3–4× the file size**, so it is comfortable to about 50 MB and breaks somewhere around 250–300 MB (the browser's single-string limit is ~512 MB, and base64 inflates by 33%). For bigger files use `--stream`, which writes the ciphertext to a sidecar `.bin` in fixed-size chunks. Reading and decryption then cost **~O(chunk size)** instead of O(file size), so multi-gigabyte files work. The trade-off is that the recipient receives **two files**. | | Embedded (default) | Streaming (`--stream`) | | --- | --- | --- | | Files the recipient gets | 1 | 2 (`.html` + `.bin`) | | Practical size ceiling | ~250–300 MB | Limited by disk | | Memory to encrypt/decrypt | ~3.7× file size | ~O(chunk size) | | Size overhead | ≈33% (base64) | ≈16 bytes per chunk | Neither mode touches the network — "streaming" here means *memory*, not the internet. Full reasoning, the memory arithmetic and the chunk format are in **[docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md)**. ## 🛡️ Security model — read this **The PIN (and keyfile) gives you real encryption.** Without them the file is unreadable even if someone opens it in a text editor. Wrong PINs are rejected cryptographically (AES-GCM authentication), not by a string comparison. Signatures are verified before the content is shown. **The view limits, watermark and one-time view are browser-enforced deterrents, not server guarantees.** Since there is no server, the view counter lives in the browser's IndexedDB. A determined recipient can copy the file first, use another browser or profile, clear their storage, or screenshot the decrypted page. These features stop casual re-sharing and help you trace a leak; they are not a hard guarantee. **This is not a substitute for end-to-end tools** when the stakes are high (medical records, credentials, legal documents). Once a recipient decrypts, the content is on their screen and in their memory. For genuinely enforced single-view delivery, use a server that deletes the document after the first fetch. | Property | Guarantee | | --- | --- | | Content unreadable without PIN | ✅ Strong (AES-256-GCM + Argon2id) | | Content unreadable without the private key | ✅ Strong (X25519 + HKDF) | | Content unreadable with fewer than k shares | ✅ Strong (Shamir over GF(256)) | | Wrong PIN rejected | ✅ Strong (authenticated encryption) | | Keyfile required as a second factor | ✅ Strong (pepper) | | Authenticity (sender identity) | ✅ Strong when signed (Ed25519) | | Works offline / no upload | ✅ Yes | | Truly view-once / expiry | ⚠️ Best-effort (client-side) | | Survives a determined recipient | ❌ No | See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) and the self-audit in [`docs/AUDIT.md`](docs/AUDIT.md). ## 📂 Project layout ``` lockhtml/ ├── lockhtml/ │ ├── core.py # crypto + payload format v2 │ ├── cli.py # command-line interface │ ├── templates/ │ │ ├── viewer.src.html # viewer source (generated files below) │ │ ├── viewer.html # PBKDF2-only viewer (small) │ │ └── viewer-argon2.html # viewer with Argon2id WASM inlined │ └── gui/ │ ├── app.html # GUI source │ ├── index.html # generated, self-contained GUI │ ├── manifest.webmanifest, sw.js, icon.svg # PWA ├── tools/ │ ├── build.py # builds the viewer variants + GUI │ ├── minify.mjs # minifies the generated assets │ ├── check_gui_compat.mjs # cross-implementation check (run in CI) │ ├── e2e_fixtures.py # builds fixtures for the browser test │ ├── e2e_browser.mjs # end-to-end browser test (embedded + streaming) │ ├── e2e_gui.mjs # locks files with the GUI code path │ └── e2e_gui_verify.py # verifies those with the Python core ├── docs/ # design notes, format spec, audit ├── tests/ # crypto + CLI tests ├── examples/ # sample.html and its locked twin └── .github/workflows/ # CI + GitHub Pages deploy ``` ## 🤝 Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Planned work lives in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml cd lockhtml pip install -e ".[dev]" npm install # build tooling: minifier + Argon2 WASM make test # run the test suite make build # regenerate + minify the GUI and viewers ``` ## 📜 License [PolyForm Noncommercial](LICENSE) © Dr Sohil Momin
Built for the web. Runs on any OS. Nothing leaves your device.

# Lofi Studio Pro **A lofi beat machine that runs entirely in your browser.** Six tracks, sixteen steps, nine ambience layers and a live tape chain — all synthesised on the fly, no samples, no account, no server. [**▶ Open the app**](https://drsamonline.github.io/lofi-studio-pro/) · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/lofi-studio-pro/landing.html) · [Report a bug](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/issues) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-4c6ef5)](LICENSE) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.10.0-e94560)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/releases) [![PWA](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-installable%20%C2%B7%20offline-5a0fc8)](manifest.webmanifest) [![Tests](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![139 browser checks](https://img.shields.io/badge/browser%20checks-139%20passing-2ea44f)](docs/TEST-REPORT.md) [![Build](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-none%20required-informational)](.) [![No trackers](https://img.shields.io/badge/trackers-zero-brightgreen)](.)
--- ## What it is Open the page, press play, and you have a beat. Tap pads to change the pattern, drag the tempo, roll the tape chain until it sounds like a dusty cassette. Every kick, hat and chord is generated by an oscillator in your browser — nothing is downloaded or streamed, and after the first visit the whole thing works with the network switched off. It was built for the ninety seconds between two tasks: no login, no library, no "start a project". One screen, one sound, immediate. ## Features **Sequencer** — six tracks (kick, snare, hat, bass, keys, melody) across sixteen steps, with ten ready patterns, twelve four-bar chord progressions, swing from straight to lazy, and an optional snare fill every fourth bar. Tap a pad to switch it on, **hold it** to cycle normal → accent → ghost, **drag** across a row to draw a run. Hold a track name to empty that row. Tap a track name to mute it; the mixer has per-track faders and solo. **Tape chain** — low-pass filter, tape saturation, vinyl crackle, reverb, chorus and wow-and-flutter, all live while the beat runs. **Ambience** — nine procedurally generated layers (rain, fireplace, cafe, wind, birds, thunder, ocean, night, vinyl), each with its own volume, mixable on their own without a beat. **Ten themes** — from a near-black studio to a paper-white daytime mode, all driven by CSS custom properties so the swap is instant. **Recording** — hit the record button to capture a take as a downloadable audio file, with an optional metronome and a one-bar count-in. **Chance** — press *Chance* in the sequencer header and each step gains a probability: always, 75 %, 50 %, 25 %. A step that is on can still skip, which is where a loop starts to breathe. **Song mode** — four slots, two bars each. Capture a pattern into A, another into B, flip the toggle and the sequencer walks A → B → C → D, swapping the pattern and its chords at the bar line. While a slot plays it is the live pattern, so edits mid-song land in that slot. **Undo** — every edit is undoable, and a drag across twelve pads is one undo, not twelve. `Ctrl/⌘ Z`, or the button in the sequencer header. **Presets and files** — name a beat and save it (up to 24), or export it as a `.json` and import it anywhere — by button, or by dropping the file on the window. A preset captures the beat and its sound, never your preferences. **MIDI in and out** — play the voices from a keyboard or pad controller, or export four bars as a Standard MIDI File: drums on channel 10, bass/keys/melody on 1–3, chords already voiced, accents as velocities. It opens in a DAW with the parts separated. **Installable and offline** — a service worker precaches the shell, Tone.js included, so the app opens from the home screen with no connection at all. **Honest about your data** — no analytics, no cookies, no network calls after load. Your pattern lives in `localStorage` on your device. ## Quick start **Use it** — open and press play. **Install it** — in Chrome or Edge, use the install button in the top bar (or *Install app* from the address bar). On iPhone, Share → *Add to Home Screen*. **Run it locally** — it is a static site with no build step: ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro.git cd lofi-studio-pro python3 -m http.server 8000 # open http://localhost:8000 ``` Opening `index.html` straight from disk also works; only the service worker is skipped, because offline caching needs `http://` or `https://`. ## Controls | Action | Keyboard | Touch / mouse | | --- | --- | --- | | Play / stop | `Space` | Play button | | Move around the sequencer | Arrow keys | Tap a pad | | Accent / ghost a step | — | Hold a pad | | Draw a run of steps | — | Drag across a row | | Track menu (clear / copy / paste) | — | Hold a track name | | Mute a track | — | Tap the track name (sequencer) or `M` (mixer) | | Solo a track | — | `S` in the mixer | | Tempo | — | `−` / `+`, or `TAP` four times | | Metronome / count-in | — | Settings | | Undo / redo | `Ctrl/⌘ Z` · `Shift Ctrl/⌘ Z` | Undo button in the sequencer header | | Shortcut list | `?` | Settings → Keyboard shortcuts | | Pan a track | — | Slider under the fader | | Surprise me | `S` | Settings → Roll | | Next theme | `B` | Themes tab | | Record a take | `R` | Record button in the top bar | | Stop everything | `X` | Panic button | | Share the beat | — | Settings → Copy link | | Save / load a preset | — | Settings → My presets | | Export / import a file | — | Settings, or drop a `.json` on the window | | Export MIDI | — | Settings → Export as MIDI | | Song mode | — | Song block: tap a slot to capture, hold to clear | Knobs and faders accept a drag, a scroll wheel, and arrow keys. Double-click a knob to reset it. Hold `Shift` while dragging for fine adjustment. ## What it sounds like, and why The 2.0 engine sounded like noise because it mostly *was* noise: a bare white-noise snare, a white-noise hi-hat through a high-pass, a kick three times louder than everything else, and a reverb wired as an insert — which meant the dry signal never reached the output at all. On top of that, the bass and melody were monophonic and cut their own release on every consecutive sixteenth. 2.1 rebuilds the voice design and the gain staging. Measured on the same four seconds of the same pattern: | | 2.0.0 | 2.1.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | Peak | 0.68 | 0.54 (no clipping) | | Crest factor | 7.9 | 6.9 | | Snare | white noise burst | tuned body + band-limited crack | | Hi-hat | broadband hiss | band-passed tick with a bell | | Reverb | insert — dry signal lost | parallel send | | Bass / melody | monophonic, self-cutting | polyphonic | | Master | limiter only | 2:1 glue compressor → limiter → DC block → fades | The figure is generated from real captures of the running app, not from a mock: the top two traces are the same pattern's output, and the bottom is the spectrum of the same window. The 2.0 trace never returns to silence between hits; the 2.1 trace does. ## Screenshots | Studio | Mixer and tape chain | | --- | --- | | | | | **Ambience** | **Light theme** | | | | | **Song mode** | **Mixer** | | | | | **Settings, presets and files** | **Ambience** | | | |
## Under the hood A static site, split into five plain scripts. No framework, no bundler, no dependencies to install — the only third-party code is Tone.js, vendored in `vendor/`. ``` index.html the app shell: top bar, rail, views, transport css/app.css design tokens per theme, layout, controls js/data.js patterns, chord sets, themes, presets, ambience definitions js/state.js defaults, validation, persistence, migration from v1 js/audio.js the whole synthesis engine: instruments, FX, transport, ambience js/ui.js rendering, knobs, faders, toasts, visualiser js/main.js controller: transport, presets, recording, PWA wiring js/midi.js Standard MIDI File writer sw.js precache + navigation fallback manifest.webmanifest install metadata, icons, shortcuts vendor/tone.min.js Tone.js 15.1.22 (MIT) ``` Signal path: six instrument channels → low-pass → tape → chorus → wow → reverb → master volume → limiter → destination, with the vinyl crackle deliberately tapped in after the low-pass so the pops stay crisp, and a recorder hanging off the limiter. Three decisions worth knowing: - **Nothing blocks the first paint.** Tone.js is fetched on the first gesture, not on load: 107 KB of script before you press play, 448 KB after. The service worker still precaches it, so offline is unchanged. - **Everything is validated at the edge.** `state.js` coerces and clamps every value on load, so a corrupted or half-written save can never reach the audio engine. A save from the old single-file build is migrated automatically. - **Nothing is locked behind a timer.** The transport is guarded by a promise, not a millisecond timeout — the previous version used a 180 ms lock and a 150 ms restart, which silently swallowed every restart. - **The shell ships with its own dependencies.** Tone.js is served from `vendor/`, not a CDN, so a blocked network cannot leave a drawn but silent app. ## Testing 139 browser checks run against the real app in headless Chromium — every transport control, all ten patterns, twelve chord sets, ten themes, nine ambience layers, the six knobs, the faders, per-step velocity, drag-to-paint, hold-to-clear, presets, export and import, link sharing, the sleep timer, the media session, audio headroom, persistence, a corrupted save, migration from v1, recording, offline reload, and the layout at 360 / 390 / 768 / 1280 px. ```bash pip install websocket-client && python3 tests/run_browser_tests.py ``` Results: **[docs/TEST-REPORT.md](docs/TEST-REPORT.md)** — 88 passing, 0 failing. ## Native builds The web app is the source of truth; the wrappers are thin and live in CI, so nothing has to be installed locally and no stale binary is ever committed. | Target | How | Built | | --- | --- | --- | | **Android** | `.github/workflows/android.yml` wraps the static files with Capacitor | `lofi-studio-pro-v2.10.0.apk` (3.8 MB) — debug-signed, so sideload it | | **Windows** | `.github/workflows/windows.yml` wraps the same files with Tauri (WebView2) | `Lofi-Studio-Pro-2.10.0-x64-setup.exe` (2.1 MB) and `.msi` (2.9 MB) | | **PWA** | The live site installs to any home screen | tested — this is the build the 88 browser checks run against | All three are attached to the [latest release](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/releases/latest). Push a tag and CI rebuilds them from that exact commit. The Android build is debug-signed, so it installs from a file but cannot go to the Play Store as-is: add your own keystore as repository secrets and a `signingConfig` to `android/app/build.gradle`. The Windows binaries are unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn on first run. ## Roadmap The next round of ideas — features, offline behaviour, performance, and a short list of things deliberately left out — is in **[ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md)**. The first eight are already shipped in 2.1.0 and marked as such. Every feature in this version is catalogued in **[docs/FUNCTIONS.md](docs/FUNCTIONS.md)**. ## Licence [**PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**](LICENSE) — free to use, change and share for any noncommercial purpose: personal projects, study, hobby work, teaching, research, charities and public institutions. Commercial use needs a separate licence; [open an issue](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/issues) and ask. > Required Notice: Copyright Dr Sohil Momin (https://github.com/drsamonline) If you would rather have a permissive or copyleft licence, the code is yours to relicense only with my permission — but do ask, I usually say yes for MIT. ## Attribution - **[Tone.js](https://tonejs.github.io/)** 14.8.49 — MIT, © Yotam Mann and contributors. The entire sound engine sits on top of it. - **Every sound is synthesised.** No samples, loops, records or third-party audio assets are included, so there is nothing to clear and nothing to credit beyond the library. - **Icons** are drawn in this repository (SVG paths in `js/data.js` and `index.html`), and the PNG app icons are generated from the same shapes. - **Type** is the system UI font stack — no webfont is loaded. - Full detail in **[ATTRIBUTION.md](ATTRIBUTION.md)**. ## Sponsor Lofi Studio Pro is free and stays free for personal use. If it earned a place in your workday: - **[Sponsor on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline)** — one-off or monthly. - **Star the repo** — it genuinely helps other people find it. - **Send a pattern** — open an issue with a screenshot of something good; good presets get shipped in the next release. ## Author **Dr Sohil Momin** — built and maintained by one person, in between other things. # Lumen

[![tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lumen/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE)
[![offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg)](#offline-enforced)
[![build](docs/assets/badge-build.svg)](#building-it)

**A photo library that never phones home.**

An offline library in the spirit of Picasa. Point it at the folders you already
keep your photos in; it reads them, indexes them, and computes everything else —
thumbnails, edits, faces, albums, duplicates — on your machine.

[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/lumen/) ·
[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/lumen/) ·
[The rule](#offline-enforced) ·
[Support](#support)

<!-- shot:start -->

![Lumen's LAN gallery: a grid of photos with star ratings, edited badges and a possible-duplicates strip](docs/assets/app-desktop.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

---

## What it does today (v1)

**Library**
- Folder indexing with incremental rescans — a file whose size and mtime are
  unchanged is never re-opened, so rescanning 50,000 photos after adding one
  folder takes seconds.
- Month-grouped timeline grid, exactly Picasa's rhythm, with a thumbnail-size
  slider from 100 to 300 px.
- Sort by capture date, index date or file name.
- Star ratings (0-5) and favourites, both filterable.
- Background folder watching: drop files in and they appear.

**Metadata**
- EXIF read at index time: capture date, camera make/model, ISO, aperture,
  shutter, focal length, GPS, orientation.
- The full details strip in the viewer.
- GPS is captured and stored. There is no map yet (see the roadmap) because
  map tiles are an internet feature and this app does not use the internet.

**Viewer**
- Swipe, pinch-zoom, per-photo details.
- Non-destructive editing: rotate, flip, brightness, contrast, saturation,
  warmth, a real crop tool (corner handles, rule-of-thirds guides, Free / 1:1 /
  4:3 / 3:4 / 3:2 / 16:9 presets), and a **tone curve** with draggable points and
  six presets. Stored as a small JSON recipe in SQLite; the original file is
  never modified.
- Saving an edit also re-renders the cached grid thumbnail, so the tile shows
  what the viewer shows.
- Export an edited copy as a real PNG beside the original.

**Browse**
- Month-grouped timeline with a year scrubber down the right edge — drag it to
  jump to any year, which is the only navigation that works at 10,000 photos.
- Slideshow mode: full screen, auto-advance at 3/5/8/15 s, arrows to step, space
  to pause, Escape to leave. Reachable from the library or from any photo.
- Places: photos grouped by rounded GPS coordinate, largest group first. No map,
  because map tiles are an internet feature — but the browsing people actually
  did with Picasa's Places survives.

**Multi-select**
- Long-press any photo to start selecting; tap to add or remove.
- One action bar for the whole selection: 0-5 stars, favourite / unfavourite,
  add to album, or export as a ZIP.
- Bulk edits run in a single transaction, so rating 400 photos is one write.

**People**
- Manual face tagging: drag a box on a photo, name the person. Face boxes are
  stored as normalised coordinates, so they stay correct at any resolution.

**Albums**
- Virtual albums. A photo can be in many; nothing is copied.

**Search**
- SQLite FTS5 over file name, folder, caption and tags, with a LIKE fallback on
  platforms whose SQLite lacks FTS5.
- Three-stage fallback so a search rarely returns nothing: exact, then substring
  ("each" finds "beach-sunset.jpg"), then typo-tolerant ("reciept" finds
  "receipt.jpg"). The bar says which stage answered, rather than quietly showing
  approximate results as if they were exact.
- Filter chips for favourites and star ratings.

**Image formats**
- Nothing about formats is hardcoded. Every format is a plugin, and the scanner,
  thumbnailer, viewer and LAN server all ask the registry rather than testing a
  suffix — so installing a decoder makes its formats indexable with no code
  change.
- **Built in, always:** JPEG, PNG, WebP (still and animated), GIF, BMP, WBMP.
- **Via open-source decoders, when installed:** HEIC/HEIF/AVIF (libheif,
  libavif), TIFF (libtiff), camera RAW — CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW, DNG, RAF, RW2, ORF,
  PEF and more (LibRaw, darktable), JPEG XL (libjxl), and PSD/TGA/DDS/EXR/HDR
  (ImageMagick).
- Settings shows every plugin, whether it is ready, and exactly what to install
  if it is not. Lumen never downloads or bundles a decoder.
- The LAN gallery transcodes formats a browser cannot paint, so a HEIC photo
  still opens on a TV.

**Duplicates**
- Perceptual fingerprints (64-bit dHash) computed from the thumbnails that
  already exist, so a duplicate scan costs one cheap decode per photo.
- Grouping by 16-bit band lookup, then verified by Hamming distance — no
  all-pairs comparison, so 100,000 photos is still fast.
- Each group marks the copy worth keeping (largest pixel count, then largest
  file) and totals the space the extras use. **Lumen never deletes a photo.**

**Export**
- Album → store-only ZIP, streamed straight to disk, so album size is bounded by
  free space rather than RAM.
- Edited copies are written as PNG, and the written bytes are then **read back**
  and scanned for EXIF, XMP, IPTC, PNG text and time chunks. The snackbar says
  "checked: nothing left" only when that is literally true of the file on disk.

**LAN streaming**
- Turn it on in Settings and any browser on your Wi-Fi can browse the whole
  library at `http://<your-ip>:8421` — a self-contained gallery page, no CDN, no
  fonts to fetch, works with the router's WAN port unplugged.
- A UDP beacon broadcasts the address so a phone can find the desktop.

**Offline, enforced**
- No `http`, no `dio`, no webview, no telemetry. `test/offline_guard_test.dart`
  fails the build if anyone adds an outbound network client.

---

## Borrowed from the rest of the estate

Lumen is the first non-web app in this fleet, but four of its features are
direct ports of ideas already solved elsewhere in it. `CREDITS.md` lists exactly
which repo each came from and what was actually taken.

---

## Building it

You need the Flutter SDK (3.27 or newer — Dart 3.6+).

```bash
cd lumen

# 1. Generate the platform folders (android/, windows/, linux/)
flutter create --platforms=android,windows,linux .

# 2. Fetch packages
flutter pub get

# 3. Run on whichever platform you are sitting in front of
flutter run -d windows      # or: linux
flutter run -d <device-id>  # Android
```

`tool/setup.sh` (Linux) and `tool/setup.ps1` (Windows) do steps 1 and 2 in one
go.

### Shipping builds

```bash
flutter build windows --release
flutter build linux --release
flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi
```

### Android notes

`flutter create` writes a manifest without storage permissions. Lumen needs to
read image files, so add these to `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
inside `<manifest>`:

```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE"
    android:maxSdkVersion="32"/>
<!-- Required only to bind the local LAN server. No outbound use. -->
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE"/>
```

Also set `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` on `<application>` — the LAN
gallery is plain HTTP on your own network, and nothing else in the app makes a
request at all.

On first run, tap **Use camera roll** on the setup screen; it adds
`/storage/emulated/0/DCIM`, `Pictures` and `Download` automatically.

---

## Tests

CI runs on every push (`.github/workflows/test.yml`): `flutter analyze`, then
`flutter test`, then three real compiles — Linux desktop, Windows desktop and an
Android APK. That is the evidence behind "one codebase, three platforms" — every
target this project claims is compiled on every push.

Locally:

```bash
flutter test
```

- `test/edit_recipe_test.dart` — the colour-matrix maths, JSON round-trips,
  garbage input.
- `test/db_test.dart` — indexing, paging, filters, FTS search, month buckets,
  albums, edit persistence.
- `test/offline_guard_test.dart` — proves no outbound network client exists.
- `test/format_registry_test.dart` — extension routing, plugin precedence, and
  that every shipped plugin declares its backing library and its requirement.
- `test/hash_test.dart`, `test/fuzzy_test.dart`, `test/zip_test.dart`,
  `test/metadata_check_test.dart` — the v1.1 feature logic.
- `test/crop_math_test.dart`, `test/batch_ops_test.dart`, `test/places_test.dart`
  — v1.3–v1.4 logic.
- `test/tone_curve_test.dart` — LUT generation, monotonicity, overshoot, LUT
  application, and recipe round-tripping.
- `test/scanner_test.dart`, `test/search_fallback_test.dart` — regressions found
  in the v1.4.1 audit.

---

## Where things live

Everything Lumen writes goes under one application-support directory:

```
<app support>/
  lumen.db          SQLite index (photos, albums, people, faces, edits)
  thumbs/           PNG thumbnails, sharded 1000 ids per folder
  exports/          fallback target for exported copies
```

Your photos are never copied, moved or modified.

---

## Headless CLI

The same index and scanner without the interface. Pure Dart, so it compiles to a
single native binary — `lumen-cli-linux-x64` and `lumen-cli-windows-x64.exe` ship
alongside the app in every release.

```
lumen scan [--root DIR]     index the library
lumen stats                 what the index holds
lumen search QUERY          file names, folders, captions, tags
lumen recent [N]            the N most recent photos
lumen compact [--orphans|--all] [--yes]
lumen --help
```

`--json` on `stats`, `search`, `recent` and `compact` gives stable objects, so
anything that can run a process can consume the library:

```bash
lumen search "harbour" --json | jq -r '.photos[].path'
lumen stats --json | jq .photos
```

The CLI and the app share one index file, so either can rescan what the other
indexed. Both need SQLite 3 available to the dynamic loader — present on most
Linux systems; on Windows put `sqlite3.dll` beside the exe.

### Driving it from a launcher

Any tray launcher or hotkey tool that runs a command can reach the library. In
[CLDR](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR) that is one line in
`~/.config/cldr/config.toml`:

```toml
alias.photos = "/run lumen search"
```

Then `/photos harbour` in the command window opens the library's index. Note the
honest limit: CLDR spawns a routed command **detached** and does not render its
stdout, so the results do not appear inside its window — use `--json` and pipe it
somewhere, or open the app itself with `alias.lumen = "/run lumen"`.

## Known limitations

- **The LAN gallery streams originals.** Edits appear in the grid thumbnail and
  in the app's viewer, but a browser on the network sees the unedited file at
  full size. Serving a rendered copy would mean a decode per request; it is on
  the roadmap rather than half-done.
- **Apple platforms are not supported**, permanently. See `ROADMAP.md`.

## Honest status

This is a working v1, not a finished Picasa replacement. What is deliberately
missing, and why, is in `ROADMAP.md`. The two you will notice first:

1. **No automatic face detection.** Face boxes are drawn by hand. Real
   detection needs an on-device ML model, which is a milestone of its own.
2. **No maps.** Picasa's geo view needs map tiles; tiles need the internet.
   The plan is bundled offline tiles or a vector basemap, not a network call.
3. **Duplicate *deletion* is not automated.** Lumen groups and ranks; removing
   the extras stays a manual act, because a wrong automatic delete is the one
   mistake a photo library cannot apologise for.
4. **Video files are not indexed.** Photos only, for now.
5. **Exotic formats need a decoder installed.** JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and
   WBMP work out of the box; HEIC, TIFF, RAW and JPEG XL need their open-source
   tool on `PATH` (see *Image formats* above). That is deliberate — bundling
   libheif and LibRaw would multiply the binary size and the licence surface.
6. **The external decoders are CLI bindings, not FFI.** That keeps the build
   dependency-free and crash-safe, and it works on Windows and Linux. On
   Android there is no shell, so those formats stay unavailable there until an
   FFI plugin is added — the interface is already shaped for one.

One file. A language model does not send a document — it sends chunks, and half of them end in the middle of a code fence. This renders what is finished and holds back what could still change. ## Use it ```js var Md = require("./markdown-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.Md Md.render("## Hi\n\nSome **bold**."); // HTML string var s = Md.stream(); s.push("## Hi\n\nSome **bo"); // { html, complete: false } s.push("ld** text.\n\n"); // { html, complete: true } s.done(); // render the finished buffer, then reset ``` ## What it does - **CommonMark's core** — ATX headings with ids, paragraphs, hard breaks (two spaces or a backslash), emphasis, strong, strikethrough, inline code, fenced code with a language (``` or ~~~), blockquotes, ordered and unordered lists including nested ones, horizontal rules, links and images - **the GitHub extensions** — tables with per-column alignment, task lists (`- [x]`), and alerts (`> [!NOTE]`, `TIP`, `IMPORTANT`, `WARNING`, `CAUTION`) - **safe by default** — HTML in the source is escaped, never passed through; a `javascript:` link or a `data:` image is rendered as text, not as a link or image - **`Md.stream()`** — `push`, `set`, `html`, `text`, `reset`, `done`. An unterminated code fence renders as code immediately; any other unfinished block renders as text, so a list item is never briefly just a dash - **`Md.blocks(src)`** — the parse tree, if you want to render it yourself - **`Md.scale(opts)`** — the two type scales from the Go source: documents at 16px with headings growing to 2.5×, chat at 14px with headings barely larger, and the heading room curve - **`Md.toDom(src)`** — a guarded DOM helper, `null` in Node The streaming model and both type scales are ported from [lobe-mygo](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-mygo) `pkg/markdown` (MIT), which delegates parsing to MyGo's own CommonMark renderer. The parser here is written from scratch, because there is nothing to port — the Go side uses a library and the kits cannot have dependencies. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 92 passed, 0 failed ``` The tests cover every block and inline construct, the sanitiser (a `javascript:` link and a `data:` image are both refused), that markdown inside a fence stays literal, nested lists, alert bodies, table padding for short rows, the heading scale in both variants, and the streaming behaviour that matters: a partial heading is not a heading, half-written emphasis is not bold, an open fence is code, and a trailing blank line is what finalises a block. ## Consumers None, by design — no app in the fleet is modified by this pass. The intended first adopters are the AI-facing apps (SmartNotes, ai-bridge, Matneo), which currently render model output by hand, and that adoption is yours to decide one app at a time. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # ml-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **The classic algorithms, from scratch — for offline features.** tf-idf · Naive Bayes · k-NN · k-means · PCA · ID3 · linear regression · Markov chains · grammar A single file, zero dependencies, no model, no API key, no network.
--- ## THE BOUNDARY — read this first This kit is for **ranking, similarity, clustering and simple trend**. It is **NOT a diagnostic or predictive engine**, and **nothing in it may be used to claim a clinical or medical capability.** Several apps that use this kit are clinical; the algorithms here are generic maths and make no clinical claim. A model that ranks notes, groups similar cases or draws a trend line is not a diagnosis, and must never be presented as one. ## Why from scratch Forge's rule is offline, single-file, zero-dependency — so the usual ML frameworks (TensorFlow, Spark, scikit-learn) are unusable: they are hundreds of megabytes and need a runtime. But the algorithms that actually earn their place offline are the *classic* ones, and each fits in tens of lines. This is the light half of Forge's AI story: **heavy AI uses the user's own key; light AI runs on the device, from scratch.** ## What's in it | Algorithm | For | |---|---| | `tfidf` + `search` | ranked text search (tf-idf weighting, cosine similarity) | | `NaiveBayes` | a tiny bag-of-words classifier (tag a note, categorise an entry) | | `knn` | "items like this one" | | `kmeans` | clustering | | `pca2` | reduce many dimensions to two, for plotting | | `id3` + `predict` | a small, readable rules classifier | | `linearRegression` | a trend line | | `markov` + `generate` | statistical generation from a corpus (char- or word-level) | | `grammar` | rule-based generation: rules, slots, weighted alternatives | Plus `rng(seed)` — a seedable RNG, so a sampled start or a generated sentence is reproducible. ## Usage ```js var ML = require("./ml-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.MLKit // Ranked search var index = ML.tfidf(["the cat sat on the mat", "dogs bark and cats meow"]); ML.search(index, "cat"); // -> [{ i: 0, score: ... }] // Classify var nb = ML.NaiveBayes().train([ { text: "good product", label: "pos" }, { text: "terrible waste", label: "neg" } ]); nb.classify("excellent product"); // -> "pos" // A trend line ML.linearRegression([0, 1, 2, 3], [1, 3, 5, 7]).slope; // -> 2 // Reproducible generation var m = ML.markov(corpus, { order: 2, word: true }); ML.generate(m, { seed: 42, length: 12 }); // same seed -> same text ``` ## Tests ``` node test-node.js ``` A known tf-idf ranking case, a Naive Bayes classification case, a k-means convergence case, a regression line against a known slope, PCA, k-NN, ID3, and seeded-reproducibility checks for the Markov chain and the grammar. CI runs it on every push. ## Design notes - **Every algorithm is reimplemented from the idea**, not copied. Where a survey suggested a reference, only the shape was taken — the code is ours. - **Deterministic where it matters.** k-means seeds from the first *k* points; Markov and the grammar take a seed, so the same seed gives the same output. - **Small and readable.** Tens of lines each, so the maths can be read and checked. - **UMD.** `module.exports` in Node, `MLKit` in a browser — the same shape as the other kits. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # motion-kit — merged into tokens-kit

**This kit is no longer maintained on its own.** On 2026-11-12 it was folded into
**[tokens-kit](https://github.com/drsamonline/tokens-kit)** as version 2.0.0, reached as
`T.motion.*`.

## Why

A token set without its motion is half a design system. `tokens-kit` says what a surface
looks like — colours, sizes, shadows — and this kit said how it moves. Consumers wanted both,
and these presets are meaningless without those durations.

The intended home was a new `design-kit`; the App has no permission to create repositories,
so `tokens-kit` keeps its name and carries both halves.

## What to use instead

```js
const T = require("tokens-kit.js");

T.motion.spring({ stiffness: 220, damping: 26 });   // the solver
T.motion.ease.out(0.25);                            // an easing curve
T.motion.transition.modal();                        // a ready preset
await T.motion.apply(el, T.motion.transition.modal(), "enter");
```

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `Motion.ease` | `Tokens.motion.ease` |
| `Motion.spring` | `Tokens.motion.spring` |
| `Motion.preset` | `Tokens.motion.preset` |
| `Motion.transition` | `Tokens.motion.transition` |
| `Motion.DURATION` | `Tokens.motion.DURATION` |
| `Motion.motion()` | `Tokens.motion.motion()` |
| `Motion.apply()` | `Tokens.motion.apply()` |

This repository stays readable so that anything vendoring it still resolves; the code here is
frozen at the last version before the merge.

# music

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)
Album-wise music page for Dr Sohil Momin, served at https://drsamonline.github.io/music/

Audio is **not** hosted here. Each track points at the platform that hosts it (SoundCloud, Suno,
Flow Music, Newgrounds, Freesound) and the page plays it through that platform's own player, or
opens it in a new tab where no player page exists.

## What is where

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html`, `styles.css`, `*.js` | the page. No build step, no dependencies. |
| `data/tracks.json` | the manifest the page reads. Generated — do not hand-edit. |
| `sources/seed.json` | crawled catalogue: profiles, tracks, licences, duplicates, takes. |
| `sources/*.links.txt` | the link list per platform, one URL per line. |
| `tools/build_manifest.py` | seed + link lists -> `data/tracks.json`. |
| `.github/workflows/` | rebuild manifest on push, deploy to Pages. |

## Add a track

1. Put the track link in `sources/<platform>.links.txt`.
2. Re-crawl that platform (or paste the row straight into `sources/seed.json`).
3. Push. `rebuild.yml` regenerates `data/tracks.json` and `deploy.yml` publishes it.

Two tiers only, decided at ingest, never in the browser:
