# MusicGen

**A pocket generative composer.** One tap makes a finished-sounding track — harmony, melody, drums, mix and master — from six presets and a 12-character seed. No accounts, no server, no samples. It runs entirely in your browser, offline, in a light or dark studio.

[![tests](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![a11y: axe clean](https://img.shields.io/badge/axe%20wcag%202.1%20AA-clean-c6f24e.svg)](#accessibility--audit)
[![license: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-c6f24e.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-9aa8ff.svg)](#)
[![tempo: 20–500 BPM](https://img.shields.io/badge/tempo-20--500%20BPM-9aa8ff.svg)](#)
[![size: 108 KB gzipped](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-108%20KB%20gzipped-9aa8ff.svg)](#)
[![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-c6f24e.svg)](#)
[![web audio api](https://img.shields.io/badge/web%20audio-api-ff9f6b.svg)](#)

**[▶ Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/musicgen/)** · **[Open the studio](https://drsamonline.github.io/musicgen/app/)** · **[Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/releases)** · **[Enhancement backlog](docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md)**

![The MusicGen landing page, with a live specimen of a generated song](docs/screenshots/landing-desktop.png)

---

## What it is

A generative composer that behaves like an instrument rather than a toy. Every song is a **pure function of `(presets, seed)`**: the same inputs produce a byte-identical song, so a link is a recording. Random is sampled through a compatibility table so it stays musical, and every note is checked against the key and the chord sounding under it.

The whole thing is vanilla ES modules and the Web Audio API — no framework, no build step, no audio files, no network requests at runtime.

| Dark | Light |
|---|---|
| ![Studio, dark theme](docs/screenshots/studio-desktop.png) | ![Studio, light theme](docs/screenshots/studio-light-desktop.png) |
| *Two columns of dials, live spectrum, section timeline* | *The same studio in light — canvas colours are tokens too* |

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ![Piano roll on a phone](docs/screenshots/studio-mobile.png) | ![Waveform visualiser](docs/screenshots/studio-spectrum.png) | ![Generated cover art](docs/screenshots/cover-art.png) |
| *Phone: piano roll, chord labels, playhead* | *Waveform mode* | *Cover art from the song's own data* |

## Try it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen
cd musicgen/app
python3 -m http.server 8080
# → http://localhost:8080
```

To preview the whole site the way it is published — the landing page at `/` and the
studio at `/app/` — run `npm run build` and serve `_site/`. The site is assembled from
`docs/` (the page) and `app/` (the studio) at deploy time, so there is no second copy
to drift, and `npm run build` fails if any link in it points at nothing.

Then use your browser's **Install** / **Add to Home Screen** (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen). The service worker precaches the whole shell, so after that first visit it launches and plays with the network switched off.

## What's inside

**The composer** — eleven stages, each testable: key and mode → harmonic grid (2nd-order Markov over style progressions, modal interchange) → voicing with a voice-leading solver → bass → drums (groove templates, Euclidean layers, phrase fills) → motif → development transforms → pad and counter-line → arp → humanise → tension curve.

**The plan** — a song is two things: the decisions and the notes they produce. `plan(presets, seed)` returns the decisions as plain JSON — key, form, the chord under every bar, the theme, the tempo map — and `render(plan)` turns them into notes. `compose()` is the two together, and the split changed not one note: 330 preset × mood × seed combinations were hashed before and after it. The **Plan** panel in the studio opens that object up: reorder a section, repeat the chorus, change how many bars the intro runs, click a chord to change its quality. Every edit re-renders from the same seed, and the seed still reproduces the original. The drum pattern of any section is editable too, in a five-voice step sequencer. An edited song carries its plan in the share link — deflated, about 1.6 KB — so the link still hands over the song you heard rather than the one the seed would have made.

**The presets** — every axis has a **None**: no genre, no mood bias, no theme, no form, plain sine tones — so you can strip the song back to the notes and add only what you want. 11 styles, 10 moods, 10 themes, 8 song types, 7 synthesis technologies, plus a compatibility table that maps styles to allowed moods and engines. Tempo is a **map, not a number**: choruses lift, verses settle, every phrase gets a little rubato and the last two bars ease off, so a song breathes instead of clicking along. The BPM dial sets the centre and *Tempo drift* sets how far it may wander (0–35%). Range: **20–500 BPM**; per-track locks freeze the drums or the melody while you reroll everything else. Every share link carries the composer version, so an old seed can tell you it will sound different instead of silently lying.

**The ambience** — eight synthesised textures (rain, wind, fire, vinyl, crickets, ocean, stream, hum) with its own **Ambience dial**: *Auto* follows the theme, *None* is silence, or you pick one outright. Sitting under the arrangement with slow LFO movement and sparse droplets/crackles. Plus section transitions: a noise riser into every lift and a soft impact on the downbeat.

**The synthesis** — subtractive, FM, chiptune (real `PeriodicWave` pulses), additive, a six-frame **wavetable with a real morph**, Karplus-Strong, a **formant/vowel** layer and noise instruments, plus two **AudioWorklet** engines (granular and a waveguide) with native fallbacks; a drum kit built from oscillators and filtered noise; generated convolution reverb, tempo-synced delay and chorus; glue compressor and limiter on the master, mono bass below 120 Hz, sidechain ducking for EDM, a filter envelope and velocity-to-timbre on every voice, analogue drift, and a stereo-width tap. A voice pool steals the quietest voice with a fade; the scheduler runs a 200 ms lookahead and skips late notes instead of firing them in a burst.

**MIDI both ways** — export the song as Type-1 MIDI, or **import a MIDI file as the theme**: the highest-register line becomes the song's idea and everything derives from it.

**The exports** — WAV (16/24/32-bit, normalised to a chosen loudness target under a −1 dBTP ceiling), per-track stems as a zip with per-stem loudness in the readme, Type-1 MIDI, **XM module**, full song JSON (export *and* import), 1024 px cover art, and seed links that reproduce the exact song elsewhere.

**The module file** — a WAV keeps the sound and loses the editability; a MIDI keeps the notes and loses the timbre. An `.XM` keeps both in about 26 KB: it opens in OpenMPT, VLC or any tracker, and it carries its own instruments. MusicGen has no samples, so they are generated — one 32-sample single cycle per pitched track, built from the harmonic series of the song's synthesis technology, and one short percussive hit per drum voice. Polyphony needs channels, so the writer allocates pools rather than one channel per track: a four-note chord voicing on a single tracker channel would lose three notes of every four. The format is written from its specification, not from any tracker's source, since the trackers are GPL-family and this app is not.

**The platform bits** — installable PWA with a real install prompt and an offline badge, MediaSession metadata with generated artwork, screen Wake Lock, gamepad and MIDI-in control, five views (piano roll, tracker grid, spectrum, waveform, generative art), a piano roll you can zoom, pan and scrub, section looping, A/B against the previous song, undo/redo, a library with search/rename/duplicate, session restore, a text song summary for screen readers, `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-color-scheme` support, and a strict CSP (`default-src 'self'`) with zero runtime fetches.

## Drum editing

The Plan panel's ▦ button opens a step sequencer for one section: five voices of sixteen steps, showing the pattern that is actually playing. Click a step to take it over; **Back to generated** hands the section back to the seed.

Two rules keep it honest. The grid you see is read from the song you can hear, not from the plan — the plan only stores what was *changed*, so an untouched section still shows what the generator wrote. And the first click on a section captures the whole lane for that voice before flipping one step, so the rest of the pattern doesn't move under your hand.

A hand-written lane replaces the generated one **for that voice only**: writing kicks leaves the snares, hats, claps and toms alone. The generator still runs for every section — its random draws are part of every other voice's determinism — and the overridden voice is filtered out afterwards. Which is why a plan with no lanes still renders byte-identical songs: 330 preset × mood × seed combinations were hashed before and after this change.

## Controllers

Menu → **Controllers** maps a standard gamepad onto the transport — play, generate, random, evolve, mutate, next view, volume, loop, A/B — and connects a MIDI keyboard that auditions the lead sound as you play it.

Three details make it behave:

- **buttons are edge-triggered.** A held button fires once, not sixteen times a second. The reader keeps per-pad held state, so two pads cannot share it, and an unplugged pad does not fire a storm of releases.
- **an analog trigger counts as pressed.** Triggers report `pressed: false` with a high `value` until the browser's own threshold, so either signal is accepted — that was a real bug, caught by a test that handed the reader `{ pressed: false, value: 0.9 }`.
- **nothing is polled or requested until you ask.** The pad poll starts when the dialog opens and stops when it closes; `requestMIDIAccess()` is behind a permission prompt, so it only ever runs from the button.

## The grid

The visualiser cycles **roll → grid → bars → wave → art**. The grid is not a piano roll with different paint: it is a tracker's reading of the same song — one row per sixteenth, one column per track, notes written the way a tracker writes them (`C-4`, `F#2`) and drums written as voices (`kck`, `snr`, `hat`), with a stacked step marked `kck+` rather than quietly dropping the second hit. A roll answers *what is the melody doing*; this answers *what lands on the sixteenth*, which is the question drums ask.

The layout is computed by pure functions (`noteLabel`, `buildStepIndex`, `rowsFor`, `windowFor`) so it is tested without a canvas; `drawTracker` only paints what they return. The step index is built once per song — scanning 1,500 notes for every row of every frame would be the entire cost of the view.

## Themes

The studio ships **light and dark**, and the choice is yours, not the OS's: the ◐ button (or `T`) cycles **system → light → dark** and the choice is remembered. Every surface is a token, including the canvas palettes — the piano roll, spectrum, waveform and generative-art modes re-theme with the UI rather than staying stuck on one background.

## Accessibility & audit

`npm run audit` runs axe-core (WCAG 2.1 A/AA + best practice) over the studio in **dark, light and desktop**, and over the landing page, then adds app-level checks axe cannot know about: duplicate ids, unlabelled controls, canvases without an accessible name, missing `lang`, console errors. Current state: **zero violations, zero app-level issues, zero console errors**.

```bash
npm install --no-save axe-core puppeteer   # audit + screenshot tooling only
npm run audit
```

## Tests

```bash
npm test              # 103 unit tests, no browser needed
npm run test:browser  # 177 tests in real Chromium with real Web Audio
npm run lint          # determinism lint: no Math.random / Date.now in pure modules
npm run budget        # shell size, precache completeness, no external requests
npm run visual        # pixel-diff the studio against committed baselines
npm run shots         # regenerate docs/screenshots
npm run audit         # axe + app checks, light and dark
npm run build         # assemble _site/ exactly as GitHub Pages publishes it
```

The suite asserts, rather than claims:

- determinism — the composer run 100× on the same seed, diffed
- musicality — 330 style × mood × seed cases through the theory validator
- audio — an offline render measured for silence, clipping and LUFS against the style target
- exports — WAV byte length, MIDI header and track count, zip archive structure
- continuity — a 3-second playback run whose event cursor must keep advancing, plus a watchdog test
- anti-aliasing — partial counts asserted against Nyquist at 22.05/44.1/48 kHz
- clipping — master peak ≤ 1.0 and no sample-to-sample jump above 0.9 in a dense render
- worklets — both processors render audio and the modules load in an offline context
- tempo — 20 BPM and 500 BPM both compose, render and validate; the range is clamped at both ends
- variable tempo — the map integrates and inverts, every scheduled event matches `secondsAt(beat)`, the render length equals the song's duration, and each section can sit at its own BPM
- audio integrity — a dense render has no silent holes, no voices are dropped, the pool stays inside its cap at 7/8 and 500 BPM
- loudness regression — three styles rendered offline and checked against their LUFS target and peak ceiling
- mix balance — every track rendered solo, checked for being audible, not buried, and not letting the drums dominate
- the app — theme switching and persistence, service worker caching, visualiser modes painting, stems quieter than the mix, track locks surviving a new seed
- the landing page — composing, drawing and linking its specimen

## Mix balance (why it sounds like a mix)

Per-track loudness is measured, not eyeballed: the drum bus has its own compressor, every track has a measured trim, and `npm run test:browser` renders each track solo and fails if anything is buried more than 18 dB or if the bass sits more than 12 dB over the drums. That test exists because the bass *did* sit 18 dB over the drums in v2.2.0, and it was the difference between "a song" and "a bass solo".

## Audio health

The menu has an **Audio health** panel: context state, clock source, sample rate, base latency, voice-pool occupancy, worst tick gap, late and dropped notes, clock stalls and rebuilds. It polls only while it is open.

It exists because a browser audio app fails in ways you cannot hear in a screenshot. A phone locking interrupts the context; a Bluetooth route closing kills it; a busy audio thread freezes `currentTime` while `state` still reports `running`. All three look identical from the outside — *it went quiet* — and none of them leave anything a bug report can carry.

Two of those now repair themselves. A `statechange` to `interrupted`/`suspended` is resumed, and a clock that stops advancing while the transport says it is playing triggers a full rebuild — new context, new graph, same song, same position. The panel's **Rebuild audio** button is the same path, for the case where nothing fired. The suite proves it by freezing `currentTime` mid-song and asserting playback comes back on its own.

## Playback resilience

Seeking, regenerating and switching seeds are all covered by tests, because each one used to be able to leave the app silent:

- **A regenerate reuses the AudioContext.** It used to build a new `Player` — and therefore a new `AudioContext` — every time, and browsers cap those at a handful; after a few regenerations the constructor threw and nothing played again. `Player.setSong()` swaps the graph inside the existing context.
- **The closing fade cannot fire in the past.** Seeking near the end used to schedule the end-of-song fade *behind* the playhead, which faded the master to silence with nothing to bring it back.
- **`ensureAudible()` on every tick.** If the master is ever left at silence while the transport says it's playing, it is restored — a safety net that turns a dead app into a blip.
- **`play` is imported where it's used.** The one-line cause of "regenerate goes silent": after the UI split, `generate()` called `play()` without importing it, so every regenerate threw `TypeError: play is not a function` *after* pausing. The suite now asserts playback survives a regenerate, a seek to 97%, eight regenerations in a row, and the landing page's seed switching.

## Performance: why it stopped stuttering

Three things were fighting for the main thread, and the fix was structural rather than tuning:

- **The scheduler now runs off the audio thread.** The clock worklet had never actually attached — `AudioWorkletNode` rejects `numberOfOutputs: 0`, so the constructor threw and the app silently fell back to `setInterval`, which stutters whenever the main thread is busy. It now has one output and a silent sink, and ticks arrive from the audio thread. Lookahead went from 200 ms to 300 ms, and a note is only dropped if it is more than 150 ms late.
- **The visualisers are two layers.** Everything static in the piano roll (grid, chord labels, ~1,500 notes, drum lane) is rendered once into an offscreen canvas and blitted; only the section band and the playhead are drawn per frame. Measured cost of one visualiser frame: **0.08 ms**, down from several milliseconds. The landing page's specimen got the same treatment.
- **30 fps, not 60.** The render loop was already capped; with the blit it now has room to spare, and `prefers-reduced-motion` drops it to 10 fps.

## Performance and audio integrity

Measured, not guessed. The reverb IR is synthesised once per context and cached (it used to be rebuilt on every pause); the saturation curve is a shared `Float32Array` instead of 1024 floats per note; analyser buffers are reused across frames; the section-intensity lookup is a binary search; and pausing fades the master instead of rebuilding the graph.

Three bugs used to make sound drop out, and they are worth naming because they were invisible:

1. **The voice counter never decremented.** It ran on `setTimeout`, which is throttled in a background tab and never fires during an offline render — so `active` hit the cap and stayed there, and from then on every quiet note was silently dropped. It is now a pool pruned by time, stealing the quietest voice with a fade.
2. **Feedback loops were never disconnected.** Karplus-Strong's delay line rang forever and the noise bed's LFO kept running; over a long session that is a CPU creep that ends in dropouts.
3. **Late notes were fired in a burst.** Anything more than 60 ms late is now skipped instead of dumped into the present.

## Architecture

```
index.html            landing page (its own live specimen)
landing.css landing.js
app/                  the PWA
  index.html styles.css manifest.webmanifest sw.js icons/
  src/core/           rng algorithms theory voicing motif composer validate
  src/presets/        styles moods themes types techs compatibility
  src/audio/          engine instruments drums fx mastering lufs
  src/export/         wav midi zip artwork
  src/visual/         pianoRoll (+ bars, waveform, generative art)
  src/state.js        src/main.js
  qa/matrix.html      listening matrix (dev only)
tests/unit/ tests/browser/
scripts/              screenshots.mjs, audit.mjs
docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md  the backlog
```

## Credits and licences

Two of my own other repositories informed this one. **ambient-sound-studio** (personal-use licence) is where the idea of layered synthesised textures comes from — the eight beds here are reimplemented for this engine, not copied. **eon-commando** (same) contributed the noise-sweep primitive that became the section risers. **audio-kit** (PolyForm Noncommercial) shares the same "patterns, not files" philosophy; its code is deliberately *not* vendored here, because mixing licences in one bundle is a trap.

## Layout

Two splits, both done for editability rather than tidiness.

**The engine** is five modules behind a barrel (`engine.js`): `worklets.js` (AudioWorklet loading and fallbacks), `graph.js` (track chains, buses, master chain), `scheduler.js` (tempo map, events, automation, voice dispatch), `player.js` (live transport) and `render.js` (offline rendering).

**The UI** is six modules behind `main.js` (205 lines of wiring and nothing else): `ui/ctx.js` (the DOM map, the mutable singletons, the small helpers), `ui/dials.js` (presets, random/evolve/mutate, groove editor), `ui/generate.js` (history, compose, the three readouts), `ui/transport.js` (player lifecycle, loop, A/B, wake lock, MediaSession, install), `ui/visuals.js` (theme, five views, piano-roll gestures) and `ui/exporters.js` (WAV, stems, MIDI, JSON, art, share, library, recording).

## Contributing

`CONTRIBUTING.md` has the one rule that matters (determinism in `src/core/`) and the five checks a PR must pass. `docs/LISTENING.md` is the golden-seed log — the place where the automated tests stop and a person listens.

## Design notes

Three decisions are worth knowing about, because they were made against the obvious choice:

**The validator accepts chromatic notes when the chord owns them.** An absolute "everything in the key" rule would reject the modal interchange and borrowed chords that make the harmony interesting. The rule is *in key **or** a tone of the chord sounding at that moment*.

**Loudness targets are per style.** Lo-fi sits at −16 LUFS, EDM at −11, Ambient at −18. Normalising everything to a single streaming number would flatten exactly the character the styles are for.

**Worklets arrived last, not first.** Granular and waveguide processors exist now, but every one of them is a per-track node with a native fallback, and the app still runs with `addModule` unavailable. Building the whole synth on worklets first would have made the fallback the interesting case instead of the exception.

## Known gaps

Stems share one gain (measured on the mix) rather than being re-mixed per track — the per-stem loudness is written into the zip's readme; undo covers preset changes, not generations; note audition and a groove editor are not implemented; granular and physical modelling remain native-node approximations rather than AudioWorklets; MIDI import, microtuning, a share target and a protocol handler are still open. The full backlog, with what is done and what is not, is in [docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md](docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md).

This one asks you to **position**. The gun is fully automatic and picks its own targets, so the only decisions left are spatial ones: how close do you dare stand, when do you break line of sight, when do you spend your slide, when do you jump and when do you duck. Every mechanic below exists to make those decisions interesting rather than to add buttons. - **Three controls.** Left, right, jump, duck. That is it. There is no fire button, and there never will be. - **Range is a resource.** Your gun only fires when something is inside its circle, so damage output is a function of positioning. - **Heat punishes camping.** Firing builds heat, and heat only cools when *nothing is in range*. Standing still and spraying is impossible — you have to weave. - **The chain rewards aggression.** Kills within 2.5s stack up to ×8. Staying close is how you score; it is also how you die. - **Graze rewards nerve.** Enemy fire that passes close but does not hit charges an EMP. The boot screen shows your current keys, so you can see what to press before you start. Touch button size and opacity are adjustable, and there is a left-handed pad layout. **Audio note.** Browsers refuse to start audio until the page has received a real user gesture — this is a hard browser rule, not a bug. The game unlocks its audio on the *first keypress or click*, and the boot screen says so explicitly while it is waiting. It changes your hitbox from 42px tall to 24px tall, and several threats are tuned around exactly that: - **Turret lasers** fire flat at standing chest height. Duck and they sail over your head. - **Laser gates** span chest-to-knee. Duck and you walk straight under them. - **Flyer volleys** aimed at your centre line pass overhead when you crouch. # Neon Velocity

**Play in the browser:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/neon-velocity/play/> — it
installs as an app (PWA) and works offline after the first load.
**Landing page:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/neon-velocity/>

![Gameplay](site/assets/shots/action.jpg)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Boss fight](site/assets/shots/boss.jpg) | ![Swarm](site/assets/shots/swarm.jpg) |
| The Core Interceptor, first of four bosses | Drone formations converging |
| ![Title screen](site/assets/shots/menu.jpg) | ![Pause menu](site/assets/shots/pause.jpg) |
| Title screen, difficulty select | Pause menu |

A retro side-scrolling shooter for **Godot 4.3** where every sprite and every
sound is generated at runtime. The repository contains no binary assets at all:
no PNGs, no OGGs, no fonts — just GDScript, three shaders and two scene files.

```
godot --path .          # or open the folder in the Godot 4.3 editor and press F5
```

There is also a **web build that installs as an app** (PWA) — see
[Play in a browser](#play-in-a-browser-pwa).

## Controls

| Action | Keys |
|--------|------|
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys |
| Fire | `Z` or left mouse button |
| Dash (brief invulnerability) | `Space` / `Shift` |
| Switch weapon | `Q` / `E` |
| Pause | `Esc` |

On a phone or tablet the game draws its own controls: drag anywhere on the left
half to fly, `FIRE` and `DASH` sit under the right thumb, and `WPN` / pause are
in the top-right corner. Turn the device to landscape — portrait shows a
"rotate your device" screen. On the web build the first tap also asks for
fullscreen and a landscape lock.

## Play in a browser (PWA)

The project exports to Web, and the export is patched into a real installable
PWA: manifest, icons, service worker, offline page. It is single-threaded, so it
does **not** need `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` / `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`
headers and will run on any static host, including GitHub Pages, Netlify,
Cloudflare Pages and itch.io.

```bash
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Web" build/web/index.html
python3 tools/pwa_post_export.py build/web

# local preview (service workers need http, not file://)
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory build/web
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

The first load pulls a ~35 MB wasm bundle; after that the service worker serves
it from cache and the game starts instantly, including offline. Install it from
the browser's address bar ("Install") to get a standalone window and an icon.

Two things to know: a **keyboard is required** (there are no touch controls),
and the page must be served over **HTTPS or localhost** — service workers are
refused on plain `http://` origins.

`tools/pwa_post_export.py` does two things the raw export does not: it registers
the service worker (Godot only does that for thread-enabled builds) and it
prunes the worker's precache list, which otherwise lists `index.worker.js` in
thread-less builds — one 404 there makes `cache.addAll()` reject and silently
kills offline support.

## What is in the game

- **Six weapons** — plasma cannon, spread shot, laser lance, seeker missiles,
  railgun, nova burst. Each has five levels and gains XP from kills.
- **18 mods** — stat modifiers and named effects (chain lightning, ricochet,
  life siphon, MIRV split, EMP slow, multi-pulse nova). Picking up a mod card
  pauses the run and offers three choices.
- **Endless procedural levels** — the world is a strip of 2400-unit chunks,
  each generated from `run_seed + chunk_index`, so a seed always replays the
  same run.
- **Four bosses** on a five-chunk cycle, each with its own attack patterns and
  a phase change every quarter of its health.
- **Full loop** — title screen, difficulty select, HUD, pause menu, settings,
  run summary with accuracy and best score, local save file.
- **Adaptive music** — four synthesised layers (bass, lead, pad, drums) that
  fade in as you get deeper into a run, plus 24 procedural sound effects.

## How the "zero assets" trick works

| Thing | Where it comes from |
|-------|---------------------|
| Sprites | `scripts/core/Art.gd` rasterises every image with the `Image` API from a fixed 16-colour palette, then wraps it in an `ImageTexture` |
| Sound effects | `scripts/core/AudioManager.gd` synthesises PCM float buffers (FM, sweeps, noise, arpeggios) and packs them into `AudioStreamWAV` |
| Music | The same file builds four 6.857 s loops at 140 BPM and crossfades them |
| Level art | Starfield, nebula and mountain silhouettes are generated once and tiled by `ParallaxBackground` |

Audio generation takes roughly half a second at startup on a modest laptop, all
of it before the title screen appears.

```
  systems/     WeaponSystem, LevelManager, GameManager, ReplaySystem
```

## Testing

```bash
# headless smoke test: boots Main, plays 7 seconds of synthetic input, asserts 27 things
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/TestRunner.tscn

# 50-second soak run: chunk streaming, pooling and the first boss fight
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/tools/SoakTest.tscn

# dump every generated sprite to art_preview/ for inspection
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/tools/DumpSprites.tscn
```

The test runner exits non-zero on failure, so CI can gate on it.

## Builds and releases

`export_presets.cfg` defines four presets: Web, Linux, Windows and macOS.
Export templates must be installed first (Editor → Manage Export Templates).

```bash
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Linux/X11"      build/linux/NeonVelocity.x86_64
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Windows Desktop" build/windows/NeonVelocity.exe
godot --headless --path . --export-release "macOS"          build/macos/NeonVelocity.zip
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Web"            build/web/index.html
```

Everything is automated in `.github/workflows/build.yml`:

| Trigger | What happens |
|---------|--------------|
| any push / PR | headless smoke test + 50-second soak test |
| push to `main` | the above, then the Web build is patched into a PWA and deployed to GitHub Pages |
| `v*` tag | the above, then Linux, Windows, macOS and Web are exported and attached to a GitHub release |
| manual dispatch | same as a tag, without publishing a release |

So shipping a new version is `git tag v1.1.0 && git push --tags`.

Note on Pages: GitHub Pages needs a **public** repository on the free plan, so
the Pages job is opt-in. To turn it on, make the repository public, enable Pages
with "GitHub Actions" as the source, then set a repository variable
`ENABLE_PAGES=true` (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables).
Every push to `main` will then publish the PWA. Until then, take
`neon-velocity-web.zip` from the release and drop the unzipped folder on any
static host — Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, itch.io and GitHub Pages all work,
because the build needs no special headers.

## Saves and replays

Settings live in `user://settings.cfg`, the last run and lifetime stats in
`user://save_game.save` (JSON, XOR-obfuscated — not encrypted, and not meant to
be), and recorded inputs in `user://replays/`.

Replays are **recorded, not yet playable**: each run writes a JSON file with the
seed, difficulty and three bytes of input per frame, which is everything needed
to re-simulate it, but no playback UI is wired up yet.

offline-pdf-toolkit: # Offline PDF Toolkit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) **Merge, split, rotate, watermark, number, protect and compress PDFs — in one small page, with no server to send them to.** The page itself is about **49 KB gzipped**; the PDF engines load only when you open a document, and the OCR and qpdf engines only when you ask for them. No upload, no account, no tracking, no install. Unplug the network and it still works. **[Open the toolkit →](https://drsamonline.github.io/offline-pdf-toolkit/play/)** · [landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/offline-pdf-toolkit/) · [downloads](#downloads) · [what's planned](ENHANCEMENTS.md) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) ## Why it exists The files people merge and split are usually the ones they should not hand to a stranger's server — patient reports, contracts, statements, identity documents. Every "free PDF tool" online uploads your file. This one cannot: the PDF engine is compiled into a single HTML file and there is no backend to send anything to. The proof is that it runs with the cable pulled out. | | | | |---|---|---| | ![The launcher, with no document open](docs/assets/app-home-desktop.png) | ![The launcher on a phone](docs/assets/app-home-mobile.png) | ![The app with five sample pages loaded](docs/assets/app-desktop.png) | The empty state is the front door: drop a file on the hero, or take one of the four tools a report usually needs. Every tool in the app is in one catalogue — the launcher, the all-tools sheet and the category dot beside each sidebar section all read from it. ## Features | | | |---|---| | **Launcher** | The empty state offers a drop target, the last files this tab wrote, and four core tools in one tap. Choose a tool with nothing open and it asks for the file, then opens itself. | | **All tools** | 27 tools in one sheet, grouped Edit / Optimize / Secure / Convert / Trust, with search. | | **Session list** | Every file the app writes, with the tool that made it and its size — in `sessionStorage`, so it dies with the tab, and the bytes are never kept. | | **Merge** | Add several PDFs; they lay out in order. Drag any page to reorder. | | **Split / extract** | Select pages (shift-click for a range) and pull them into a new PDF. | | **Rotate** | 90° steps, left or right, per page or for a whole selection. | | **Reorder / duplicate / delete** | Drag and drop, or move selections earlier/later. | | **Trim & resize** | Cut the same margin off every edge, or re-lay mixed pages onto A4 / Letter — text stays selectable. | | **Impose** | 2-up, 4-up and saddle-stitch booklet on A4 landscape sheets. | | **Watermark** | Text, centre / tiled / corner, with size, opacity, angle and colour. | | **Header & footer** | Six positions, with `{n}`, `{total}`, `{date}` and `{file}` tokens. | | **Bates numbering** | Prefix, start, zero-padded digits, four positions. | | **Split** | Every N pages, one file per page, or ranges (`1-3, 4, 8-10`). | | **Export images** | Every page as a PNG at the DPI you choose. | | **Redaction** | Cover every match of a word — or of a shape: 12-digit numbers, phone numbers, emails, PAN, dates, IFSC, and labelled identifiers (MRN, UHID, OPD, policy). With *rebuild* on the page is rasterised, so the text underneath is really gone. | | **Form fields** | Reads the AcroForm, fills it, and flattens the values into the page so they cannot be edited back. | | **Signature** | Draw it with a mouse or finger, or load a picture; the empty margin is trimmed and it is stamped where you choose. | | **Extract images** | Recovers the pictures stored inside the PDF at their original resolution. | | **Compress, three ways** | *Photos only* re-encodes the JPEGs and leaves the text as text; *lossless* runs qpdf over the result; *every page* rasterises, with an optional greyscale pass. | | **Batch** | *One file per source* — the same tools on every loaded document, one output each. | | **Share locked** | Wrap the finished PDF in a single HTML file that asks for a PIN — AES-256-GCM, the same container [LockHTML](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml) writes, so either viewer opens either file. | | **Page labels** | The numbers a reader *sees*: i, ii, iii for the front matter and 1, 2, 3 for the body, written as a `/PageLabels` tree. | | **Compare** | Reads the text of the first two documents and reports the pages that differ, with the first line that changed. | | **A whole folder** | Pick a folder, and every PDF in it is processed and written to an `out` folder beside it. Chrome, Edge and Android Chrome only — the button says so when the browser cannot. | | **Insert blank pages** | Drop an empty page after the selection, sized like the page before it. | | **Interface languages** | English, हिन्दी and ગુજરાતી for the interface, switched in the header and remembered. | | **Remembered tools** | Your tool settings come back on the next visit; *Reset tools* forgets them. | | **Flatten & strip** | Flatten form fields, or remove the metadata before sending a file on. | | **Page numbers** | Four formats, four positions, starting number, size. | | **Metadata** | Title, author, subject, keywords. | | **Compress** | Renders each page to JPEG at a chosen DPI and quality, then rebuilds. | | **Images → PDF** | PNG and JPEG, one image per page. | | **Open a protected PDF** | Asks for the password, then lets you edit it — and keeps the protection on the way out unless you set a new one. | | **Password protect** | AES-256, with user/owner passwords and permissions for printing, copying, modifying. | | **Unlock** | Remove a password you already know, in the browser. | | **Extract text** | From a digital PDF → `.txt`. | | **OCR** | From a scan. The engine ships beside the app, so it works offline on the first try. | | **Credits** | All bundled libraries credited in-app and in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. | | **Themes** | Dark, light, high-contrast. | | **Network counter** | Every `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` this page makes, listed in the app. A fresh copy reads `0 requests`. | | **Self-test** | Proves merging, rotating, cropping and AES-256 work — on your machine, in your tab. | | **Command palette** | `Ctrl-K` — every tool by name. | | **Undo / redo** | `Ctrl-Z` and `Shift-Ctrl-Z` across rotate, delete, duplicate, move and loading files. | | **Keyboard** | `Alt-←` / `Alt-→` moves the selected pages; the grid is a labelled listbox for screen readers. | | **Shortcuts** | `a` select all · `d` deselect · `[` `]` rotate · `Delete` remove · `t` theme · `Ctrl-K` commands · `Ctrl-Z` undo · `Alt-←/→` move pages · `?` help | ## Command line The same two engines, without the browser. `pdfkit` loads pdf.js and pdf-lib from `vendor/` — the exact bytes the page inlines — so a file merged in a shell and a file merged in the app are written by the same writer. ```sh node cli/pdfkit.mjs info report.pdf node cli/pdfkit.mjs merge a.pdf b.pdf -o merged.pdf node cli/pdfkit.mjs split merged.pdf --every 10 -o chunk node cli/pdfkit.mjs watermark merged.pdf --text CONFIDENTIAL --opacity .12 -o marked.pdf cat report.pdf | pdfkit info - --json | jq .pages ``` Twelve commands — `info text merge split rotate delete order watermark number meta labels impose` — plus `-` for stdin, `-o -` for stdout, `--json`, `--quiet` and `--locale`. Rasterising (PNG export, compress-by-rendering, redaction rebuild, OCR) stays in the app, because those need a canvas. **[cli/README.md](cli/README.md)** — the commands, the pipes, and why CLDR is used through `Intl` instead of being vendored. kept in the source pipeline/build_pdf.py inlines the libraries + minifies → app.html pipeline/build_landing.py emits index.html + docs/index.html from landing.html vendor/ the three libraries, with # optical-kit — merged into frame-kit

**This kit is no longer maintained on its own.** On 2026-11-12 its fountain code, its decoder
and its sender/receiver were folded into **[frame-kit](https://github.com/drsamonline/frame-kit)**
as version 2.0.0.

## Why

`frame-kit` wrapped bytes and `optical-kit` moved them, and both described "self-describing
frames" — two formats (22-byte and 17-byte), two CRCs, two decoders, used by the same three
apps: `helioprism`, `blinkcode-ai`, `BLINKTRANSFER`. Two definitions of one thing drift; this
one had, and `frame-kit`'s default decoder could only peel a stream whose sender used session
`1`.

## What to use instead

```js
const Frame = require("frame-kit.js");

const tx = Frame.Sender(bytes, { blockSize: 1400 });   // tx.next() → frame bytes
```

planner-pro:
Planner Pro

An offline-first planner that behaves like a tool, not a website.
Day, week, month and year planning in one quiet screen. Multi-profile, PIN-locked, no accounts, no servers.

--- ![Planner Pro — Today view](docs/screenshots/today-desktop.png) ## Why another planner Most planners are either a website with a calendar bolted on, or a subscription that owns your data. Planner Pro is a single small app you can open from a file, install as a PWA, or build into an APK/EXE. It loads instantly, works on a plane, and stores everything on your device. - **Zero runtime dependencies.** No React, no build step, no CDN, no fonts to fetch. ~210 KB of HTML/CSS/JS minified (290 KB readable). - **Genuinely offline.** A service worker precaches the whole shell; the app opens in under a second with the network off. - **Local-first data.** One versioned `localStorage` document, exported to JSON in one click. Your planner is a file you own. - **Fast by construction.** Views render in a single string pass with event delegation — no virtual DOM, no re-render churn, no spinners. ## Screenshots | Day | Week | |---|---| | ![Day view](docs/screenshots/day-desktop.png) | ![Week view](docs/screenshots/week-desktop.png) | | Year | Insights | |---|---| | ![Year view](docs/screenshots/year-desktop.png) | ![Insights](docs/screenshots/insights-desktop.png) | | Command palette | Mobile — Insights | |---|---| | ![Command palette](docs/screenshots/palette-desktop.png) | ![Mobile insights](docs/screenshots/insights-mobile.png) | | Mobile — Today | Mobile — Day | Light theme | |---|---|---| | ![Mobile today](docs/screenshots/today-mobile.png) | ![Mobile day](docs/screenshots/day-mobile.png) | ![Light theme](docs/screenshots/today-light.png) |

## Features **Planning** - **Today** — greeting, live clock, completion ring, streak, time-block count, open-task count, 7-day completion bars, brain dump. - **Day** — intention line, to-do list with priorities and inline editing, time blocks with a live "now" highlight, notes & reflection. - **Week** — real calendar weeks (not "every Monday forever"), weekly focus, weekly goals, seven day columns with completion counts. - **Year** — year theme, year goals, twelve month cards with goals and task progress. - **Archive** — finished years move out of the way automatically; restore, export or delete any of them. - **Carry over** — pull yesterday's unfinished tasks into today in one click. - **Repeating tasks** — daily, weekdays or chosen days; instances are created lazily when you open a day, so a missed day fills itself in. - **Day templates** — build a routine once ("clinic day"), save it, apply it to any date. - **Estimates and capacity** — put minutes on a task and see planned time against your day; the bar turns amber when you overbook. - **Insights** — a year heatmap, best streak, busiest weekday, 30-day trend and your most-used tags. Click any day to open it. - **Encrypted backups** — AES-256-GCM with a PBKDF2-derived key, unlocked by a passphrase you choose. Safe to keep in cloud storage; no recovery if you forget it. - **Bulk actions** — select several tasks to move them to another day or delete them (with undo). - **Markdown vault export** — one `.md` note per day and per week, zipped in the browser with a hand-rolled store-only writer (no dependency, verified against `unzip`). - **Focus timer** — start 25 minutes from the Schedule card; the countdown lives in the top bar with pause and stop. - **Subtasks** — one level of steps under any task, with a done count and an inline add box. - **CSV import** — `date,text,done,tags` pasted or chosen as a file; duplicates are skipped. - **Data health** — a check for missing ids, duplicates, dangling repeats and trash; repair fixes what can be fixed and never deletes a day or a note. - **Panic blur** — blur the planner when the window loses focus. - **In-place updates** — ticking a task patches the row and the counters instead of re-rendering the view: 1.7 ms instead of 66 ms on a 50-task day. - **Month view** — the whole month as a 7-column grid: tasks per day, done ones struck through, block dots, the month's focus above. - **Attachments** — drop a PDF or a photo on a day. Files are blobs in IndexedDB (8 MB cap), listed with name and size, opened or removed individually. Kept out of the JSON backup on purpose. - **IndexedDB storage** — the document lives in IndexedDB, gzip-compressed where `CompressionStream` exists, with localStorage as the fallback for `file://` and private windows. Existing localStorage documents migrate on first load. - **Month at a glance** — a mini calendar in the rail (and at the bottom of Today on phones) with a dot for every planned day. - **Share into the planner** — Chrome on Android can share text straight in; it opens quick add, prefilled. - **Swipe between days** — horizontal swipe on the day view on touch screens. - **Reviews** — a weekly review with an auto-generated summary (what got done, what didn't, what changes, next week's focus) and an end-of-day review that can seed tomorrow's first task. - **Tag filtering** — click a `#tag` anywhere, or type `#health` in search. - **Undo and a 30-day trash** — every delete is reversible, twice over. - **Drag to reorder** — order is meaning in a plan; move a task or block by its handle. **Craft** - Multi-profile with a 4-digit PIN, stored as a PBKDF2-SHA256 hash (120k iterations, per-profile salt) — never as the profile key. PIN asked on launch (configurable); profiles never see each other's data. - Command palette (`Ctrl/⌘ K`) that searches every task, note, block and goal, runs commands, and understands dates (`tomorrow`, `next friday`, `25 dec`). - Keyboard shortcuts for everything (`N`, `T`, `D`, `W`, `Y`, `A`, `/`, `1–5`). - Four themes — Midnight, Ocean, Light and System — with correct contrast in each. - Layout that actually fits: 3-column desktop, icon rail on tablets, bottom tab bar + FAB on phones, no horizontal scroll at 320 px. - 44 px touch targets, visible focus rings, `aria-current` navigation, reduced-motion support. - Print stylesheet — printing a day or a week gives you clean paper output. - Markdown export for a single day or the whole planner; **ICS export** for a day or a week, so the plan lands in your calendar. - Inline editing — click a task, fix it, press Enter. No dialog. - **Keyboard-first list** — `j`/`k` to move, `x` to tick, `e` to edit, `Alt+↑/↓` to reorder. - **Quick add reads English** — "call the clinic tomorrow 4pm #health" fills the date, time and tag, with a live preview of what will be saved. - **Copy a day** — pull yesterday's blocks and tasks into today (or any date) in one dialog. - A backup nudge if you have not exported in 14 days, and a prompt when a new version is cached. **Data** - One JSON document, versioned, with automatic migration from the v13 layout. - Debounced saves, a "Saved" indicator, corrupt-document quarantine, quota-failure warnings. - Import/export the whole database; export any archive separately. ## Quick start **Use it online** — [drsamonline.github.io/planner-pro](https://drsamonline.github.io/planner-pro/app/) **Install as an app** | Platform | How | |---|---| | Android / ChromeOS | Open the site → menu → **Install app** (or **Add to Home screen**) | | iPhone / iPad | Open in Safari → Share → **Add to Home Screen** | | Windows / macOS / Linux | Open the site → install icon in the address bar | | No browser install | Download `planner-pro.html` — one file, double-click it | ### Release downloads Built by CI from the tagged commit (Windows and macOS binaries are unsigned, so SmartScreen/Gatekeeper will ask you to confirm the first launch): | File | Platform | What it is | |---|---|---| | [`planner-pro.html`](https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro/releases/latest/download/planner-pro.html) | any | The entire app in one file — no server, no internet | | [`planner-pro-web.zip`](https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro/releases/latest/download/planner-pro-web.zip) | any | Offline web build: unzip, open `index.html` | | [`planner-pro-14.1.0-windows-setup.exe`](https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro/releases/latest/download/planner-pro-14.1.0-windows-setup.exe) | Windows | Installer (Electron) | | [`planner-pro-14.1.0-windows-portable.exe`](https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro/releases/latest/download/planner-pro-14.1.0-windows-portable.exe) | Windows | Portable, no install | | [`planner-pro-14.1.0-macos-arm64.dmg`](https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro/releases/latest/download/planner-pro-14.1.0-macos-arm64.dmg) | macOS (Apple silicon) | Disk image | | [`planner-pro_14.1.0_amd64.deb`](https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro/releases/latest/download/planner-pro_14.1.0_amd64.deb) | Debian / Ubuntu | Package | | [`planner-pro-14.1.0-android.apk`](https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro/releases/latest/download/planner-pro-14.1.0-android.apk) | Android | Debug APK — sideload it, or `adb install planner-pro-14.1.0-android.apk` | **Run from source** ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/planner-pro.git cd planner-pro python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory app # open http://localhost:8080 ``` > Opening `app/index.html` directly from disk works too — the app is written as > classic scripts, not ES modules, exactly so `file://` keeps working. The service > worker only registers over http(s), so "offline" is automatic either way. ## Keyboard shortcuts | Keys | Action | |---|---| | `Ctrl / ⌘ + K` | Command palette — search everything, run any command | | `J` / `K` | Move down / up the task list | | `X` / `E` | Tick / edit the focused task | | `Alt + ↑ / ↓` | Move the focused task up or down | | `N` | Quick add a task to any day | | `T` / `D` / `W` / `Y` / `A` / `I` | Today · Day · Week · Year · Archive · Insights | | `1` – `5` | Switch the main views | | `/` | Search | | `Esc` | Close palette, dialog or search | ## Data model ```js { v: 14, activeUser: "1234", users: { "1234": { name: "Sohil Momin", theme: "midnight", weekStart: 1, quickNotes: "", days: { "2026-11-10": { intention, notes, todos: [...], blocks: [...] } }, weeks: { "2026-11-09": { focus, todos: [...] } }, // keyed by the week's first day months: { "2026-11": { focus, goals: [...] } }, years: { "2026": { theme, goals: [...] } }, archives: { "2025": { days, weeks, months, years } } } } } ``` Days are keyed by the full date, so moving across a year boundary no longer writes to the wrong year (that was the v13 bug). Weeks are keyed by their start date, so a plan belongs to *one* week instead of repeating every week. ## Building ```bash npm install # dev tooling only: puppeteer-core + electron-builder npm test # 122 end-to-end checks in headless Chromium npm run build:single # one portable planner-pro.html npm run build:web # zip of the offline web build in dist/ ``` | Target | Command / workflow | Output | |---|---|---| | Web (offline, minified) | `npm run build:web` | `dist/planner-pro-web.zip` (−27 % assets) | | Single HTML file | `npm run build:single` | `dist/planner-pro.html` | | Android APK | [`.github/workflows/android.yml`](.github/workflows/android.yml) | `app-debug.apk` via Capacitor (JDK 21) | | Windows / macOS / Linux | [`.github/workflows/desktop.yml`](.github/workflows/desktop.yml) | `.exe`, `.dmg`, `.AppImage`, `.deb` via Electron | Desktop and Android binaries are built by CI, not on a developer machine: they need an Android SDK and per-OS toolchains. Push a `v*` tag (or run the workflow from the **Actions** tab) and the artifacts attach to the release. To sign them for distribution you will additionally need a keystore for Android and code-signing certificates for Windows/macOS — see [`build/android/README.md`](build/android/README.md). ## Roadmap The full, prioritised list of what could be added next — and what is deliberately left out to keep the app small — is in [ENHANCEMENTS.md](ENHANCEMENTS.md). Highlights: recurring tasks, ICS/calendar import-export, encrypted backups, optional cloud sync via a file the user owns, per-day attachments, a focus timer, and a "review" mode for weekly/monthly reflection. ## Privacy No analytics, no telemetry, and **no networking code at all** — grep the source for `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest` or `WebSocket`: there is none. The only way data leaves the device is a file you export. Nothing is sent after the shell is cached. The only outbound links are the ones in this README and the About screen. If you clear site data, the planner starts empty — export a backup first. ## Author **Dr. Sohil Momin** — built this to run his own days. [GitHub](https://github.com/drsamonline) · [Sponsor this work](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) ## Sponsor Planner Pro is free for personal use and developed on unpaid time. If it earns a place in your day, you can [sponsor the work](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) — sponsorship pays for the release builds and keeps the licence non-commercial. ## License [PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](LICENSE) — free for personal, academic, hobby, charitable and government use. **Commercial use requires a written licence** from the author. See [ATTRIBUTION.md](ATTRIBUTION.md) for the ideas and books this planner draws on.

profile-kit: # profile-kit ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **A small, reusable kit for a theme-aware, self-updating GitHub profile.** [![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/landing%20page-open-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/profile-kit/) [![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/) [![Offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/offline--first-yes-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/profile-kit) [![Built with Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Python-3572A5?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/profile-kit) [![Type: reusable kit](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-reusable%20kit-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/profile-kit/) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **Landing page:**  ·  **All projects:** Lift it into your own `username/username` profile repo — by hand, or by handing this repository to an AI agent — and you get a profile page that: - renders the right artwork and stats card for **light and dark** GitHub themes, - keeps its **badge counts and project list current** from the GitHub API, on a daily schedule, without you editing the README, - stays **self-contained and offline-first**: inline SVG, no external JS, no build step, no service to sign up for. Built and maintained by [Dr. Sohil Momin](https://github.com/drsamonline) — see **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)**. --- ## The three ideas it combines 1. **A theme-aware hero.** A hand-drawn SVG banner served through `` with `media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"`, so GitHub shows the light artwork on a light theme and the dark artwork on a dark one — no JavaScript, just two committed files and the right markup. 2. **A metrics card, rendered twice.** [`lowlighter/metrics`](https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics) with the `classic` template, rendered once per theme into `assets/metrics-light.svg` and `assets/metrics-dark.svg`. Each render pins its own palette through the action's `extras_css` option, because metrics has no real light/dark switch (see the known limitation below). 3. **A self-updating README.** A small Python script regenerates the regions of the README that sit between HTML comment markers — a row of badge counts and a categorised project list — straight from the GitHub API, and a workflow commits the result daily. Everything outside the markers is left alone. Each idea stands on its own; you can take one, two, or all three. --- ## What's in the kit ``` README.md this file assets/hero-light.svg hero banner template (light) — edit the placeholders assets/hero-dark.svg hero banner template (dark) — edit the placeholders metrics.yml the metrics workflow — copy to .github/workflows/ profile-generator/ update_profile.py regenerates the marked README regions profile-data.json owner + markers + categories + curated repos update-profile.yml the workflow that runs it daily README.md how the generator works and how to configure it docs/ the kit's own landing page (GitHub Pages, served from /docs) ``` --- ## How to use it ### 1. Create your profile repo Create a public repo named exactly `username/username` (GitHub treats it as your profile README) and give it a `README.md`. ### 2. Add the hero Copy `assets/hero-light.svg` and `assets/hero-dark.svg` into your repo's `assets/` folder, then embed them in the README with a ``: ```html ``` **Editing the hero.** Both SVGs ship with three visible placeholders — `YOUR KICKER`, `YOUR NAME` and `YOUR TAGLINE` — plus the two-letter monogram `YN` in the corner circle. Open **both** files and replace those four strings in each, and update the `aria-label` / `` at the top of each file (they repeat the name and tagline for screen readers). Keep the two files byte-for-byte identical apart from their palette so the light and dark banners line up. ### 3. Add the metrics card Copy `metrics.yml` to `.github/workflows/metrics.yml`, replace `YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME` with your login, and run it once (Actions → *Metrics* → *Run workflow*). It commits the two SVGs to `assets/`. Embed them the same way as the hero: ```html <picture> <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/metrics-dark.svg"> <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/metrics-light.svg"> <img src="assets/metrics-light.svg" alt="GitHub metrics" width="480"> </picture> ``` Read the **Known limitation** below before you expect the languages panel to show anything. ### 4. Add the self-updating README regions - Copy `profile-generator/update_profile.py` to `.github/scripts/update_profile.py`. - Copy `profile-generator/profile-data.json` to `profile-data.json` at the repo root. - Copy `profile-generator/update-profile.yml` to `.github/workflows/update-profile.yml`. - Put the four markers in your README: ```markdown <!-- BADGES:START --> <!-- BADGES:END --> ... <!-- PROJECTS:START --> <!-- PROJECTS:END --> ``` - Edit `profile-data.json` — set `owner`, keep or change the `markers`, set your `categories`, and curate your repos. Run the workflow once to fill the regions. See [`profile-generator/README.md`](profile-generator/README.md) for the full configuration reference. ### 5. Turn on GitHub Pages (optional) The kit's own landing page lives in `docs/`. To publish something similar: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch → `main` / `/docs`**. The `docs/.nojekyll` file tells Pages to serve the files as-is. --- ## Known limitation: the languages panel is empty under `GITHUB_TOKEN` `lowlighter/metrics` works with the default `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`, but its **languages plugin renders empty** because the token is forbidden from reading a field the base query asks for: - metrics' base repositories query requests `stargazers { totalCount }`; - the repository-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` is **not permitted** to read that field, and the GraphQL call comes back `FORBIDDEN: Resource not accessible by integration`; - that leaves the repositories data unusable, so `plugin_languages` renders "0 Languages" with a bare, unstyled "Most used languages" link and no chart; - **the action still reports success.** There is no failing step and no red X, so the card simply looks broken with no error to explain why. **The fix:** a **classic personal access token with no scopes**, saved as the secret `METRICS_TOKEN`, is allowed to read `stargazers`. Create one (GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic) → Generate new token (classic); no scopes required for public data), save it as `METRICS_TOKEN`, switch the `token:` input in both render steps to `${{ secrets.METRICS_TOKEN }}`, and re-enable the `plugin_languages*` lines. The steps are spelled out at the foot of `metrics.yml`. **Also worth knowing:** `config_theme` is **not a real metrics option**. It is copied around the web often, but it silently does nothing. There is no built-in light/dark switch — light and dark have to be done with `extras_css` and **two renders**, which is exactly what `metrics.yml` does. --- ## Built with This profile is assembled from other people's work, and it deserves the credit. - **[lowlighter/metrics](https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics)** — the rendering engine behind the stats card. It uses the `classic` template with the `base` (header, activity) and `calendar` plugins, and its `extras_css` option to produce a matched light and dark pair from one configuration. Worth knowing: `config_theme` is not a real option and silently does nothing, despite how often it is copied around — light/dark has to be done with `extras_css` and two renders. - **[avgupta456/github-trends](https://github.com/avgupta456/github-trends)** — the idea of tracking lines of code by language over time, and the pattern of embedding a hosted SVG instead of generating one in the repo. Its embed is parked here until an account is created on their service. - **[rzashakeri/beautify-github-profile](https://github.com/rzashakeri/beautify-github-profile)** — the catalogue this was worked from. The badge vocabulary comes from its Badges section (the shields.io family), and metrics was chosen from its Widgets list; the busier widgets it also lists (typing SVG, profile trophy, contribution snake) were deliberately left out to keep this page quiet. --- <sub>Part of **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** · built and maintained by [Dr. Sohil Momin](https://github.com/drsamonline)</sub> ## Support <img src="docs/assets/support-portrait.jpg" width="72" height="72" alt="Dr. Sohil Momin" align="left" style="border-radius:50%;margin-right:1rem"> Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.
