# Weft-8 on hardware ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **The Loom's 8-bit machine, in C — and a bench that proves it is the same machine.** [![Live bench](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-the%20parity%20bench-6ee7a0?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-c98b4b?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b1f14)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-c98b4b?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [**Open the parity bench →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/)
![The parity bench](docs/shot.png) A machine described in one language can hide a mistake inside that language's habits. So the Weft-8 — the 8-bit computer from [Jacquard, the Loom](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — is written here a second time, in about 180 lines of C, and the two implementations are held against an answer neither of them produced: **eleven programs whose results were worked out by hand from the instruction set**. | | | |---|---| | `c/weft8.c`, `c/weft8.h` | the machine: 16 registers, Z/C/N/V, 256 bytes, 27 two-byte opcodes | | `c/main.c` | runs the corpus, prints one JSON object per program | | `corpus.json` | eleven programs and the results they must produce — **hand-computed** | | `tools/gen-corpus.mjs` | assembles the corpus with the Loom's own assembler into `c/corpus.h` | | `tools/sync-demo.mjs` | writes `docs/play/corpus.js` for the page, from the same `corpus.json` | | `tools/parity.mjs` | three-way comparison: hand-computed vs C vs JavaScript | | `docs/play/` | the bench: the same corpus, run live in your browser | ## The three that must agree 1. **the hand-computed expectation** — worked out from the ISA, not recorded from either machine 2. **the C machine** — `gcc -O2`, run over the corpus in CI on every push 3. **the Loom's JavaScript machine** — `docs/play/weft8.js`, byte for byte the engine every Weft app runs If any of the three drifts, the build goes red. That is the whole design. ## What the corpus proves | program | claim | |---|---| | `add` | 5 + 7 lands in a register with no flags raised | | `borrow` | 2 − 5 wraps to `0xFD` and sets carry and negative | | `overflow` | 127 + 1 sets overflow — what makes signed branches correct | | `countdown` | a counted loop runs exactly five times | | `signed` | −1 is less than 1, though 255 is greater | | `stack` | PUSH/POP return values in reverse order | | `callret` | CALL and RET come back to the right place | | `ram` | STORE then LOAD round-trips through scratch RAM | | `shift` | SHL moves the top bit into carry | | `ports` | two bytes written to a port arrive in order | | `signed-cmp` | −2 is less than −1, so a signed branch works on negatives | ## Run it ``` node tools/gen-corpus.mjs # assemble corpus.json -> c/corpus.h gcc -O2 -o weft8-corpus c/weft8.c c/main.c ./weft8-corpus # eleven JSON lines node tools/parity.mjs ./weft8-corpus # the three-way check node test-node.js # 96 assertions about the corpus, the C and the page ``` On a microcontroller the same `weft8.c` is the machine, and the peripherals become real pins: a port write can drive an LED or read a button. That step is not shipped here yet — an ESP32 sketch that has never been compiled would be a claim, not a proof, and this repository is about proofs. **Honest note.** This repository's own sandbox had no C compiler, so the C is compiled and checked by CI on every push, not locally. `test-node.js` covers everything that can be checked without a compiler: that the corpus is well-formed and unique, that the JavaScript machine reproduces every hand-computed result, that the C source implements all 27 opcodes and carries the same guards, and that `c/corpus.h` carries the exact bytes of every program. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | **Weft-8 on hardware** (you are here) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. ![The rule bench](docs/shot.png) A rule is a **Weft-8 program with a contract**: the caller puts inputs in the ports, the rule writes one byte to the verdict port, and everything else is the machine's business. ``` IN0 0xD0 IN1 0xD1 IN2 0xD2 IN3 0xD3 the inputs, 0-255 VERDICT 0xD7 0 pass · 1 flag · 2 stop ``` That is the whole interface. The same in the browser, in a test, and in any app that adopts the kit. ## Why a rule engine at all Three properties a rules engine in a general-purpose language struggles to promise: - **Readable** — a rule is twenty lines you can read aloud. No callbacks, no hidden state, no library deciding what "and" means. - **Bounded** — 27 opcodes, none of which touch a file, a network or a page, and a step limit. A runaway rule stops and says so. - **Provable** — every rule ships its cases and the test suite runs them on the real machine, including a case where the comparison is deliberately flipped to prove the test bites. ## The five example rules | Rule | Question | What it shows | |---|---|---| | `record-complete` | are both fields filled in? | two inputs, one comparison each — the smallest possible rule | | `follow-up-due` | has it been longer than the agreed interval? | a threshold that is an **input**, not a number baked into code | | `two-red-flags` | two or more flags, and severity ≥ 7? | what an "and" costs when the machine has no `and` branch | | `ceiling` | is the value above the ceiling you set? | the pattern a dose or budget check uses | | `two-of-three` | are two of the three fields present? | counting is not an instruction — you add one per input and compare | > These are **examples of the pattern, not clinical guidance.** The numbers in them are illustrations. ## Built on the Loom `docs/play/weft8.js` is the **Weft-8** from [Jacquard (the Loom)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — byte for byte the same engine, the same one its 102 assertions cover. This kit adds one file on top: `rules.js`, the port contract and the rule set. ## Adopt it Copy two files into your app: ```html ``` `Rules.evaluate(rule, values)` returns `{ verdict, word, steps, halted, error, bytes }` and never throws on a bad rule — a rule that does not assemble comes back with `errors`. ## Test it ``` npm install node test-node.js # 99 assertions — the machine, every rule case, and the guarantees node tests/page-smoke.js # 9 assertions — the bench, driven in jsdom ``` The suite asserts every rule's own cases, that a runaway rule writes **no** verdict and stops at the step limit, that **no opcode reaches the network, the filesystem or the DOM** (the opcode list *is* the permission list), and that flipping a comparison or deleting a check makes the matching case fail. ## The limits, stated - The machine compares **signed** bytes, so an input above 127 reads as negative. The `ceiling` rule says so in its own words, and a test pins that behaviour rather than hiding it. - Four rules is a demonstration, not a library of clinical logic. Adopting the kit means writing and checking your own. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | **weft8-kit** (you are here) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. Buttons, tags, avatars, badges, alerts, progress, modals, drawers, toasts, tooltips, popovers, menus, tabs, accordion, pagination, breadcrumbs, steps, skeletons, grids and headers — with the behaviours that matter actually implemented. ## Use it ```js var W = require("./widgets-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.Widgets document.body.appendChild(W.button({ label: "Save", variant: "primary" }).el); var m = W.modal({ title: "Delete?", body: "This cannot be undone." }); m.mount(document.body).open(); // focus is trapped, Escape closes W.toastHost(); W.toast("Saved", { type: "success" }); ``` ## What it does - **Action** — `button` (variants, sizes, icon, block), `actionIcon`, `actionIconGroup`, `copyButton` (confirms what it copied, and says so when it cannot), `segmented` - **Display** — `text`, `tag` (closable), `avatar` (image or initials), `groupAvatar` with a remainder, `icon` from path data, `image`, `list` (**keyed**: the same node is reused, so a re-render keeps focus), `accordion`, `empty`, `skeleton` - **Feedback** — `alert` (four kinds, live-region roles), `badge` (count, max, dot), `progress` (determinate and indeterminate), `spinner`, `result`, `modal`, `drawer`, `toast` with a host - **Overlay** — `tooltip` (hover and focus, with a delay), `popover`, `dropdownMenu` (outside click, Escape, separators, dangerous items) - **Nav** — `tabs` (arrow keys, Home/End, panels wired by `aria-controls`), `pagination` (ellipsis, disabled ends), `breadcrumb`, `steps` - **Layout** — `block`, `grid` (auto-fill or fixed columns), `divider` (labelled or vertical), `scrollArea`, `header` (left, title, right) Behaviours that are usually faked are real here: the modal traps Tab, restores focus to whatever opened it, and closes on Escape or the backdrop; the menu closes on an outside click; tabs move with arrow keys; the accordion keeps `aria-expanded` and the panel's `hidden` in step. ## Styling The kit ships **no CSS**. Every element carries a plain class (`w-button`, `w-modal`, `w-toast`…) and the state classes you would want (`is-on`, `is-open`, `is-current`, `is-danger`). Your `design.css` styles them; nothing here imposes a look, a font or a colour. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 206 passed, 0 failed ``` The tests run against a small DOM written inside `test-node.js`, so the kit takes the same code paths in Node that it takes in a page. # ziptastic

[![Licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Dependencies](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg)](docs/BUILD.md)
[![Build](docs/assets/badge-build.svg)](docs/BUILD.md)
[![Live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg)](https://drsamonline.github.io/ziptastic/)


![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)
**One self-contained binary that compresses a game asset tree 20–36% smaller than `xz -9`, and
tells you when it cannot.** No external processes, no network, no model files.

```bash
ziptastic c assets/          # → assets.dr
ziptastic d assets.dr        # → byte-identical
ziptastic info assets.dr     # → header, block table, offsets
```

`.dr` is the format's extension. Detection is by the `CHCE` magic, not the name: a `.dr` renamed
to `.bin` still decodes, and a file that is not a CHCE stream is refused.

## What it is actually good at

Format-aware transforms under a strong backend. A ZIP of PNGs, a raw CD image, a spreadsheet, a
packed asset tree — the engine recognises the container and the payload, undoes the compression
that is already there, and re-compresses what is underneath.

| case | ziptastic `-9` | `xz -9e` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed game-asset tree, 6.3 MB, as `.tar` | **1,275,048** | 1,983,636 | **−35.7%** |
| The same tree as a `.zip` | **1,284,836** | 1,610,228 | **−20.2%** |
| 6.8 MB spreadsheet sheet XML | **70,090** | 163,656 | −57.2% |
| 4.7 MB raw CD image (Mode 2, with ECC) | **1,417,452** | 2,014,224 | −29.6% |
| 2 MB English prose | **408,421** | 543,572 | −24.9% |
| 4.8 MB cooked ISO | 3,333,904 | 3,339,112 | −0.2% |
| 1.4 MB floppy image | 1,257,830 | 1,257,792 | +0.0% |

Every row round-trips byte-exactly. Full tables, the audit and the rejected ideas:
**[`docs/FINDINGS.md`](docs/FINDINGS.md)**.

## What it is not

- **Fast.** 0.3–0.6 MB/s at `-9` against `xz`'s 1–2 MB/s on the same machine. The ratio is bought
  with time, deliberately. `--parallel` trades ratio for speed.
- **A general-purpose winner.** Where no format transform fires it is level with `xz`, and twice
  marginally behind. The advantage is concentrated in a handful of formats, not spread evenly.
- **Magic on incompressible data.** A cooked ISO gains 0.2%; a file of random bytes gains nothing.

## Build

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build        # 37 suites, ~4 minutes
```

Linux and Windows. macOS is not supported. The long form — vendor-by-vendor builds, the zig
toolchain, and the depfile trap that costs a debugging session if you hit it — is in
**[`docs/BUILD.md`](docs/BUILD.md)**.

## What is inside

Format **v8**. Per block, nine encoders compete and the smallest wins: RAW, rANS (static and
adaptive), range, static Huffman, BWT (libbsc), PPMd, an LZMA2 fallback that guarantees the output
is never much worse than `xz` — it declines the full run only when a sample says it is more than 20%
out of reach (`FINDINGS.md` §3f) — and context mixing under `--max-ratio`. Above them sit eighteen Layer 0
transforms — container inflation (ZIP, gzip, PDF), base64, spreadsheet cells, CSV columns, WAV PCM,
SQLite pages, CD-sector Reed-Solomon parity, PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP one level down inside archives, and an `.xz` stream rebuilt from a recipe read out
of its own block header.

Each block carries its own SHA-256, the stream carries a manifest digest, and a `true_size` field
makes the decoded length an exact check rather than a heuristic. The trailer also carries a
**block offset table**, so a block can be reached without walking the stream: `ziptastic info`
prints it, `ziptastic d --block N` decodes one block on its own, and `--from-block N` resumes a
decode that stopped. Reading the index touches under 1% of an archive.

## Where to read next

| | |
|---|---|
| [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) | what each release changed, and what it cost |
| [`docs/FINDINGS.md`](docs/FINDINGS.md) | every measured number, the audit, what was rejected, what is open |
| [`docs/RELEASE_PLAN.md`](docs/RELEASE_PLAN.md) | 1.0 first, speed after, and why in that order |
| [`docs/BUILD.md`](docs/BUILD.md) | building it, including the traps |
| [`docs/FORMAT.md`](docs/FORMAT.md) | the stream format |
| [`docs/index.html`](docs/index.html) | the landing page |

## Support

| | |
|---|---|
| UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` |
| GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) |

MIT for ziptastic itself. It links vendored compressors — liblzma, brotli, brunsli, libbsc, zpaq,
ppmd, preflate — whose terms are summarised in [`docs/LICENCES.md`](docs/LICENCES.md), with

read the LGPL paragraph there: it is the one that asks something of you.
